title: Iowa Dominates Washington 41-24 Behind Career Night From Kamari Moulton
description: Hawkeyes Deliver Statement Win in Seattle The Iowa Hawkeyes delivered an impressive performance Friday night, defeating Washington 41-24 at Husky Stadium. No. 20 Iowa dominated the first half, built a 24 point halftime lead and held off a second-half push from the Huskies to secure a major road victory. The win improved Iowa to 5-1…
fullText:
The Iowa Hawkeyes delivered an impressive performance Friday night, defeating Washington 41-24 at Husky Stadium. No. 20 Iowa dominated the first half, built a 24 point halftime lead and held off a second-half push from the Huskies to secure a major road victory.

The win improved Iowa to 5-1 overall and 2-1 in Big Ten play, giving the Hawkeyes momentum heading into the second half of their season. Washington fell to 3-3 after struggling to contain Iowa's balanced offense and powerful rushing attack.

Running back Kamari Moulton was the star of the night, rushing for a career-high 208 yards and two touchdowns on 26 carries. His biggest play came late in the first quarter, when he broke free for a 56-yard touchdown run to extend Iowa's lead to 13-0.

Quarterback Jeremy Hecklinski also delivered a standout performance in his first career start. Filling in for the injured Hank Brown, Hecklinski completed 14 of 19 passes for 202 yards and three touchdowns.

He connected with tight end DJ Vonnahme twice in the second quarter, finding him for touchdown passes of 20 and 24 yards. Those scores helped Iowa build a commanding 27-3 halftime advantage.

Kicker Caden Buhr also contributed with field goals from 51 and 27 yards as the Hawkeyes controlled the opening half.

The Huskies showed signs of life after halftime, scoring on their opening possession of the third quarter. Backup quarterback Elijah Brown connected with Chris Lawson for a 10-yard touchdown, cutting Iowa's lead to 27-10.

Brown entered the game after starting quarterback Demond Williams Jr. suffered a left shoulder injury late in the first half. Williams did not return.

Washington continued fighting, with Brown throwing three touchdown passes and finishing with 251 passing yards. However, Iowa answered with another touchdown pass from Hecklinski to Reece Vander Zee before Moulton added a three-yard rushing score in the fourth quarter.

The Hawkeyes' defense also played a major role, recording six sacks and limiting Washington to minus-three rushing yards.

Iowa finished with 465 total yards and 263 rushing yards, showcasing the offensive balance that helped secure the victory.

The Hawkeyes will now look ahead to their October 24 matchup against Minnesota after a bye week. With Hecklinski stepping up and Moulton delivering a career performance, Iowa has plenty of positives to build on.

Friday night's victory was an important statement for the Hawkeyes as they continue their push through the Big Ten schedule.

title: NFL Trade Proposal Sees Lions Land 22.5-Sack Edge Rusher
description: The Detroit Lions could help their defense by acquiring New York Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV. The post NFL Trade Proposal Sees Lions Land 22.5-Sack Edge Rusher appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Pundits have continuously linked the Detroit Lions to potential cornerbacks set to be available in the trade market before the NFL trade deadline. It's not hard to understand why. The Lions entered Week 5 ranked last in yards allowed, passing yards yielded and third-down defense.

But adding a cornerback isn't the only way for Detroit to improve its defense. The Lions could also aim to acquire an edge rusher.

If the Lions go that route, one potential target they could pursue currently plays for their former defensive coordinator with the New York Jets — Will McDonald IV.

Heavy Sports proposes the Lions offer a third-round pick to the Jets for McDonald.

"Will McDonald may actually be the best trade Detroit can make to improve its defense given the circumstances, even despite the fact that he could cost a late Day 2 pick," wrote Heavy Sports's Max Dible. "That is because he is young, in his fourth year, and has juice as a former first-round pick who tallied 18.5 sacks in 2024-25 combined."

Over 51 career games, McDonald has posted 22.5 sacks for the Jets. New York selected him at No. 15 overall in the 2023 NFL Draft.

The 2024 campaign remains McDonald's best season from a statistical standpoint. He registered 10.5 sacks with 11 tackles for loss and 24 quarterback hits that year. This season, he has one sack with one tackle for loss and one quarterback hit in four games.

In a perfect world, the Lions will acquire a cornerback at the trade deadline. They arguably could use multiple defensive backs to solidify their struggling secondary.

But adding a defender who could create additional pressure would help too.

"McDonald is a pass-rush specialist and isn't necessarily an every-down player," Dible wrote. But he can create quick pressures and make splash plays, which is the quickest fix for a Lions' defense that has no secondary to speak of but could line McDonald up across from Aidan Hutchinson on pass downs, thereby creating havoc and speeding up the QB clock significantly, which would help the secondary in turn.

McDonald also wouldn't be a rental player, which would help justify the team giving up a third-rounder pick for him. The edge rusher is on the fourth year of his rookie contract. The 2027 campaign will be the fifth-year option of his first NFL contract.

title: Nick Saban calls ESPN show he co-hosts ‘rat poison’
description: Nick Saban used to hate when Alabama was picked to win on "College GameDay."
fullText:
Nick Saban is one of ESPN's premiere college football personalities. He has been featured prominently on College GameDay since 2024, following his retirement from coaching. The network also just released a six-part documentary series about him. Despite their cozy relationship, it wasn't long ago that he did not seem to like the network at all.

With the show traveling to Tuscaloosa in Week 6 they took a look back at something Saban said about ESPN when he was still coaching the Alabama Crimson Tide. Saban still seemed to agree with himself, simply calling it, "rat poison."

MORE: Pat McAfee trolls Alabama football fans with 'College GameDay' kick twist

Nick Saban: "It's rat poison… I used to hate it on Saturday morning… Everybody [on College GameDay] picks us to win. And I know the players are watching that…" Pat McAfee: "Should they listen to people on ESPN now, or no?" Nick Saban: "Hell no." https://t.co/e1fV8Peciw

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 10, 2026

"When I say lock on and lock out I want players to lock out what other people think," Saban explained. "What other people say. I used to hate it. On Saturday morning and I'm sitting there and we're playing the game later in the day and everybody here picks us to win and I know the players are watching that. And I'm wondering is that going to affect their psychological disposition toward competing. The intensity they have. How they're going to play in the game because you think they're gonna win instead of us having to go out and prove it."

Asked by McAfee if he still thought anyone should listen to the people on ESPN, Saban said, "Hell no." McAfee then told him how much he enjoyed the documentary.

MORE: Nick Saban praises Jalen Hurts while explaining 2018 CFP championship QB controversy

It would have been interesting for Saban to talk about what entertainment value the show has for the general public since he doesn't think football players should be watching. More importantly, his record as a head coach seems to prove that it doesn't matter who they're picking to win games on ESPN.

He coached 17 seasons at Alabama and went 206-17 over that period. Either his players weren't watching everyone at ESPN pick them or it actually didn't have any affect on them at all.

For what it's worth, Saban picked Alabama to beat Georgia, as did Desmond Howard and Bryce Young. With McAfee taking George its unclear how this will affect either team.

title: Chiefs Rookie Kahlil Benson Shares Life-Changing News After Impressive NFL Start
description: Chiefs offensive lineman Kahlil Benson has another reason to celebrate after sharing a special announcement during Kansas City's bye week. The post Chiefs Rookie Kahlil Benson Shares Life-Changing News After Impressive NFL Start appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs rookie offensive lineman Kahlil Benson announced that he and his girlfriend, Jayda, are expecting their first child.

Benson shared the news early Saturday morning, October 10, during the Chiefs' bye week, posting a carousel of photographs on Instagram.

The announcement featured Polaroid-style pictures of the couple celebrating the pregnancy. In one photograph, a shirtless Benson held a positive pregnancy test while Jayda showed off her growing baby bump and held a sonogram.

The couple kept their announcement simple, captioning the post, "Love yours. 2027."

The caption indicates they are expecting their baby in 2027.

Benson's announcement comes during an eventful first NFL season for the former Indiana offensive lineman, who went from an undrafted rookie trying to earn a roster spot to becoming Kansas City's starting left tackle.

Benson's post drew congratulatory messages from his Kansas City teammates, including quarterback Patrick Mahomes.

"Congrats 🙏," Mahomes wrote in the comments.

Fellow rookie running back Emmett Johnson also responded to the news.

"Congrats fam 🙏," Johnson wrote.

Jayda, who uses the Instagram handle @thejaydag, identifies herself as an artist and Indiana University alumna. She also maintains a separate Instagram account dedicated to her tattoos and artwork.

The couple did not reveal their baby's sex or an exact due date in the announcement.

The personal milestone arrives shortly after Benson received one of the NFL's top monthly honors for his performance during the opening weeks of the 2026 season.

On October 1, the NFL named Benson its Offensive Rookie of the Month for September after he started Kansas City's first three games at left tackle.

Benson arrived in Kansas City in the spring as a rookie minicamp tryout player without a guaranteed contract.

The former Indiana standout impressed the coaching staff enough to earn more opportunities throughout the offseason and eventually made the Chiefs' 53-man roster.

His path to the starting lineup changed when Josh Simmons suffered a back injury that sidelined him ahead of the regular season.

Kansas City moved Benson to left tackle, a position he hadn't played in college.

The rookie made his first NFL start against the Denver Broncos on September 14, helping Kansas City secure a 31-10 victory.

Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy discussed the challenge facing Benson before his debut.

"Go play and have fun. That's all you can say," Bieniemy told reporters. "Yes, he is a young player. He's going to have some good plays, he's going to have some bad plays. But when it's all said and done with, he just needs to go out there and play and have fun."

Benson responded with a strong September performance.

According to NFL Next Gen Stats, he allowed seven quarterback pressures across 106 pass-blocking snaps during the first three games. That ranked third-fewest among NFL left tackles through the opening three weeks.

He became the first Chiefs player to win a Rookie of the Month award since linebacker Nick Bolton in October 2021.

Benson also became the first offensive lineman in the NFL to receive the monthly honor since Quenton Nelson in October 2018.

He continued starting in Kansas City's October 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, helping the Chiefs reach 4-0 entering their bye week.

Kansas City returns to action against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, October 18, at Arrowhead Stadium.

title: Why Lane Johnson's retirement is not yet official for Eagles
description: This Lane Johnson retirement situation is a bit complicated.
fullText:
Why Lane Johnson's retirement is not yet official for Eagles originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The 2026 season for the Philadelphia Eagles is beginning to collapse in Week 5. Cam Jurgens was traded; there are plenty of key players dealing with injuries, and Lane Johnson has retired from the NFL.

Unfortunately, that's only scratching the surface of the issues with this team. The offense looks stagnant, the defense isn't as dominant as it looked last season, and there's even more to the Johnson retirement story than it initially appeared.

As The Athletic's Jonathan Jones shared, the retirement of Johnson isn't actually official just yet. The Eagles have not filed his retirement paperwork. Why? Well, this is a very complicated situation for the Eagles thanks to the cap implications of this move.

"Philadelphia, meanwhile, still has not processed the paperwork on Lane Johnson's retirement -- that's due to cap considerations, I'm told," Jones reports.

While Johnson's NFL career is over, his status on the Eagles roster is murky. If the Eagles were to file the paperwork for his retirement, they would have some cap problems.

As Jones notes, Johnson has a $21.7 million option bonus this season, with half already paid, and the other half due to be paid in December.

How that option bonus and the rest of Johnson's deal affect the Eagles' books will be determined based on how they file his retirement paperwork. If they do it normally, the Eagles' cap would become a bit of a problem.

But there are ways to manage this situation, one of which is by placing Johnson on the "left-squad list" that would "allow the team to clear the roster spot and preserve the cap hits in 2027 and 2028 as a June 2 cut," according to Jones.

MORE: Chiefs reportedly could bring back Tyreek Hill after Rashee Rice, Tyquan Thornton injuries

Philadelphia's front office also needs to be careful about how they manage this situation with its franchise legend. The Detroit Lions demanded some of the money back from Calvin Johnson when he retired. That relationship soured afterwards.

The Eagles should avoid that situation unfolding with Johnson, even if it means this decision becomes a lot more complicated.

There are a lot of moving parts with this Johnson retirement for the Eagles, and the cap situation is the one thing looming over Johnson officially saying goodbye to the Eagles and the NFL.

How Howie Roseman and the Eagles handle this will be noteworthy. Things could be resolved quickly, or there could be a delay as the Eagles' front office tries to figure out how best to manage the cap hits from Johnson's retirement over the next few years.

title: How Hamilton "tipped it over the edge" with a setup change too far in Singapore GP qualifying
description: After showing an impressive turn of speed in the first knock-out phases, Lewis Hamilton pushed too far to unlock more pace
fullText:
Ferrari will be pondering whether both its cars should have been on the front row for the Singapore Grand Prix. Lewis Hamilton set an impressive pace through the opening segments of qualifying and team-mate Charles Leclerc said "I think the car had potential for pole".

But ultimately Leclerc came up 0.054s short of beating Max Verstappen's Red Bull to pole, with Hamilton a further 0.069s off. Small margins, but both drivers felt they could have done better.

F1 Singapore GP: Max Verstappen overcomes Ferrari challenge for pole

Hamilton set the pace in Q1, where he finished 0.345s up on Leclerc, and in Q2, where he became the first driver to set a lap below the 1m32s mark in Singapore this year. In that session he was 0.110s faster than second-placed Verstappen.

But Lewis then made a front-wing change, adding a little more angle on the front-right flap, which fundamentally altered the balance of the car in an unexpected way. Although he then went faster in Q3, it was only a marginal improvement and both Leclerc and Verstappen found more. Some of this can be accounted for through track evolution as the session neared its end.

"I think it's just balance," said Hamilton afterwards.

"The car felt good. My team, the engineers, did a fantastic job as well as the mechanics between the sessions.

"I think the car felt amazing in Q1 and Q2. And when I finished the laps, I was like, 'She's got 

"The only way to try and extract that is to try and add wing. And in doing so, I think it just tipped it over the edge.

"It was only one hole [of adjustment] or something like that. But it's like it was on the knife-edge. And after that, then the car was just snappy and none of the laps in Q3 were any good.

"So I'm grateful to be third, to be honest, given that those laps weren't very good."

The theory that the setup change had made the Ferrari a little too 'on those nose' was bolstered by Hamilton having to correct huge snaps of oversteer at Turn 3 on both his Q3 laps, then having to saw at the steering wheel through the final chicane.

"There's a real fine line with our car where it's over the edge or under the limit and finding that sweet spot is very, very difficult," said Hamilton.

"I probably had it in the first two, but you have to look for the progress of the track, the grip coming up. So you have to kind of react to that in hindsight."

Track evolution is always a factor at street circuits such as Singapore, which aren't used for racing through the rest of the year. The surface offers more grip as more rubber is laid down through each session, which can lead teams and drivers down the wrong setup route since it can be difficult to distinguish how much improvement is coming through setup, and how much is simply the track being more grippy.

Leclerc explained that he simply struggled to put a clean lap together until right at the end.

"I did some mistakes," he said.

"And I think there was a potential to be on pole today, but Max just did a better job."

title: Robin Fellhauer sets new Bundesliga record with fastest goal ever vs. Bayern Munich
description: This was no the kind of record FC Bayern wants to set.
fullText:
It took just eight seconds for Robin Fellhauer to etch his name into Bundesliga history, and Bayern Munich will not want to remember this particular record for very long.

The FC Augsburg midfielder scored the fastest goal in Bundesliga history on Saturday, finding the back of the net just 8.4 seconds into the Bavarian derby against Bayern Munich. The previous record of nine seconds was jointly held by Kevin Volland, who scored for Hoffenheim against Bayern in 2015, and Karim Bellarabi, who scored for Bayer Leverkusen against Borussia Dortmund in 2014.

Robin Fellhauer's goal against Bayern is the fastest goal in Bundesliga history pic.twitter.com/1BahCfPKqC

After Luis Díaz played the ball back to Bayern Munich goalkeeper Manuel Neuer from kickoff, the veteran attempted to chip the onrushing Fellhauer. Instead, Neuer hit the Augsburg player with the ball, allowing Fellhauer to race toward an empty net and calmly finish.

It was a dream start for Augsburg and a nightmare opening for Bayern, with Fellhauer suddenly becoming a piece of Bundesliga history.

Eight seconds. One costly mistake. One unforgettable record.

Fellhauer has officially rewritten the history books, even if Neuer would probably prefer that particular page to be torn out.

title: Jaylen Brown Compares Celtics Matchup To Seeing An Ex
description: Jaylen Brown compares his first game against the Celtics with the 76ers to running into an ex. He shares raw thoughts on the emotional shift.
fullText:
Jaylen Brown does not view his upcoming game against the Boston Celtics as a standard rivalry clash. Instead, the new Philadelphia 76ers star compares the emotional weight of facing his former team to running into an ex-partner in public. This surprising take comes just days before the 76ers hit the court for a preseason tilt against the squad that helped build his career.

The 76ers are set to play the Celtics on Saturday night in Boston, marking the first time Brown will face the franchise that traded him this summer. According to Sportsnaut, Brown broke down this unique dynamic during a recent video on his Twitch channel. He noted that the feeling is less about hatred and more about the awkward reality of life moving forward after a split.

Brown described the situation with a blunt analogy that captures the strangeness of the moment. "We about to preseason play the Celtics tomorrow. Interesting dynamic," Brown began by saying. He then dove into the personal side of the trade, explaining that the matchup feels like a chance encounter with someone from a past life. "And it's just life. It feels like bumping into your ex publicly, thinking, …, we once dated, you get it," noting that both parties just have to keep moving forward with their own business.

This sentiment highlights how quickly the NBA landscape shifts for elite players. Brown was Boston's top player last year while Jayson Tatum recovered from a ruptured Achilles. Yet, the team decided to trade him to Philadelphia, a move that shocked many fans. The regular season game on November 10 drew attention, but this Saturday's preseason contest brings the reality of that split into the spotlight much sooner.

Beyond the emotional weight of facing his old team, Brown is now part of a Philadelphia roster loaded with star power. The 76ers recently saw LeBron James make his debut in a preseason game against the Brooklyn Nets, where he posted 10 points, five assists, and four rebounds in just the first half. Per Associated Press, James made all eight of his free throws and did not even attempt a field goal until late in the first quarter, showing he can facilitate without needing to shoot constantly.

With James, Joel Embiid, and Tyrese Maxey in the lineup, Brown has less pressure to be the sole scoring option. Danny Green, a three-time NBA champion, praised James for adapting his game to the new team rather than forcing others to change. Brown remarked that James looked excellent while adjusting to others instead of forcing them to adapt, adding that the 76ers possess sufficient scorers so James need not carry the previous scoring burden.

With two preseason games left against the Boston Celtics, the 76ers will face their regular season opener in New York on October 20. This Saturday's game serves as a crucial test for chemistry and emotional readiness. Brown admitted he is "super excited" despite the awkward comparison to seeing an ex, signaling he is ready to compete. The team will look to prove they can handle the pressure of a top-four conference spot against the very team that once held his jersey number.

title: Arsenal player picks up injury in post-Leeds warm down
description: Piero Hincapie suffered a knock in the warm down after Arsenal’s win over Leeds United, according to a report.Photo via Arsenal.comFootball insider Hand of Arsenal reports that Piero Hincapie suffer...
fullText:
Football insider Hand of Arsenal reports that Piero Hincapie suffered a knock to his ankle in the post-game warm down, following Arsenal's victory over Leeds United.

The same source adds that Hincapie will now be monitored in the coming days, with the severity of the injury evidently not entirely clear.

The knock will be frustrating for Hincapie, who had only just returned to the pitch after missing the international break with a muscle injury.

The defender was also absent for the League Cup game against Ipswich Town on September 15th due to injury, and though he technically made the squad that weekend against Brighton, he was unused and clearly not fully fit.

The belief was that Hincapie had now overcome his injury issue, and that he was ready to make his comeback. But this new ankle problem may now leave him sidelined once again.

It's positive at least that Hincapie hasn't suffered a muscle setback, as that would have been particularly worrying given he's already been in and out of the squad. Even so, the reliance on Riccardo Calafiori is less than ideal, with the games coming thick and fast over the next few weeks.

That starts with a Champions League match at home to Lille on Tuesday, a game which Calafiori now seems almost certain to start.

title: Allen Vs. ’CLD’ Odds, Full Fight Preview & Prediction
description: Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Middleweight sluggers Brendan Allen vs. Christian Leroy Duncan will clash TONIGHT (Sat., Oct. 10, 2026) inside Meta Apex in Las Vegas, Nevada, for UFC Vegas 122. Allen enters this fight in a rather unusual position.
fullText:
Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) Middleweight sluggers Brendan Allen vs. Christian Leroy Duncan will clash TONIGHT (Sat., Oct. 10, 2026) inside Meta Apex in Las Vegas, Nevada, for UFC Vegas 122.

Allen enters this fight in a rather unusual position. His upset victory over Reinier de Ridder last year should have pushed him back into the title mix; however, high-profile bouts aren't materializing for "All-In." Perhaps as a result of earlier losses to top contenders, Allen is being forced to fight down for a third time in a row.

Perhaps victory here can finally score him that long-awaited grudge match versus Dricus du Plessis? Just no more "finesse."

Duncan is no easy task, however. The English striker is starting to live up to his potential, winning five in a row as well as seven of his last eight. A dynamic kickboxer with knockout power, Duncan could vastly improve his own position in the title picture with a victory in his first-ever main event opportunity.

Let's take a closer look at the betting odds and strategic keys for each athlete:

Brendan Allen via TKO/KO/DQ: +850

Brendan Allen via submission: +300

Brendan Allen via decision: +250

Christian Leroy Duncan victory: +108

Christian Leroy Duncan via TKO/KO/DQ: +240

Christian Leroy Duncan via submission: +2500

Christian Leroy Duncan via decision: +500

Allen is a well-rounded Middleweight, particularly offensively. He's a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt with great back attacks, a very capable wrestler, and has potent combinations of punches, kicks and knees. Historically, he's a little too easy to hit, which has cost him on several different occasions.

Fortunately, Allen's well-roundedness is a great advantage. We have seen Duncan struggle with his output when forced to defend against both threatening combinations and genuine takedowns. By mixing up his attacks, Allen can quite possibly outstrike the "cleaner" kickboxer.

It also helps that Allen is well-equipped to counter a couple key Duncan traits. For one, Duncan often likes to crash into the clinch, a position where Allen is the superior wrestler and in-fighter. If Duncan leaps forward with a right, lands in the clinch, and eats a knee or elbow for his trouble, he's less likely to advance. Similarly, Duncan loves to spin, and Allen is an excellent backtaker.

One well-timed side step could produce a strange for Allen or at least make Duncan think twice before utilizing one of his key weapons.

Duncan is a tall and athletic Middleweight who fights with a traditional martial arts flair. He stands side-on and controls distance well, aided by that formidable 79-inch reach. Unlike most Karate-style kickboxers, he's actually more dangerous while initiating, stepping forward with long, powerful straight punches, explosive kicks, or his favored spinning techniques.

As mentioned above, Duncan will want to be careful with his spinning strikes here. He shouldn't abandon them entirely — they're a core part of his offense — but Duncan has to feint often and only throw them when appropriate. For example, if Allen is along the fence and covering up because of the threat of punches, a spin kick to the gut would be perfectly appropriate.

Though Duncan fights well moving forward, the threat of the reactive takedown while over-extending might actually cause him to shift strategies here. Allen is chronically aggressive and has been walked onto heavy counter punches by men like Sean Strickland and even Chris Curtis. If Duncan chooses to really trust in his jab, he could pop Allen in the face, retreat and then try to time a heavier blow as Allen steps forward.

I have mixed feelings about this matchup, as I don't particularly trust either man. Allen is the more experienced veteran, but he's also somewhat prone to falling apart when he starts to lose the standup. Duncan, meanwhile, is still making mistakes in how he manages distance. If he's not careful, he'll walk right onto a takedown or give up his back spinning, two possible mistakes that could drastically alter the course of the fight.

If Duncan stays composed and feeds Allen one-two combinations, he should win here. If Allen smartly blends his pocket boxing, clinch striking, and offensive wrestling, he should win here.

Who to trust? I'll side with momentum. Duncan is still just in his sixth year as a professional, and things seemed to start clicking in early 2024. Two years later, he should be further on the path towards becoming an elite Middleweight. Conversely, we have likely already seen Allen's best and been left wanting in the past.

A close decision either way wouldn't shock me, nor would an early Allen strangle. However, in a tossup, siding with the more athletic up-and-comer isn't the worst idea.

title: Daylight robbery! Luis Díaz’s disallowed goal should have stood vs. Augsburg
description: That decision may have cost FC Bayern all three points.
fullText:
Bayern Munich was on the backfoot for the most part of the 2-2 draw with Augsburg. Ismael Saibari and Nathaniel Brown rescued a point for the Rekordmeister after Manuel Neuer gifted Augsburg their two goals. Luis Díaz actually opened the scoring, but his goal was ruled out for an offside player in the build-up, a goal that former Bundesliga referee Patrick Ittrich said should have stood.

"[The offside position] was completely irrelevant in this case," Ittrich said on Sky Germany (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia). "There was an offside situation, and then the player essentially cleared the ball completely unchallenged. That means the situation was over, and then there was a new situation. That's a classic next play situation, and therefore the goal should have stood in my opinion. I think it's a very, very controversial decision."

Bayern played far from their best, but did just enough (well, more than enough) to get at least a draw from a seemingly hopeless position. With big Champions League matches on the horizon, Vincent Kompany must make changes.

title: Could the Saints be the mystery team trading for Marvin Harrison Jr.?
description: The Arizona Cardinals are trading wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. but they won't say where. Are the New Orleans Saints the mystery team getting him?
fullText:
Are the New Orleans Saints making a big move at wide receiver? With rookie first-round pick Jordyn Tyson still on injured reserve and little production to show from the receivers behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, it could be worth weighing their options. Maybe the Saints are the mystery team landing Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Arizona Cardinals.

Multiple reports Saturday morning said that Harrison will be inactive for Sunday's game with the Detroit Lions while Arizona finalizes a trade to send him elsewhere. The fourth overall pick in the 2024 draft is on the move, but what no one seems to know is where he's going. Whether the Cardinals have a deal in place or are just trying to bait a better offer from another suitor remains to be seen.

ESPN's Adam Schefter added that the Cardinals front office had told teams "it wanted first-round value in return for Harrison, the former No. 4 overall pick." That lined up with a previous report from Tom Pelissero for The Ringer, who shared that "Other teams that have spoken to the Cardinals say Arizona would want a second-round draft pick and more—perhaps an additional mid-round pick—to consider dealing Harrison."

That would be a lot to pay for a receiver averaging just 21.3 yards per game this season, but Harrison has been dealt a bad hand in Arizona. He's had to navigate a couple of different offenses without a sure thing at quarterback. The hope, for whichever team is acquiring him, is that a stable situation can help him play his best football.

Just don't bet on the Saints being the ones to get him. Even though Harrison has a mentor in place -- he was teammates with Chris Olave on the Ohio State Buckeyes back in 2021 -- New Orleans is just not in a position to go for broke after losing three of their first four games. They should be holding onto their draft picks ahead of the NFL trade deadline in November. If they do feel like they can make a move, it should be to upgrade a defense in need of playmakers at all three levels. Harrison would be a fun pickup, but he isn't one they can afford.

title: Arizona Cardinals Finalizing Deal to Trade Marvin Harrison Jr.
description: The Arizona Cardinals are reportedly finalizing a trade involving Marvin Harrison Jr., who will miss Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions.
fullText:
The Detroit Lions just received a surprising development ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, and it could significantly impact how Detroit prepares defensively. Arizona is reportedly finalizing a trade involving former first-round wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and the talented pass catcher will not play against the Lions.

According to ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Cardinals informed Harrison on Saturday morning that he would be inactive for Sunday's contest as the franchise works through the final details of a trade. NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport also contributed to the breaking report, although Harrison's destination and the compensation Arizona will receive have not been publicly confirmed.

The timing is particularly significant because Detroit enters Sunday's game with one of the NFL's most vulnerable passing defenses. Losing a receiver with Harrison's physical talent and potential could force Arizona to make considerable adjustments to its offensive game plan.

Sep 27, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18) during halftime against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Harrison entered the NFL with enormous expectations after Arizona selected him fourth overall in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Ohio State. The son of Pro Football Hall of Fame receiver Marvin Harrison, he was widely considered one of the most talented receiving prospects in his draft class.

His rookie season offered encouraging signs, as Harrison finished with 62 receptions for 885 yards and eight touchdowns. However, his production declined during the 2025 campaign, when he recorded 41 receptions for 608 yards and four touchdowns in 12 games.

Things have become even more difficult this season under Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur. Through four games, Harrison has managed just five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown, a disappointing start for a player expected to develop into Arizona's featured outside receiver.

According to NBC Sports' reporting on the pending move, Arizona has reportedly been seeking a trade package that includes a second-round draft pick. Houston has also surfaced in league speculation as a possible destination, although no agreement with the Texans has been confirmed.

For Arizona, moving Harrison would represent a significant change in direction only two seasons after using a premium draft selection to acquire him. For Harrison, a fresh start could provide an opportunity to rebuild his career in an offense better suited to his abilities.

The development could provide some relief for a Detroit secondary that has struggled throughout the first month of the season. The Lions have surrendered 127 points in four games, and opposing quarterbacks have repeatedly capitalized on breakdowns in coverage.

As we previously reported following Kelvin Sheppard's criticism of Detroit's back seven, the defensive coordinator believes his defensive front has performed at a high level. However, the linebackers and secondary have failed to consistently support that pressure with dependable coverage.

Harrison's absence removes one potential outside threat, but Arizona still has capable offensive weapons who can challenge Detroit's defense. Tight end Trey McBride remains one of the Cardinals' most dangerous targets, while receivers Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne could see additional opportunities.

That means Sheppard cannot assume Arizona's passing attack will suddenly become ineffective. In fact, the Cardinals could respond by emphasizing McBride even more heavily, creating additional challenges for Detroit's linebackers and defensive backs.

The Lions will also be without defensive backs Brian Branch and Rock Ya-Sin on Sunday. As we previously reported in Detroit's final injury update, both players were officially ruled out, leaving the coaching staff with important decisions about its secondary rotation.

The Lions enter Sunday's matchup with a 2-2 record and a chance to head into their bye week above .500. With difficult divisional games against Green Bay and Minnesota approaching, defeating Arizona has become increasingly important.

Harrison's reported departure is a major development for the Cardinals, but Detroit cannot afford to treat it as a guarantee of defensive success. Arizona still possesses enough talent to challenge a Lions defense that has struggled with communication, missed assignments, and explosive plays.

Still, losing a receiver who entered the league as the No. 4 overall draft pick is hardly the development Arizona envisioned just one day before facing Detroit. The Cardinals are apparently preparing to move on from a player once viewed as a foundational piece of their offense, creating another challenge for a team already sitting at 1-3.

For Campbell and the Lions, the objective remains unchanged: Win Sunday, show meaningful defensive improvement, and enter the bye week with some much-needed momentum. Thanks to Arizona's surprising decision, Detroit will have one fewer talented receiver to worry about.

title: Ten-man Brighton beat Sunderland to continue impressive start
description: Brighton held on for an impressive 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light despite playing the final half-hour with ten men.The visitors had the first big chance when Diego Gómez capitalised ...
fullText:
Brighton held on for an impressive 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light despite playing the final half-hour with ten men.

The visitors had the first big chance when Diego Gómez capitalised on a Kevin Danso mistake, but Robin Roefs saved well.

Sunderland threatened through Thomas Meunier before half-time, only for Ferdi Kadioglu to make an important block.

Brighton took the lead early in the second half when Pascal Groß's cross found Maxim De Cuyper, who beat Roefs at his near post.

The Seagulls were then reduced to ten men after VAR recommended a red card for Pascal Struijk for denying Wilson Isidor a goalscoring opportunity.

Sunderland pushed for an equaliser but struggled to create clear chances, and Brighton sealed the win deep into stoppage time when Georginio Rutter played in Jaouen Hadjam to score on the counter.

title: Swansea lose first game at revamped St Helen's
description: Swansea suffer late loss to Ebbw Vale on their return to St Helen's as unbeaten Cardiff take over from Newport at the top of SRC.
fullText:
Ebbw Vale fly-half Cai Evans spoiled Swansea's St Helen's homecoming with a penalty to seal a 27-26 win in Super Rygbi Cymru (SRC).

The Whites had led 26-10 after home full-back Mat Protheroe became the first player to score a try at the revamped venue and added another in the second half.

Further tries came from scrum-half Matthew Aubrey and fly-half Josh Phillips, who finished with 11 points.

Ebbw Vale responded with two tries from hooker Ieuan Morris and scores from number eight Rhys Jenkins and prop Luke Garrett.

Dragons back Evans added seven points with the boot, including the vital penalty that left Swansea still searching for a first win of the 2026-27 season.

There was a lengthy second-half stoppage following a serious leg injury for Swansea wing Iwan Glynn.

One stand was open for the first game back at St Helen's and a second will be open for the next home game against Cardiff on Thursday, 15 October.

There was a crowd of more than 1,000 present, with close to 3,000 anticipated for the Blue and Blacks fixture.

Ospreys' opening United Rugby Championship (URC) match in Swansea will be staged against Dragons on Saturday, 24 October.

Rygbi Gogledd Cymru (RGC) became the first team to beat Newport this season by easing to a 65-28 win in Colwyn Bay.

RGC, with fly-half Billy McBryde pulling the strings on his 100th appearance for the club, ran in nine tries as they stylishly avenged an opening weekend defeat by the Black and Ambers.

Newport did claim a four-try bonus point from their trip north but lose top spot to Cardiff, who beat Carmarthen Quins 35-12 at the Arms Park.

It was 7-7 at half-time but Dan Fish's side claimed a six-point haul thanks to tries by wings Dewi Cross (2) and Iwan Pyrs-Jones, scrum-half Sion Davies and hooker Tom Howe.

Cardiff are now the only unbeaten side after five rounds of the season.

Champions Llandovery lost at Pontypool on opening weekend but climbed to fourth in the table with a 31-15 victory against Pooler at Church Bank, turning four points into six with a late try.

Bridgend showed their fighting spirit to earn a bonus-point win against Aberavon in tricky conditions at the Brewery Field on Friday.

The Ravens triumphed 24-19 after trailing 19-5 at half-time, with wing Cameron Ellis scoring the winner in the 73rd minute.

title: 5 quick hitters with Gang Green Nation: Geno Smith’s outlook, and how the Browns can attack the Jets
description: A look at how the Browns can attack the Jets’ defense, whether Geno Smith was welcomed back by fans, and more.
fullText:
This Sunday, the Cleveland Browns are on the road as they take on the New York Jets in Week 5. To help preview a few topics from the Jets' perspective, we reached out to MacGregor Wells from Gang Green Nation and exchanged five questions with him.

Chris: "How has Geno Smith looked in his return to the Jets in this offense? Were fans at all excited to have him back?"

MacGregor: "Geno has been a mixed bag. He has played well in a couple of games and poorly in a couple of games. The bottom line with Geno is he has always had a reasonably strong and accurate arm. His issues have always been with processing what's in front of him and making good and timely decisions. Keep him well protected for long enough and he can do well. Pressure him or force him into quick decisions and Geno will struggle.

Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations

Faster commenting and posting experience!

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

Most Jets fans were probably somewhat glad to get Geno back, if only because of the absolute dreck the Jets had at quarterback last year. At least Geno can competently run an NFL offense if he's given time. On the other hand, I don't think Jets fans were under any illusion they were getting a great quarterback. He's a legitimate starter but he's nowhere near an upper tier starter. He is what he is – a decent stopgap until the Jets can draft or trade for a better option."

Chris: "What do you view as the Jets' biggest strength and weakness on defense right now?"

MacGregor: "On defense the Jets' secondary has been surprisingly effective. Going into the season I thought the secondary would be a major liability, but they have held their own fairly well.

The Jets run defense, on the other hand, particularly the defensive line, has not been effective, despite the Jets having spent the offseason accumulating guys whose strength was supposed to be stopping the run. In addition, the defensive line has done a poor job pressuring opposing quarterbacks. It's been a rough start to the season for the Jets defensive line."

Chris: "Which of the Jets' 2026 draft picks has the best chance of making an immediate impact in Week 5?"

MacGregor: "I'll go with rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq was selected #16 overall in the first round of the 2026 NFL draft. He is an insanely athletic dude at tight end, and the Jets have a bunch of receivers currently injured, leaving Sadiq as the second priority target in the Jets passing game behind Garrett Wilson. If the Jets can protect Geno Smith against the Browns pass rush Sadiq has the potential to have a big game."

Chris: "Tell us about one player who Browns fans may not have heard of, but who could have an impact on this Sunday's game."

MacGregor: "Dane Belton might fit the bill. He's a safety the Jets signed away from the New York Giants in free agency this past offseason. Belton spent most of his Giants career primarily as a special teams guy, but he is starting at safety for the Jets, and he has done a nice job. Belton's not a star in pass defense, but he is outstanding in run support. He is a very sound tackler, always wraps up, and always seems to be around the ball. He's no superstar, but he's just fundamentally sound and he hustles like crazy. A fun guy to watch."

Chris: "The Browns are underdogs against the Jets on Sunday (Browns +1.5 as of this question, per FanDuel). Who would you pick to win the game?"

MacGregor: "I am a bit shocked that the Browns are underdogs here. The Browns have won three straight and the Jets have lost three straight. The Jets have looked progressively worse with each game played. The Jets aren't completely devoid of talent like they have been in some recent seasons, but given the trajectory of each team's season, it's difficult to understand why the Jets are favored. I suppose it comes down to home team advantage, but the Jets haven't been particularly good at home in recent years.

I hate to say it, but I'd pick the Browns to win this game."

Thanks again to MacGregor for taking the time to answer my questions.

title: Andy’s Player Ratings: Sunderland 0-2 Brighton – Disappointing Black Cats Struggle Against 10 Men
description: Sunderland couldn’t find a way past 10-men Brighton, as the visitors run out 2-0 winners, here’s how Andy rated the lads
fullText:
Made a really good save early where he was out quickly to block a shot but another game where almost every shot on target went in, even if they were good finishes. Really poor kick out led to the second goal.

Defended OK but sold himself short for the opening goal, stretching for a pass, missed it and left his man open at the back post.

Loads of effort today, tried to spur us on going forward and had a good attempt from range before the break that forced a save but struggled a little with the number of runners around him.

Attempted a couple of sloppy passes that put us under pressure, wasn't bad defensively, but not his best game.

Went off for the more attacking option in Methalie to come on as we chased the game, made plenty of defensive contributions in the first half, with plenty of blocks and tackles down the left.

Got in a really good position for a shot in the first half but didn't consider that as an option and the chance went begging, forced a save from a free kick and then had a couple from range go well over. Was a mixed bag all round this afternoon, made some great passes out wide, with one in the first half to Le Fee out on the left with the outside of his left foot being outstanding but then some sloppy ones that led to counter attacks.

Covered a massive amount of ground as usual, passed the ball fine but without really causing any problems and was often too deep when Brighton went down to 10.

Had started OK and looked a threat down the right but was a bit slow to shoot on a couple of occasions when he was well placed. Went off with what looked an injury to his hamstring.

Tried really hard to make something happen but other than a cross to Isidor in the first half, had little to show for his efforts.

Really struggled to get into the game today and snatched at everything that came his way.

Had a deflected shot clipped onto the post in the first half and would have been in behind but for Struijk to drag him down (not sure why VAR was needed for that one). Very quiet otherwise, picked up a knock early on that was obviously causing him discomfort and had no chance in the air against Brighton's big centre halves.

Cut inside and fired a shot down the goalkeepers throat but wasn't aggressive enough when he was on the ball, too often preferring to lay the ball off for the player behind him.

Replaced Angulo but struggled against the two banks of Brighton defenders, absolutely no room for him to run into.

Gave us a more attacking option down the left but only had one burst to show for that, winning a corner. Got back well to stop a cross late on.

Came on as we switched to 442 but absolutely nothing came his way and all the long balls seemed to be aimed at Isidor.

I don't think there was a stand out player today, with flat performances all round but I'll give my man of the match to Reinildo as he made plenty of blocks and tackles in the first half. Not that he had a good game but there were just no plus points from today.

title: Vincent Kompany backs Manuel Neuer after massive gaffe during 2-2 draw with FC Augsburg
description: The FC Bayern boss was not going to hammer his captain.
fullText:
Vincent Kompany is not about to let one mistake define Manuel Neuer, even after the Bayern Munich captain gifted FC Augsburg an early goal in Saturday's frustrating 2-2 draw.

Neuer's afternoon got off to a disastrous start when his attempted clearance following the kickoff struck Robin Fellhauer, allowing the Augsburg midfielder to race through and score after just 8.4 seconds. The goal set a new Bundesliga record for the fastest strike in league history, giving Bayern an unwanted place in the record books.

However, Kompany was quick to defend his experienced goalkeeper after the match, emphasizing the importance of responding to adversity rather than dwelling on a single costly moment.

"Of course, we had wished for a better start. I played enough football to know that it happens, and you can't change that. The important thing is how you react afterwards. Manu is experienced enough. He just has to carry on and show how good he is. He will do that, but we shouldn't forget that we also missed many chances on the other side," Kompany explained (as captured by @iMiaSanMia).

The Bayern Munich manager has a point. While Neuer's error immediately put his team on the back foot, Bayern had ample opportunities to take control of the match and secure all three points.

For a team with Bayern Munich's ambitions, a draw against FC Augsburg inevitably feels like two points dropped. Neuer's mistake was an obvious talking point, but Kompany is right that the goalkeeper should not shoulder all the blame for a disappointing afternoon.

The response matters now. Neuer has earned enough credit throughout his extraordinary career to deserve the opportunity to move on, and Bayern Munich must make sure that one costly mistake does not overshadow the broader problems exposed by this result.

title: Mike McCarthy Reveals Steelers Are Not Alone In Early Season Struggles
description: An NFL analyst points out a shocking truth about Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy after their viral sideline clash. The coach admits the team's record tells the whole story.
fullText:
The most surprising fact after the viral sideline fight between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy is not the anger itself, but the admission that the Steelers are not the only team feeling lost.

While fans watch the heated exchange on Thursday night, the head coach told reporters that almost every squad in the league feels just as stuck as Pittsburgh does right now. This perspective shifts the narrative from a single team's meltdown to a league-wide struggle that no one wants to admit out loud.

Mike McCarthy spent the weekend reviewing tape after the uneven loss to the Cleveland Browns, searching for answers in a game that ended with a 27-24 score. The first-year coach knows he is hardly alone in this mess. "You're hard-pressed to find a team or two that feels really good about where they are right now," he said, according to Times Observer.

This blunt assessment from the coach cuts through the noise of the viral video and suggests that the current chaos is the norm, not the exception, across the NFL.

Despite the frustration, McCarthy refuses to make excuses for the sloppy play that led to a fifth straight road setback in Cleveland. He laid out the hard truth about the team's standing with a simple shrug. "I mean, you are what you put on film and you are what your record says you are," McCarthy said. He followed that up by noting the current reality for the coaching staff and the players alike: "So, we're 2-2 as a coaching staff and as a football team."

This 2-2 record means the Steelers have won just half their games, leaving plenty of work to do before the Indianapolis Colts visit on Sunday. The team remains a work in progress, and the coach knows that looking the part is just as important as believing they can make it to January. The focus now shifts to fixing the mistakes that show up on the film before the next opponent arrives.

Instead of blaming the new system or the transition from the Mike Tomlin era, McCarthy points to his own habits as the solution. He insists that preparation is the only way to turn things around when things look wrong. "I'm a huge believer in preparation," McCarthy said.

He explained his personal approach to the problem, stating, "When it doesn't look right, I prepare more. That's the way I'm wired. That's the way I've always done it. That's what I'll continue to do, and we're going to be a better football team because of it."

This commitment to extra work is the only tool the coach has to get the team ready for a Colts squad that has been improving steadily since losing to Baltimore. The Colts have shown they can bounce back, so the Steelers must match that energy or risk falling further behind in a wide-open AFC North.

Indianapolis is not coming to Pittsburgh for a friendly visit, and their coach knows exactly how tough this game will be. Finding a way to win in the Steel City would prove that the Colts have moved past their late-season fade from last year. According to reports Shane Steichen said, "We know it's a big one."

He told his players that the challenge is huge because of the hostile environment they are walking into. The pressure is on both sides, but the Steelers must first settle their own internal issues before they can handle the pressure from the outside.

title: NASCAR Moves O’Reilly Series Race to Sunday as Carson Kvapil Starts On Pole at Charlotte
description: Weather Forces Major Schedule Change NASCAR has made a major change to its weekend schedule at Charlotte Motor Speedway, postponing the O’Reilly Auto Parts Series Blue Cross NC 300 from Saturday to Sunday night because of expected heavy rain. The race will now take place Sunday, October 11, at 8 p.m. Eastern, following the NASCAR…
fullText:
NASCAR has made a major change to its weekend schedule at Charlotte Motor Speedway, postponing the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Blue Cross NC 300 from Saturday to Sunday night because of expected heavy rain.

The race will now take place Sunday, October 11, at 8 p.m. Eastern, following the NASCAR Cup Series Bank of America 400, which is scheduled to begin at 3 p.m. Eastern. The postponement creates a doubleheader at Charlotte and gives fans an additional race to watch during an already important weekend in the NASCAR postseason.

The weather also forced NASCAR to cancel practice and qualifying for the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series. Officials had moved the sessions earlier on Saturday in an attempt to avoid the incoming rain, but conditions ultimately prevented teams from getting on track.

With qualifying canceled, NASCAR used its established starting-lineup formula to determine the field for Sunday's race. Carson Kvapil will start from the pole position, giving the JR Motorsports driver an important advantage heading into the 300 mile event.

Kvapil enters the weekend looking to build on his strong performance at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, where he finished second to Corey Day. His consistency has kept him near the top of the championship battle, and starting first at Charlotte gives him another opportunity to make a statement.

Corey Day will join Kvapil on the front row, setting up an interesting battle between two drivers who finished first and second at Las Vegas. Jesse Love will start third, followed by Brent Crews in fourth and Sam Mayer in fifth.

Starting on the pole gives Kvapil a valuable opportunity, but the lack of practice creates additional uncertainty for the entire field. Teams will have to prepare for the race without the usual chance to evaluate their cars on the track and make adjustments based on real-world conditions.

Charlotte's 1.5-mile oval places a premium on handling, speed and clean execution. With the O'Reilly Series race following the Cup Series event on Sunday, teams will also need to adjust to the revised schedule.

With the postseason continuing, every position matters for drivers fighting to advance toward the championship. Kvapil has an opportunity to capitalize on his pole position, while Day and the rest of the field will be looking to challenge him from the opening laps.

The weather has changed the weekend, but the stakes remain high. Sunday night now sets up an important showdown at Charlotte, with Kvapil leading the field and hoping to turn the pole into a victory.

title: Cristiano Ronaldo provisionally suspended by Portugal
description: Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by Portugal after walking out on the national team. Ronaldo left the Portugal squad after he was an unused substitute for a 2-1 win away to Norway in the Nations League on September 27.
fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been provisionally suspended by Portugal after walking out on the national team.

Ronaldo left the Portugal squad after he was an unused substitute for a 2-1 win away to Norway in the Nations League on September 27.

The 41-year-old, who has scored a record-breaking 146 goals in 234 appearances for his country, subsequently issued a near 2,000-word statement saying he withdrew from the squad after a "breach of trust" between him and head coach Jorge Jesus.

The Portuguese Football Federation have now acted, saying in a statement reported by Lisbon-based newspaper A Bola: "Disciplinary proceedings were initiated against Cristiano Ronaldo, by decision of the non-professional section, on October 9, 2026, with the objective of ascertaining the potential disciplinary relevance of the facts reported on October 7, 2026.

"Without prejudice to the automatic preventive suspension to which he was subject until the date of initiation, a non-automatic preventive suspension of the player was determined, and the proceedings were given urgent status.

"The proceedings were sent, on October 10, 2026, to the disciplinary instruction committee of the FPF (Portuguese Football Federation), with publicity excluded until the end of the investigation."

Ronaldo missed Portugal's following two fixtures, wins over Denmark and Norway, which left them top of Group A4 with four straight wins, fuelling speculation his international career could be over.

Jesus left the door open to the veteran forward in a press conference after Sunday's win against Norway, saying: "If he wants to, he'll return to the national team."

Ronaldo argued Jesus had reneged on an agreement about how many minutes he would play but apologised for his actions and accepted he deserved to be sanctioned.

He put his difficulties to one side with a goal for club side Al Nassr on Friday in their 3-0 Saudi Pro League victory against Diriyah.

title: Guimaraes puts Arsenal's title defence back on track, Chelsea shine
description: Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit. After a thumping 3-0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break, Mikel Arteta's side were staring at a second shock loss in as many matches after James Justin fired the visitors ahead with 55 minutes gone.
fullText:
Arsenal struck twice in eight second-half minutes to secure a comeback 2-1 win against Leeds at the Emirates Stadium and move level on points with Manchester City at the Premier League summit.

After a thumping 3-0 defeat at Brighton & Hove Albion before the international break, Mikel Arteta's side were staring at a second shock loss in as many matches after James Justin fired the visitors ahead with 55 minutes gone.

However, Riccardo Calafiori drew the champions level when he converted Ben White's header from close range in the 62nd minute, before substitute Bruno Guimaraes struck the decisive blow just six minutes after he came off the bench.

Arteta said of Guimaraes: "This is the level for Arsenal, every week, every game, every minute, every action that you have to be at.

"Against Brighton he wasn't at that level, and today he was much better, and he can still be much better, and that's what we have to demand."

Arsenal were below their best against a well-drilled Leeds side, who, prior to the contest, were unbeaten in the league.

But the Gunners' revival here puts their championship defence back on course, and places the onus on City, with Enzo Maresca's side contesting their first match since the club were found guilty of an avalanche of financial breaches, at Liverpool on Sunday.

Jordan Henderson was the unlikely hero as Chelsea's entertainers blew Bournemouth away in a comprehensive and chaotic 5-1 win at Stamford Bridge.

Former Liverpool captain Henderson, 36, scored two and set up one for Morgan Rogers while Joao Pedro also hit the net twice for the rampant Blues.

Ipswich produced a dramatic turnaround to beat Fulham 2-1 after late goals by Abdoul Ouattara and Dara O'Shea extended Alvaro Arbeloa's winless start to six Premier League matches.

Maxim De Cuyper and Jaouen Hadjam were both on the scoresheet as 10-man Brighton clinched a 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light.

Kristoffer Ajer's second-half equalizer ensured Brentford continued their unbeaten start to the Premier League season in an entertaining 2-2 draw at Aston Villa.

title: Players of the game from FSU's despair-inducing loss to Louisville
description: Florida State's 44-20 loss to Louisville was disastrous, but who are the players of the game for the Seminoles?
fullText:
The Florida State Seminoles traveled to play the Louisville Cardinals and put up yet another stinker in the Mike Norvell era, blowing a 14-0 lead and losing 44-20. They are now 3-3 on the season, including 1-2 in ACC games.

It was another disappointing performance by FSU, which was once again unable to handle adversity on the road and has several tough games ahead of them. The fans made their displeasure with Norvell and the rest of the program clear on social media.

Micahi Danzy was without question the brightest spot of the day, with two touchdowns. Florida State has now scored 20 or more points in all six of their games, and with a trip to a likely top-five Miami up next, they'll need any luck they can get if they are to stop the rival Hurricanes.

With all of this in mind, here are our players of the game.

Daniels was ok. Yes, he did throw one interception, but it was in garbage time while the Seminoles were down by a lot. He went 21/37 for 209 yards and two touchdowns last night, which, while not as impressive as his five-touchdown performance against Virginia, is still respectable.

We talked about Danzy already, but his first touchdown of the day helped FSU get out to a 14-0 lead and seemingly kept them in the driver's seat. His second helped the Seminoles cut Louisville's lead to 15.

Despite not finding the end zone, it wasn't a quiet day for Kromah, who tacked on 131 all-purpose yards against Louisville, 88 rushing and 43 receiving.

title: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns reportedly 'irked' owner James Dolan with extension talk comments
description: It seems like Karl-Anthony Towns has done enough talking in the media to make the owner of the organization unhappy. That could have been a major part in stopping the extension talks.
fullText:
Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns reportedly 'irked' owner James Dolan with extension talk comments originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Karl-Anthony Towns has been a great addition to the New York Knicks since they traded for him in 2024. After all, the center has helped the Knicks reach the NBA Finals and win a championship after a long wait.

New York has some big decisions to make regarding contract extensions. Towns is one of the players seeking an extension, but he doesn't feel like he has been offered a fair deal just yet.

"Simply put – I want to do something to keep the team together and can work with the Knicks and also values me. And none of those things are close to happening," Towns said.

During training camp, the two sides attempted to work out an agreement but were unable to reach a deal. On Friday, New York shut down extension talks with every player until later in the season.

"As an organization, our entire focus is on preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of. As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season," a Knicks spokesperson told ESPN's Shams Charania.

It turns out that Towns' comments about the two sides not being close to reaching an agreement reportedly pushed owner James Dolan over the edge, prompting him to halt extension discussions.

"Bobby Marks says that scenarios have been presented to the Knicks where Josh Hart and KAT (both CAA) accept contracts that keep the Knicks under the second apron in 2027-28. He says KAT's comments Monday irked Dolan, which prompted today's statement," New York Post's Stefan Bondy wrote.

This is now an interesting situation to monitor, as Towns appears to have upset someone within the organization he needs to work with to get an extension done. New York will have to find a way to resolve the situation with its veteran center.

Towns is a valuable piece of the puzzle for the Knicks, and everyone knows that. However, publicly expressing frustration over what he considers an unfair offer could complicate the situation as both sides try to find common ground.

title: Bears linked to trade reunion with All-Pro edge rusher at fifth-round pick price tag
description: This veteran All-Pro edge rusher would make a lot of sense for the Bears at this price.
fullText:
Bears linked to trade reunion with All-Pro edge rusher at fifth-round pick price tag originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Chicago Bears are 2-2 entering Week 5 and appear to be likely buyers at the trade deadline, barring a collapse over the next month.

If they're contenders by the early November trade deadline, one of the more obvious needs this team could look to fill is the edge rusher position. Fortunately, they might have a good option readily available.

Jonathan Jones of The Athletic linked the Bears to Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack for what could be a very intriguing trade reunion. He also shared the projected price of Mack, which came in at a very reasonable fifth-round value.

"But Khalil Mack to Chicago is something multiple league sources told me makes the most sense if both teams continue on their respective trajectories," Jones writes.

With the Bears an obvious landing spot for Mack in a trade, it's important to know what it might cost Chicago to acquire the veteran edge rusher from the Chargers.

Jones shared that, "One GM and one assistant GM on different teams slotted Mack's value as worthy of a fifth-round pick."

Chicago can afford that price, and with the 0-4 Chargers likely to be sellers by the November trade deadline, Mack to the Bears for a fifth makes perfect sense.

MORE: Justin Herbert leads four reasons why Chargers are an 0-4 disaster

Of course, another team in need of pass rush help could offer more to beat the Bears in this trade, but there isn't a more sensible landing spot for Mack this season.

He previously played with the Bears during his lengthy NFL career, and the Bears are in clear need of pass rush help as well. With the cap space to make a trade work, and this fifth-round evaluation, a trade for Mack would make too much sense for the Bears.

The biggest hurdle will be whether the Chargers sell or not. A loss in Week 5 to the Denver Broncos for the Chargers could be a good thing for the Bears, as it'd likely increase the odds that Mack is available.

So long as Ryan Poles and the Bears are willing to move a fifth-round pick, and maybe more, to land Mack, then they should have a realistic chance of landing the potential future Hall of Famer when it's all said and done.

title: SEC Nation analyst reveals the key for Oklahoma's defense on Saturday
description: Chase Daniel says Oklahoma's defense must hit Arch Manning early to disrupt the Texas quarterback.
fullText:
The Oklahoma Sooners and the No. 1 Texas Longhorns will meet in the 122nd edition of the Red River Rivalry on Saturday. The Longhorns enter the game 4-0 with national championship expectations, while Oklahoma enters at 2-2 with major question marks.

Star quarterback Arch Manning leads the Longhorns. He's thrown for 862 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions, while completing 63.5% of his passes. The Sooners' defense leads the way. They rank No. 5 in total defense, No. 4 in passing yards allowed, No. 41 in rushing yards allowed and No. 25 in scoring defense.

"SEC Nation" was outside the Cotton Bowl to preview Saturday's matchup. College football analyst Chase Daniel identified the key to the Sooners' defense.

"I agree with (Steve Sarkisian) that Arch Manning is playing better than he was last year," Daniel said. "But he's a completely different quarterback when he gets hit. That's where I think OU defensively, they have to hit him. He's been hit 45 times in the last three weeks... I think that's the biggest thing for OU defensively. Can you hit Arch Manning early?"

Oklahoma's defense has a clear challenge heading into the Red River Rivalry: make Manning uncomfortable from the opening drive. The Sooners have talent to pressure the Texas quarterback, but they will need to do it without losing their assignments or giving him easy opportunities to exploit the defense. Consistent pressure could disrupt Texas' offensive rhythm and give Oklahoma's offense more chances to make the most of its possessions.

With the rivalry offering a chance to reset the narrative, Oklahoma's defense could play a major role in determining how the game unfolds. If the Sooners win at the line of scrimmage, deliver timely hits and force Manning into difficult decisions, they can build a strong foundation to compete with the Longhorns and leave Dallas with momentum.
