title: Game Day Q&A With Roll Bama Roll
description: Longtime readers of this site will know that while we here at Dawg Sports love all our fellow SB Nation sister sites, but that we have a special place in our hearts for the crew over at Roll Bama Roll, SB Nation’s home for Alabama Crimson Tide coverage. The reasons for that are numerous. For […]
fullText:
Longtime readers of this site will know that while we here at Dawg Sports love all our fellow SB Nation sister sites, but that we have a special place in our hearts for the crew over at Roll Bama Roll, SB Nation's home for Alabama Crimson Tide coverage. The reasons for that are numerous. For one, they have a southern fried football sensibility that meshes well with our own. Two, they take the game as seriously as we do, and have seen enough good and bad to know how special it is to root for a championship football team. And third, the writers over there are uniformly knowledgeable about Crimson Tide football in a way that only true fans can be.

So it's a happy accident (or maybe an inevitable reality) that our two obsessive fanbases have watched our respective finely-tuned football programs face off in high stakes football games side by side almost annually for over a decade. As best I can tell the first of these opponent Q&As with RBR occurred during this site's first full season of operations in 2007. It's always a pleasure to participate, and always informative to read.

This time out I was joined by RBR editor and longtime friend Brent Taylor, who knows as much about Crimson Tide football as anyone who isn't named Kalen and didn't use to coach at the University of Washington. And to be fair, that guy could learn a thing or two if he'd just let Brent bend his ear now and then.I hope you'll enjoy Brent's insights as much as I did.

MD: Is it safe to say Keelon Russell has answered the questions surrounding him early in the year? Just how excited are Bama fans about his ceiling, and how can Georgia hope to contain him?

Brent: I was questioning him HARD the first 2.25 games. Even with the Tide scoring plenty and him putting up numbers, I wasn't sold because all of his plays were scramble drill type of stuff.

Something flipped during the FSU game, though, and since then Russell has been operating a passing game on time and navigating within a pocket like a maestro.

He was the highest ranked recruit that Alabama has ever signed for a reason: he's got it all. Pocket presence, decision making, incredible arm and accuracy, and extremely fast.

The ceiling is a Heisman and a #1 overall selection in two years. But he's got to prove it with consistency.

Biggest keys for containing him are 1) that your DL cant get selfish going for sacks or he'll just slip right through rushing lanes, and 2) Kentucky did a good job against him, mostly by blitzing relentlessly. He's started to beat that more against further opponents, but its still the only thing that's worked so far.

MD: It seems like it's been a solid two weeks since I've seen an Alabama fan on Twitter declare that Kalen DeBoer just isn't the man for the job in Tuscaloosa. Is there any factual scenario under which he's in any job jeopardy in 2026?

Brent: Unless we finish the regular season with 4+ losses (basically losing out from here), DeBoer's job is not in jeopardy. We're relentless critics as Alabama fans, so there's grumbling about literally everything. And we're also great at revisionist history and acting like Nick Saban never had a bad game.

MD: The Crimson Tide defense is generating turnovers at an alarming, SEC-leading rate. How are they doing that, and can they keep it up?

Brent: As always, turnovers are somewhat luck. Two of MSUs turnovers were ones where Kamarion Taylor just inexplicably dropped the ball ans one where he got a little pressure in his face but missed his man terribly. Still, the Alabama defense has been great at dropping into flat and hook zones with some deception, and they've racked up some picks doing that (and turning them into scores). So I think the Tide will continue to be one of the better teams in the country at forcing turnovers, but it will probably regress a bit from the pace we've been on.

MD: It seems like only ten months ago that these teams were meeting in the Benz and the Georgia defense was making Ty Simpson revisit his every life choice. What are the biggest differences between that team and the one that will take the field in Tuscaloosa on Saturday playing as well as anyone in the country?

Brent: The offensive line is night and day from the disaster we had on the field a year ago. Its been totally overhauled (4/5 new players and a new coach), and that change had been the catalyst for Alabama looking like a legitimate contender. The coaching effort, and attention to detail are just leagues above a year ago, and its pretty much that simple.

On the other side of the ball, the defensive line also got overhauled, and they're playing with a lot more consistency than last year as well.

MD: I would argue that there are no "under the radar" players at a program followed as closely as Bama's. But to the extent you can, tell me one player on the Tide roster Bulldog fans haven't heard of yet but who could make a huge impact on Saturday.

Brent: TE Josh Ford is my pick. He transferred in from Oklahoma State, and, in my opinion, epitomizes and has maybe even led the identity change in the Alabama offense to a physical blocking team. Ford isn't much of a pass catcher, but holy moly is he a powerful and aggressive blocker.

MD: Fill in the blanks: Georgia is in trouble in this game if they _____. Alabama is in danger if they ____.

Brent: I think this hinges on the same answer: Georgia passing the ball downfield.

If the Bulldogs cant get a medium-to-deep passing game going, then the Alabama defense has been excellent at run stuffing and defending the short passing game. Plus Keelon Russell and the Tide rushing attack has just felt inevitable.

However, Alabama has struggled with downfield coverage issues intermittently all season, so if Gunner Stockton can take advantage of that, get the lead, and get the Tide out of boa constrictor mode, then we don't know how the offense might respond.

MD: Because we must: what's your score prediction?

Brent: My optimism for the Tide the last two weeks has really increased, but that SEC Championship performance (or lack thereof) still lingers in my psyche. Georgia is tough for me because they've looked like the best team in the country to this point, but have done so with a faily weak early schedule and are relatively untested.

My head says Alabama has a good chance of winning (like 55%), but my heart isn't ready for that. Let's go 35-31 UGA.

thanks as always to Brent for his insightful responses. If you'd like, you can take a look at my responses to questions Brent posed over at Bama roll. Until later… thanks as always to Brent for his insightful responses. If you'd like, you can take a look at my responses to questions Brent posed over at Roll Bama Roll. Until later…

title: Draymond Green believes people should leave LeBron James alone for his helicopter trips
description: LeBron James' constant helicopter trips from Philadelphia to New York City have continued to make headlines.
fullText:
Draymond Green believes people should leave LeBron James alone for his helicopter trips originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

LeBron James seems to be enjoying his time playing for the Philadelphia 76ers so far. The basketball has been good for the 76ers, but it seems that another story is overshadowing the potential for good basketball in Philly.

That story is LeBron regularly taking a helicopter to go from Philly to New York City, where he is reportedly settling while playing for the 76ers. It has caused an uproar across social media because some people feel he's not fully committing to his new team.

James is regularly riding a chopper to commute between Manhattan and Philadelphia for both practices and games. The flight takes about 30 to 45 minutes, which is much better than a drive in traffic that will double that time.

He is also using a corporate helicopter that is provided through his endorsement deal with Fanatics. It does not involve the 76ers at all, but it seems that it's the fans who are not big fans of this move.

MORE: LeBron James admits that he is finding his stride with the 76ers in preseason

Some feel that it is him not committing to the team and the city. That is a valid point, but it seems James is not like most players because the organization is allowing it, and his teammates seem to not pay any mind to it. Another person who does not mind it is Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green.

"Number one, like, let that man fly in peace. Like, y'all recording this man every time he take off and land and he's landing in the city and landing, leaving like, let that man fly in peace. Let that brother get to work. How he going to get to work and get home? How he going to get home," Green said on his podcast about James' helicopter trips.

At the end of the day, it seems the 76ers are okay with him making the trip regularly. Since the helicopters are driven by professionals, it seems that James won't have any pushback from his team, so people might need to accept that.

title: ‘Focus on your batting’: Wasim Jaffer questions Yashasvi Jaiswal’s wicketkeeping move
description: Wasim Jaffer has raised eyebrows over Yashasvi Jaiswal’s late venture into wicketkeeping practice as he gears up for the Ranji Trophy. Jaffer pointed out the difficulty of mastering wicketkeeping, particularly without foundational training. He recommends that Jaiswal focus on his batting skills instead, especially since he aims to secure a spot on India's white-ball teams.
fullText:
NEW DELHI: Former India opener Wasim Jaffer has questioned Yashasvi Jaiswal's decision to take up wicketkeeping at the age of 24, urging the India Test opener to concentrate on his batting rather than attempt to develop a demanding new skill. Jaiswal's reported move to work on his wicketkeeping has drawn attention ahead of the 2026-27 domestic season, with the left-handed batter seen wearing the gloves during Mumbai's preparations for the Ranji Trophy.

Mumbai captain Siddhesh Lad recently revealed that Jaiswal had been working on his wicketkeeping skills as a possible back-up option to his batting and part-time leg-spin. Lad suggested that the 24-year-old could eventually aim to keep wickets for Mumbai or even India, although he admitted that he did not have complete clarity on Jaiswal's plans.

Jaffer, however, was surprised by the development and questioned whether wicketkeeping was a practical option for a batter who had not trained in the role from a young age.

"I myself was surprised when I heard this. It is very difficult if you have not kept wickets since childhood. First of all, it is a very demanding job. Apart from that, where is that place even if he starts? There are Ishan Kishan, Sanju Samson, and Rishabh Pant. I am sure he wants to do it in white-ball cricket," Jaffer said on his YouTube channel.

Jaffer stressed that wicketkeeping, particularly in Test cricket, requires considerable preparation and cannot be mastered quickly. Rather than dividing his attention between batting and an entirely new skill, the former Mumbai captain believes Jaiswal should focus on strengthening his primary game.

"It is very difficult in Test cricket. But I feel this is a bit of a joke because wicket-keeping is not an easy task if you have not done it since childhood. It is not an easy skill that you can develop very quickly," Jaffer said.

The former India opener also suggested that Jaiswal could be looking for ways to improve his chances of breaking into India's white-ball sides. Despite establishing himself as a key batter in Test cricket, the left-hander has yet to secure a regular place in the ODI and T20I setups.

"I think he is getting a little desperate to get into the white-ball teams. I think he needs to focus on his batting ahead of the Ranji Trophy and the New Zealand tour," Jaffer added.

Jaiswal is expected to feature in Mumbai's Ranji Trophy opener against Chandigarh at the Wankhede Stadium on Sunday. He is also understood to have kept wickets for around 10 overs during one of Mumbai's practice matches ahead of the domestic season.

Lad had indicated that Jaiswal was keen to explore wicketkeeping as a potential additional skill, while making it clear that the batter's long-term plans remained uncertain.

"With Yashasvi, I feel he is trying hard to start keeping wickets; that's what I heard from him. He wants to eventually, in future, keep wickets for maybe Mumbai or go on to keep wickets for the Indian team. This is what he is aiming for, that is what I feel. But I haven't got any clarity on that," Lad said at a pre-season press conference, as reported by ESPNcricinfo.

title: Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri Move On After Talks Post Singapore GP Sprint Collision
description: Oscar Piastri expands on post-sprint talks after he and Lando Norris got together in F1 Singapore GP, as they have moved on from it. The FIA stewards adjudged both as guilty parties in the last lap collision between McLaren teammates…
fullText:
Oscar Piastri expands on post-sprint talks after he and Lando Norris got together in F1 Singapore GP, as they have moved on from it.

The FIA stewards adjudged both as guilty parties in the last lap collision between McLaren teammates Piastri and Norris in the F1 Singapore GP sprint. The Brit tried a move taking the inside line on the Australian, but their rear wheels tapped and they spun around.

While Piastri retired immediately after hitting the barrier, Norris managed to continue and finish eighth to score a point. It looked like the Brit may be handed a penalty, but the stewards thought both drivers contributed to the incident, with not one wholly to be blamed.

Norris apologised on the radio, as, post-sprint, he noted that he had gone for a gap and that his car was with Piastri, that meant he had the right to space. The Australian, meanwhile, did not expect a move from the Brit and by the time he could move, they collided.

New document: Doc 59 – Decision – Car 81 – Alleged causing a collision with car 1Published on 10.10.26 15:40 CET#F1 #Formula1 #FIA #SingaporeGP

https://t.co/rRAAU4CVkc— FIA F1 Documents Bot (@fiadocsbot) October 10, 2026

Naturally, they held talks with Zak Brown and Andrea Stella before F1 Singapore GP qualifying and have moved on from the episode. "As you probably expect, no one's very happy, I'm not happy, Oscar's not happy," said Norris to the media.

"None of us wanted to go that way. There was things both of us could have done better and, yeah, we spoke about it, and we've moved on," summed up Norris. Teammate Piastri concurred with the Brit's say, highlighting the loss of points.

Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri | Photo Credit: McLaren F1 Team

He found the positive aspect that the McLaren F1 pair are good at apologising after a mistake and moving on. "Yeah, I mean the biggest thing obviously is we just can't have that happen in terms of the points and, yeah, for the workload and money," said Piastri.

"Yeah, just wasn't a situation that needed to happen really, so yeah, Lando apologised and yeah, [we] moved on. Unfortunately, it's not our first coming together, but we always, I think we're both very good at saying sorry when we need to and moving on, and I think that's what makes us strong as a team."

When pressed if Piastri accepts the blame on his side, the Australian did not clearly answer. He felt it was just not a smart move, considering he didn't mind finishing behind Norris, as the net result in terms of points was to be the same for McLaren.

"Not really for me to say, but I think in the context we were going to have the same amount of points either way, and I didn't really mind if I finished behind him," said Piastri. "I don't really mind. I mean, I don't think there was anything massively out of line, but at the same time, it's not very smart to try and get each other penalty."

But Piastri stated that there was no need for 'Papaya Rules', considering the situation is vastly different to last year, when the rules were put in place. He reiterated that it wasn't a bad move from Norris, just a bit unnecessary in that situation.

"It was just in isolation," continued Piastri. "Obviously, the situation this year is worlds apart from last year. I think, yeah, it was just a shame for the team to miss out on points and add to the workload and the damage bill, that's all.

"Again Lando, I don't think it wasn't a bad manoeuvre necessarily, I think just in the context of where we are, yeah, maybe it didn't need to happen, but no, we moved on as a team and what we got," summed up Piastri, who qualified seventh in an average performance, with Norris in fifth in F1 Singapore GP qualifying for Sunday's race.

title: Garrett Whitlock injury news raises new questions about Red Sox medical staff
description: Another significant injury to a key Sox player was not properly diagnosed.
fullText:
On Friday morning, a picture was posted to Instagram from Garrett Whitlock's wife, Jordan, showing an offseason beach picture of Garrett, overlooking the beach, with the hashtag #thriving. Less than notable, living his best life. Except for, you know, the walking boot that Whitlock was wearing.

Garrett Whitlock with some type of boot on. Not the same leg as his knee injury from over the summer. Notable. pic.twitter.com/nEENu0nhMv

We learned later on Friday from Gabrielle Starr that Whitlock had been pitching with "a fractured right tibia that was not properly diagnosed until after the Red Sox were eliminated from the postseason last week, the 30-year-old reliever told the Herald on Friday."

This season, we also had Garrett Crochet's shoulder and lat soreness that lingered from late April into September. We had Roman Anthony's hand/wrist injury which, as Matt Gross outlined in great detail, was a wrist sprain (day-to-day), and then a minimum IL stint, which was actually a ligament in his ring finger for a bit more than a minimum IL stint, which was also a sprained right hand/wrist progressing slower than expected, to not swinging a bat a month later, to getting sent to Fort Myers which may or may not have been to send a message, to missing nearly four months of MLB game action.

During Monday's press conference, when asked about why Anthony did not get any additional imaging after early July, Breslow pushed back asking why they would need to do that if the player hadn't asked for it.

Good for Garrett Whitlock pitching through his injury to the tune of a 0.00 ERA in September, but perhaps this team's medical staff needs to be a little bit more proactive when it comes to identifying injuries and not just trusting the player that "they're fine."

Discuss this, and whatever else you have on your mind about baseball in October in the comments, and be good to each other.

title: Will Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney determine the 2027 coaching carousel?
description: If Clemson were to move on from head coach Dabo Swinney, college football’s coaching carousel would be completely shaken up.
fullText:
A $57 million buyout makes replacing Dabo Swinney an expensive proposition. But ESPN's Pete Thamel sees Clemson's more pressing question as what changes the program makes around him.

The Tigers' coach appeared in Thamel's examination of six buyouts that could shape college football's coaching carousel, ranking behind only USC's Lincoln Riley. His inclusion came with a clear distinction.

"Clemson is not firing Swinney," Thamel said. "Let's start there."

Thamel pointed to Swinney's championship résumé, his connection to the university and the financial cost of a dismissal. Still, keeping the coach leaves Clemson with decisions about how to restore a program that once regularly competed for national titles.

At 3-2, the Tigers have opportunities to build a respectable season. Their losses to LSU and Miami, however, have exposed a gap that another winning record alone would not erase.

Thamel's analysis raised questions about the coaching staff, Clemson's personnel operation and how aggressively it will pursue transfers. The Tigers added 10 defensive transfers last offseason but just one on offense.

One particularly significant decision could involve freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds. Clemson could invest in his development or pursue a proven transfer, with Thamel estimating that a top quarterback could cost at least $5 million.

"But there remains a vexing gap to close to catch up to the sport's elite," Thamel wrote.

Clemson football schedule: Are the Tigers playing today?

📸 Butch Dill, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect https://t.co/OKLHRB1r8I pic.twitter.com/T1TAmIxBrm

The discussion also included two coaches awaiting Clemson later this season: Florida State's Mike Norvell and South Carolina's Shane Beamer. Their buyouts stand at approximately $51 million and $22.5 million, respectively.

Clemson visits the Seminoles on Oct. 31 before hosting the Gamecocks on Nov. 28.

For Swinney, the immediate task is preparing for Charleston Southern on Oct. 17. The broader challenge is showing that Clemson can turn its next round of decisions into meaningful progress.

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. was an elite prospect, and didn't even last three seasons in Arizona before he was traded
description: Marvin Harrison never broke out for the Cardinals and now he's on the move.
fullText:
Marvin Harrison Jr. was one of the best wide receiver prospects ever.

That's why, even though he didn't work out for teams before the 2024 NFL Draft, he was still picked fourth overall by the Arizona Cardinals. The first three picks were Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye, all franchise quarterbacks off to remarkable starts to their pro careers.

There was no way Harrison was going to fall flat in Arizona, until he did. On Saturday, ESPN reported that Harrison will be traded after Sunday's games. When it was reported it wasn't certain which team Harrison was going to and for what compensation, only that Harrison's career in Arizona was done.

Of all the possible outcomes for Harrison's NFL career, being done with the Cardinals and shipped off after just 33 games for far less than Arizona invested in him was practically unthinkable.

The can't-miss prospect missed, somehow. At least in his first NFL stop.

Harrison was a phenomenal college player. In 2022 he had 1,263 yards and 14 touchdowns. Then his quarterback, C.J. Stroud, went to the NFL. And in 2023 Harrison had 1,211 yards for 14 touchdowns.

It's not like Harrison was dominating bad competition. He had two 100-yard games against Michigan. He had 185 yards and then 162 against Penn State. In a bowl game against Georgia he had 102 yards and two touchdowns. He was facing high-level competition and putting up ridiculous production.

Harrison not working out at the combine or in any drills was unusual, but the results at Ohio State were so good it didn't matter. Maybe it should have. When the Cardinals picked Harrison, no reasonable draft analyst was against it. He was widely considered the top non-quarterback in that draft class.

Then the results never came. He had a respectable 885 yards and eight touchdowns as a rookie, though 130 yards and two touchdowns came in one game against the Rams and that proved to be an outlier. That was in Harrison's second game, and over the rest of his Cardinals career he had just one 100-yard game.

In Harrison's second season, when he was out due to injury, Michael Wilson had three 100-yard games and another with 99. Wilson simply looked better in the offense than the platinum prospect out of Ohio State, which was alarming. Harrison had just 608 yards and four touchdowns in 12 games last season. A new coaching staff came in. Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million contract extension in September, a sign of how much the Cardinals valued him.

And when Harrison started the season slowly, it seemed clear that he could get traded. There were just no signs that a breakout was coming.

Harrison had one catch through two games this season. A video of his routes, in which he wasn't explosive or just not playing hard enough, went viral.

The player who didn't run for scouts before the combine couldn't separate. The superstar in college who routinely put up 100 yards was the fourth option, at best, in the Cardinals offense. He finished this season for Arizona, assuming the trade goes through, with five catches for 85 yards.

Harrison could still emerge as a good NFL receiver. He's 24 years old. It went sour in Arizona but sometimes a trade wakes a player up. Perhaps he'll do better in his new home. The reasons he was a great prospect still exist, though it's hard to remember those traits after his mediocrity with the Cardinals.

It can still happen for Harrison, but it will happen somewhere else if it does. When Arizona drafted Harrison, the Cardinals celebrated. They couldn't figure that they'd be throwing in the towel before Harrison's third season was half over.

title: Are Browns fans pumping the breaks on playoff talks this early?
description: Playoffs for the Browns? Ok, maybe fans aren’t that optimistic yet.
fullText:
The Browns have now been victorious in three straight games and lead the AFC North. People around the NFL are starting to talk positively about the Browns, and that of course means that Cleveland fans themselves are going to feel like they are on cloud nine a bit. Week-to-week, fan confidence increased by 15 percentage points up to 83%, a new season high. By comparison, Jets fans are not happy with their outlook, with only 18% of fans being in favor of the direction of their team.

Take Reacts surveys, create Browns polls, and see how your answers compare with fellow Dawgs By Nature fans. Then discuss the results with the Dawg Pound.

Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android.

Besides the confidence meter, the main question we asked this week was a simple Yes or No question, asking if you think the Browns will make the playoffs. Only 38% of fans said Yes, while 62% of fans said No. Based on the confidence results, you can see fans gaining traction, but it's too early for the overall fanbase to be convinced that the Browns can make the playoffs. I was actually surprised how low the Yes vote was here, as things are looking quite optimistic for Cleveland, when you factor in their easy schedule. On the topic, one Browns fan said:

I'm not buying into this possibility until we win some games definitively, like from beginning to end. All the late game heroics coupled with the fact that this team is full of young and inexperienced players that are still adjusting (along with a new O-Line that is also still adjusting to a new team/system) tells me that this party is going to end at some point.

Another fan debated which teams we'd have to beat out for a wildcard spot:

Who might they have to beat out for a wild card to make the playoffs? Bengals, Patriots, Broncos, Raiders? Are we better then 3 of them?

On a national scale, fans were asked which team between the Browns, Giants, Vikings, and Raiders will finish with the worst record. The Browns led the way with 46% of the vote, which means that even though Cleveland has turned heads, the broader audience of fans still thinks Cleveland will fall off at some point.

According to FanDuel, the Browns are 1.5 point underdogs against the Jets this week, with the over/under being 39.5.

title: Rayo Vallecano game abandoned after paper plane protest
description: Rayo Vallecano's match against Athletic Club was abandoned after the home fans threw paper airplanes onto the pitch in protest against the club's owner.
fullText:
Rayo Vallecano's match against Athletic Club was abandoned on Saturday after the home fans threw paper planes and rubber balls on to the pitch in protest against the club's owner.

The La Liga game was Rayo's first of the season at the Estadio de Vallecas, which had been temporarily closed after an audit highlighted serious health and safety issues - including a risk of contracting Legionnaires' disease.

Rayo fans blame owner and president Raul Martin Presa, who has long been criticised for the poor upkeep of facilities and a failure to modernise the club.

In the 13th minute of the game, when Rayo fans usually chant "Presa leave now", supporters threw paper planes and small rubber balls on to the pitch.

The referee stopped play and the stadium announcer urged fans not to throw objects on to the pitch, while stewards hastily removed the items from the grass.

When play resumed 15 minutes later, supporters in the south stand again threw objects on to the field and the referee abandoned play with the game goalless.

Following the game, Athletic Club released a statement to say they would contact their fans who travelled to the game in Madrid to arrange refunds.

Last season, the Spanish football association published a letter written by Rayo's players that described the Vallecas pitch as "unplayable" and noted a lack of hot water in the showers and inadequate cleaning.

They began last season without being able to use their own training ground because of mould. However, they were able to reach the final of the Uefa Conference League, which they lost 1-0 to Crystal Palace.

Supporters regularly have to queue for hours to purchase match tickets at the stadium's small box office as Rayo is the only top-flight Spanish club without a ticketing website.

Rayo sit 13th in La Liga with two wins from their opening seven games.

title: Darkness Falls beats Desert Castle in Dewhurst Stakes
description: Darkness Falls proves the stronger to narrowly beat Desert Castle in the Dewhurst Stakes at Newmarket.
fullText:
Darkness Falls proved the stronger to narrowly beat Desert Castle in the Dewhurst Stakes at Newmarket.

The pair led the five runners in the race for the line and Darkness Falls, ridden by Ryan Moore, held off favourite and previously unbeaten Desert Castle, who had William Buick on board.

Aidan O'Brien-trained Darkness Falls had dropped back to seven furlongs from a mile-and-one after winning the Golden Fleece Stakes at Leopardstown last time out.

"He's a really good colt," Moore told ITV Sport. "It feels like there's 

"How far he'll go I don't know, he has a lot of pace."

O'Brien added: "It was a big call to come here and it's incredible to bring a horse back from nine furlongs to win a Dewhurst.

"We've always loved him and he's always had a lot of class. Ryan gave him a brilliant ride and I'm so grateful to win this for everyone, he's very exciting.

"We came here to give him the experience with a view to the Guineas and we were always going to find out plenty.

"It was a massive ask to bring him back to seven furlongs, it was a tough nine at Leopardstown last time and he has so much class obviously.

"He's so exciting, as you saw what he did over nine furlongs and I don't think he'll have any problem going further either, he has a lot of quality.

"When they have as much class as he has they can do anything and the Triple Crown is the dream."

The Triple Crown covers the 2,000 Guineas, the Derby and the St Leger, with Nijinsky - in 1970 - the last horse to win all three races in a year.

title: 'We lost the life of a brother' - rider protest delays Giro di Lombardia
description: Riders at the Giro di Lombardia stage a protest over safety concerns which delays the start for five minutes, before 20-year-old Paul Seixas goes on to victory.
fullText:
Riders at the Giro di Lombardia staged a protest which delayed the start of the race by five minutes as they sought to draw attention to safety concerns following a series of incidents.

Organisers completed the countdown and a starting flag was waved but the peloton remained stationary, creating confusion among spectators in Bergamo, Italy.

Belgium's Remco Evenepoel then addressed the crowd, saying "there are too many incidents happening with vehicles in the race" and highlighting the death of British cyclist Fin Tarling, who died in a collision with a vehicle at the Volta a Portugal in August.

"Unfortunately we lost the life of a brother and a colleague, so we want to make this statement to show to the world that we cannot keep accepting the fact that guys are getting injured or literally dying in what we like the most to do," added double Olympic champion Evenepoel.

After five minutes had elapsed, a second starting flag was waved and the riders set off for Como.

French 20-year-old Paul Seixas broke with 19km to go to become the youngest winner of the Giro di Lombardia and the youngest winner of a Monument race since 1944.

Seixas finished 48 seconds ahead of Spain's Enric Mas, having dropped Italy's Giulio Ciccone and Great Britain's Tom Pidcock, who finished third and sixth respectively, shortly after his break.

His solo ride for over 18km saw him take a Monument title in only his third appearance, having made his debut with a seventh-place finish in this race last year.

"This week alone, there were multiple incidents of vehicles on race courses," said the CPA union, which represents professional cyclists, in a statement which was re-posted on Instagram by riders including Evenepoel and Pidcock., external

"This summer, a life was tragically lost to exactly this kind of failure. We will not stand for this any longer."

The CPA has called for cycling's governing body, the UCI, to help ensure race organisers "take responsibility" and "act" to improve safety standards.

Earlier this week, Thomas Gloag and Marcel Camprubi were struck by a police motorcycle travelling in the opposite direction during the Tre Valli Varesine race.

"Riders race at high speed with little protection, and we depend on the UCI and race organisers to secure the roads. That responsibility is not being met," the CPA statement added.

"We did not want to affect the race, only to show what riders can do when we stand as one.

"We love this sport. We respect the race organisers. We want to race hard and put on a show for our fans. However most importantly we want to come home safe to our loved ones."

The Giro di Lombardia is the last of the season's five Monuments, a set of long-standing, prestigious one-day races.

It has been won by Tadej Pogacar for the past five years but the Slovenian was not present at the race, which is also the penultimate event on this year's UCI World Tour calendar, after sustaining a season-ending injury at the Vuelta a Espana.

Seixas, who finished fourth in this year's Tour de France, also finished second behind Pogacar at Liege–Bastogne–Liege, his only other Monument appearance this season.

The Decathlon–CMA CGM rider is the first Frenchman to win a Monument since Julian Alaphilippe at Milan–San Remo in 2019, and the first to triumph at the Giro di Lombardia since Thibaut Pinot in 2018.

Il Lombardia is known in Italy as The Race of the Falling Leaves and changes in seasonal temperature often makes for a tricky event.

The barometer for cyclists' thresholds for danger is changing too. Several riders have died, or been seriously injured, in and out of competition in the past five years.

The protest leader, Evenepoel, himself nearly lost his life in this race in 2020 following a harrowing crash on a descent.

And it's been a harrowing season – the loss of 19-year-old Tarling has stunned the whole sport, and the fury of the peloton has been evident.

Even the sport's best rider is not in Lombardy because of a serious, season-ending, crash, and cars continue to enter closed public roads in races.

The UCI recently published results of a consultation to reform cycling, which treats safety as "non-negotiable, with stricter enforcement of existing requirements".

Such changes may not exist in the sport before 2029.

But the riders want change now.

title: Verstappen beats Ferraris to Singapore pole
description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen beats the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton to pole position in qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix.
fullText:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second pole position in a week by beating the Ferraris of Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in qualifying at the Singapore Grand Prix.

Verstappen's first lap in final qualifying was enough to take pole, his time fending off a second lap from Leclerc that was 0.054 seconds off pole.

Hamilton was closest to Verstappen after the first runs but was unable to improve on his second run.

In fact, most of the front runners struggled to improve on their second runs, as Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli took fourth on the grid, from McLaren's Lando Norris.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell was sixth fastest but will drop to the back of the grid with a penalty for using too many engine parts.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was the only driver in the top four teams other than Leclerc to improve on his second run but could do no better than qualify seventh.

Alpine's Pierre Gasly and the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

Verstappen wins sprint after Russell crashes out

Verstappen came to Singapore fresh from his and Red Bull's first victory of the season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and he has continued where he left off.

The four-time champion has looked the man to beat all weekend, and took pole for the grand prix a few hours after winning the sprint, following Russell crashing out of the lead.

Verstappen said: "This was the one I really wanted. The car has been really strong all weekend.

"We have been on a really on a positive trend and it's really special to take the pole here."

Leclerc felt pole had been on the cards if he had not made a few small mistakes on his final lap.

He said: "Q1 and Q2 were really difficult. I had some weird struggles under braking. Q3, the lap was OK. I did some mistakes. I think there was a potential to be on pole today but Max just did a better job."

Hamilton, second to Verstappen in the sprint, was quickest in the first and second parts of qualifying but could not repeat that pace when it mattered during what he described as "another difficult Q3".

He added: "The car was feeling much better. I really felt she had 

"I think there's a really fine line with our car whether you are over or under the sweet spot and I didn't get it quite right today."

Hamilton said he had adjusted brake balance on his car for the final part of qualifying and he thought it had "just tipped it a little over the edge".

Sunday, 11 October at 13:00 BST

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

Antonelli's fourth place was the first relatively bright moment for the Mercedes upgrade that was introduced in Malaysia but about which the team have question marks.

Although it shows in the data to have more downforce than the previous specification, which Russell is running this weekend, it has proved difficult to access that.

In that context, for Antonelli to be only 0.189secs from pole could appear to be a promising step forward after being only seventh in sprint qualifying on Friday, even if the upgrade was still expected to deliver more performance than so far has been the case.

Russell, who crashed out of the sprint at the end of the first lap, said he had competed in qualifying "mainly just to make sure the car was feeling as it did yesterday after the crash but it didn't quite feel the same".

He added: "I had great pace yesterday. We were in the top three every lap I completed. And today I wasn't in the top five at any point throughout the session so we need to understand why that is."

McLaren had hoped for a step forward this weekend after struggling in the past two races but fifth and seventh marked only a small amount of progress for the world champions, despite flashes of promise through the weekend.

Norris said: "In the end we're where we should be. Nothing has changed so no reason why we would suddenly be on the pace. I could put good bits together, but the car is just too much of a challenge, I have to feel like I am almost crashing to put in a purple sector but you just can't do that, the tyres don't survive, the car is too difficult to be in that perfect limit when it's quick."

Norris addressed the incident with Piastri on the final lap of the sprint race, when an attack by the Briton into Turn Five led to them colliding, and turning what had been fourth and fifth places into an eighth for Norris and retirement for Piastri.

Norris said: "There are two sides. One is what the stewards say and that's a fair reasoning, no-one's to blame.

"But I did apologise because it was still me attacking, as I had the right to do. If I just sat there and was boring like I should be, nothing would have happened. So really it's still my fault but I deserved to go for the space and I still believe I had the right for it."

title: Hincapie injury adds to Arsenal issues after Guimaraes rescue act
description: Heroics and battling performances have already become a theme of Arsenal's season with Bruno Guimaraes coming to the rescue again.
fullText:
For the second time in three Premier League matches, Bruno Guimaraes has come to Arsenal's rescue.

Having sparked their 2-0 win at Sunderland in September with the crucial first goal, the £75m summer signing came off the bench again to have a pivotal impact against Leeds on Saturday.

This time it was the winner as the Gunners came from behind for a 2-1 success in a testing encounter at Emirates Stadium.

But Ecuador international Piero Hincapie was carried off during the warm-down, raising concern the defender has suffered an injury.

He came on as a late substitute against Daniel Farke's side but completed extra running after the final whistle - a practice most clubs use.

A fifth win in six league games put Mikel Arteta's side level on points with leaders Manchester City, but their title defence has certainly not been without its scares so far.

Following on from their comprehensive 3-0 defeat at Brighton last time out, Arsenal fell behind in a league match for a third time in four league matches - and only a David Raya penalty save stopped them from trailing at Sunderland as well.

For large parts of the game against Leeds, they were nowhere near their best but, after going behind in the 55th minute, Riccardo Calafiori and Guimaraes - on his full home debut - secured an important three points.

"It was a great game of football. Leeds were brilliant for one hour." said Ally McCoist on TNT Sports.

"Mikel Arteta made changes when he needed to and the substitutions gave Arsenal what they needed. That's what champions do. Leeds can hold their heads high."

Coming into the season as defending champions, Arsenal were looking to make a statement signing to make their rivals take notice.

They did not bring in the attacker they wanted but Guimaraes looks like he could be that key arrival to help Arteta's men build on their success.

The 28-year-old midfielder is a 'win-now' signing in the peak years of his career.

He responded well to a disappointing performance in the defeat by Brighton, where he made his full league debut.

The Brazilian international has now scored two goals that have helped his side to valuable points and justified the decision to spend big on Guimaraes, even if the Gunners are inundated with top quality options in midfield.

Arteta said: "He wasn't at that level against Brighton, and this is the level for Arsenal. Every week, every game, every minute, every action, you have to be at that level.

"Today was much better. That's what we have to demand, and this is what I demand to myself. I'm going to demand the same with the players, because if we do that, he will raise the standards and we will be a better team."

Guimaraes was the first player to score twice from the bench this season and both goals have been from outside the box.

Arsenal won the league last season in part because of their excellent defence.

The Gunners conceded the fewest goals in the league but have already conceded five in six games.

The partnership of Gabriel Magalhaes and William Saliba is one of the best in the world and Arsenal look to be missing the injured Frenchman's calmness.

Ezri Konsa was brought in from Aston Villa for £55m and, despite his quality, is still getting used to his new surroundings.

It is unclear how serious Hincapie's injury is, although he was seen clutching his right ankle as he was carried off by goalkeeper Illan Meslier.

He signed for the club on a permanent deal this summer, having initially joined on loan from Bayer Leverkusen last season.

Hincapie has suffered from muscular issues this term and now faces an anxious wait to discover whether he requires another spell on the sidelines.

Left-back Calafiori, though, has proved integral to Arsenal's attacking threat. His equaliser against Leeds was his first league strike this term but no defender has been involved in more Premier League goals than the Italian (one goal, two assists).

"The last time we put our shirts on, something was missing." added Arteta.

"And we need to be very conscious of that. From being exceptional and being the champions to being extremely average, like in that game, is a really thin line.

"So if you don't want it more than the opponent, you are not able to cope emotionally with certain situations, you're going to suffer.

"And we all suffered and we didn't enjoy that game, but then you have to learn the lesson and we certainly done that.

"We speak about it and you could sense that there was something in those tummies."

Arteta made some big calls when naming his starting XI.

He opted to start with German Kai Havertz up front despite the forward returning early from international duty after picking up a hamstring issue, leaving Viktor Gyokeres on the bench again.

Gyokeres had scored four goals, registering in every match for Sweden, in the last international break, but looks to have work to do to win his manager round.

The 28-year-old has yet to start a Premier League game and in his cameos this season has looked far from the level required as a striker who could fire Arsenal to back-to-back titles.

The forward line did not click against Leeds and, with Havertz looking like he lacked match sharpness, thoughts turned towards whether Arsenal missing out on an elite attacker in the summer would haunt them.

Winger Christos Tzolis, who has shone at times this season following his summer arrival, suffered a hamstring issue with Greece and, with Eberechi Eze out of form, Arteta used Noni Madueke on the left wing.

Madueke was left out of the last England squad due to a lack of minutes with Arsenal but, after "being the best player in training for the last 10 days" according to Arteta, now could be the chance for him to prove his worth.

Loud blast at Riyadh airport as travelers evacuated and airlines cancel flights
description:
Many people were wounded in a blast at Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, according ‌to two eyewitnesses and two people briefed on the matter, and travellers ‌were evacuated from parts of the facility. 
   One of the eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and then ​seeing multiple people lying injured on the ground inside the airport. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport. 
   The Saudi government's media office and the Saudi civil aviation authority did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the ‌incident. 
   Saturday's incident comes amid an ⁠escalation of missile strikes by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on the kingdom.
fullText:
RIYADH, Oct 10 (Reuters) - Many people were wounded in a blast at Riyadh's international airport on Saturday, according ‌to two eyewitnesses and two people briefed on the matter, and travellers ‌were evacuated from parts of the facility.

One of the eyewitnesses reported seeing an explosion and then ​seeing multiple people lying injured on the ground inside the airport. More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport.

The Saudi government's media office and the Saudi civil aviation authority did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the ‌incident.

Saturday's incident comes amid an ⁠escalation of missile strikes by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on the kingdom. The airport has already been attacked twice this week, leaving ⁠four people dead and others wounded, and badly damaging an aircraft.

Flight-tracking site flightradar24 showed all flights to Riyadh had either been diverted or cancelled, with only a helicopter ​hovering over ​the airport at one point.

The airport urged ​passengers to contact their airlines ‌directly and check their flight status before heading there.

Kuwait Airways said it had cancelled flights to and from the Saudi capital due to what it described as the closure of Riyadh airport because of the "security situation" there.

Etihad Airways and Qatar Airways earlier cancelled multiple flights between their respective hubs and Riyadh, with some cancellations ‌extending into Monday.

Houthi attacks on Thursday and earlier ​in the week had already prompted a number ​of carriers to suspend or ​cancel services to the Saudi capital, shortly before Riyadh is ‌due to host major energy and investment ​conferences.

Organisers of those ​conferences said on Saturday they would go ahead as planned, and they sought to reassure attendees of their security.

The Houthis have said airliners should avoid ​Saudi airspace, declaring it ‌a zone of military operations after the Saudi-backed Yemeni government launched an ​offensive against the group earlier this month.

title: Army officials caught off guard by Hegseth's plan to livestream execution
description:
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth looks on as President Donald Trump speaks to the news media, on the South Lawn of the White House on October 6. - Finn Gomez/Getty Images
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s announcement that the execution of the convicted Fort Hood mass shooter would be shown in public caught people across the Pentagon and the Army off guard, three sources familiar with the matter told CNN.
Hegseth made the announcement in an interview with far-right podcaster Jack Posobiec aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Wednesday, which he’d visited to give a speech to the crew welcoming them home from their deployment to the Middle East.
“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said during the interview.
That comment was the first time many in the Army and Pentagon heard about the idea of a firing squad’s execution of Nidal Hasan in Texas being made public, and there were immediately questions about what “public” would mean.
fullText:
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s announcement that the execution of the convicted Fort Hood mass shooter would be shown in public caught people across the Pentagon and the Army off guard, three sources familiar with the matter told CNN.

Hegseth made the announcement in an interview with far-right podcaster Jack Posobiec aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln on Wednesday, which he’d visited to give a speech to the crew welcoming them home from their deployment to the Middle East.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said during the interview.

That comment was the first time many in the Army and Pentagon heard about the idea of a firing squad’s execution of Nidal Hasan in Texas being made public, and there were immediately questions about what “public” would mean. There are Army regulations about who can watch a military execution, including family of the prisoner and of the victims, media representatives and a chaplain.

But it was decided by Hegseth, acting Army Secretary Adam Telle, and Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell and his staff that “public” would mean it would be livestreamed, one source familiar said. The Pentagon then confirmed as much to the media, saying in a statement, “The Secretary is correct. It will be livestreamed. Details will follow.”

The Army referred questions to the Pentagon, and a Pentagon spokesperson said they had nothing to add beyond Thursday’s confirmation that it would be live-streamed.

The idea has shocked many service members and veterans and provoked a bipartisan backlash. Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on Friday that the livestream could ultimately go forward, saying he didn’t know “if that’s actually going to happen,” but said if it was, “I’m not going to be watching it.”

“It takes away everything America stands for when we do public executions,” one Army officer with multiple deployments to the Middle East told CNN. “The generational harm caused by allowing troops in uniform to stand in front of a man in a wheelchair and watch him get shot to death is irreparable.”

President Donald Trump welcomed the idea of a firing squad execution on Friday.

“We’re giving a man the death penalty who killed 14 soldiers a couple of years ago. Death penalty through firing squad — and he deserves it,” the president said to applause during a White House event honoring Christopher Columbus.

Trump told CNN-affiliate WSTM on Friday he was not involved in the decision to livestream the execution, adding, “but I understand the decision.”

Asked about the livestream by reporters at the White House earlier Friday, the president said his administration would make a determination about it, while reiterating that Hasan will be killed and “through firing squad.” He didn’t answer when a reporter asked if he’d watch the livestream.

FCC chair Brendan Carr told CNBC’s “Squawk on the Street” it was his understanding that the execution would not be shown on broadcast TV – but that he would defer to Hegseth and “his decisions on how to move forward.”

Many of the details around the livestream have yet to be finalized, and multiple sources told CNN that officials have been working to find answers since it was announced. A second source familiar told CNN that great care is being taken to determine which soldiers would fire on Hasan, taking into consideration the potential psychological impacts of doing so. A specific unit has been selected to carry out the execution, the source said.

Showing the execution on a livestream presents more challenges, the source said, including any effort to obscure from the public the identities of the soldiers involved. It’s also unclear where and if the execution will be streamed beyond the Pentagon’s own website. Broadcasters and social media platforms have strict restrictions on violent and disturbing content.

The first source familiar said there are still questions about whether soldiers can decline to participate, given that the military is moving forward with this as a legal order.

The second source familiar echoed the same, saying while many soldiers may have “taken a life in combat,” this is a very different situation.

“This is a situation where the guy has done a very bad thing and hurt a lot of people, years removed,” the second source said. “He’s going to be immobile and put up like a target.”

title: Verstappen wins Singapore sprint after Russell meets disaster
description: Max Verstappen won a rain-delayed sprint race at the Singapore Formula One Grand on Saturday while George Russell's small title ambitions took another hit when he crashed out in leading position early on. Mercedes driver Russell beat pole sitter Verstappen of Red Bull for first place at the start which was delayed by half an hour because of a heavy downpour shortly before the original start time.
fullText:
Max Verstappen won a rain-delayed sprint race at the Singapore Formula One Grand on Saturday while George Russell's small title ambitions took another hit when he crashed out in leading position early on.

Mercedes driver Russell beat pole sitter Verstappen of Red Bull for first place at the start which was delayed by half an hour because of a heavy downpour shortly before the original start time.

But Russell lost control on a still wet curb in lap two and hit the pit wall, opening the door for Verstappen to top the podium again a week after his first regular GP win of the season in Malaysia.

Verstappen won from Ferrari pair of Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli was gifted fourth place when both McLarens ahead of him spun in a last lap-duel when champion Lando Norris made contact with team-mate Oscar Piastri. Norris limped home in eighth while Piastri had to retire.

Antonelli now leads Russell by 89 points, with 175 points still on offer in the remaining seven races.

Qualifying is scheduled for later Saturday and the full Singapore race is on Sunday.

"The start was horrendous again, that is definitely something we need to improve on, because if we have something like that tomorrow, that is your race over if anything crazy happens. Not ideal and then we got lucky with what happened with George," Verstappen said.

"After that you just want to keep it calm and under control because you know you can't pass around here, especially in a condition like this, with the intermediates.

"Of course happy to win here in the sprint. But I also know that I want to win tomorrow, not today."

All drivers started on intermediate tyres and there were two formation laps before the standing start in which Russell shot past Verstappen at the start and Hamilton rose from sixth to third.

But Russell's joy was short-lived as he lost control on a wet curb in the last turn of lap two and spun into the pit wall.

It was another setback in a season more and more turning into one to forget, a week after he had to retire late in Malaysia with a power unit problem. In addition, he will be at the back of the grid on Sunday owing to using too many power unit components.

"Sorry, sorry, sorry," Russell said via team radio before saying later that an error of judgement by him caused the crash.

Russell's crash brought out the safety car as the Cadillac of Sergio Perez also made heavy contact with Lance Stroll's Aston Martin.

Verstappen handily won the restart from Hamilton and never looked back. Further back, Antonelli took no risks and eventually earned two more points than he had hoped for when the McLarens hit each other.

As of now, second-choice goalkeeper Gollini is expected to start between the sticks for the Giallorossi in Como.

title: Manchester City & Premier League held settlement talks
description: Manchester City held settlement talks with the Premier League in the early stages of the financial breach case against them, according to reports.Photo by Carl Recine/Getty ImagesGiles Turner and Lucc...
fullText:
Giles Turner and Lucca de Paoli report for Bloomberg UK that Manchester City held early-stage settlement talks with the Premier League, prior to the revelation that City had been found guilty of over 100 breaches of the English top-flight's regulations.

The talks quickly fell apart, but if they had reached an agreement, it would reportedly have helped to mitigate the massive sanctions the club now face. Though it would never have resolved the case completely.

Both Manchester City and the Premier League declined to comment on the reports.

Bloomberg add that rival clubs like Arsenal and Liverpool would likely have vehemently opposed a settlement anyway, so perhaps it's for the best that talks broke down.

It's strange that City ever took part in the conversations to begin with, as they've repeatedly claimed they have "irrefutable evidence" of their innocence.

If their evidence cannot possibly be refuted, it's unclear why they would need to reach a settlement, as they could simply have provided that evidence and been found not guilty.

Of course, it's strange that City are still claiming to have that irrefutable evidence anyway. The evidence has already been refuted by the independent commission, unless the club chose not to provide said evidence at their hearing.

From an Arsenal fan perspective, it's certainly positive that City and the Premier League aren't settling. There's no desire among rival fans to see a nice compromise, the biggest case of breaches in Premier League history merits the biggest punishment.

title: 5 things to know about the Commanders' Week 5 opponents
description: We go Behind Enemy Lines to learn more about the 2026 Giants.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders (1-3) return home to Northwest Stadium on Sunday to host the first-place New York Giants (3-1). Yes, you read that correctly; the Giants enter Week 5 atop the NFC East.

This is a huge game for Washington. A loss would not only drop the Commanders to 1-4, but also to 0-3 in the division. Even in what looks like a down year for the NFC East, a 0-3 start would put Washington in an almost impossible position.

The Commanders and Giants are dealing with several high-profile injuries. While the Commanders get star quarterback Jayden Daniels back for this game, wide receiver Stefon Diggs is one of six players ruled out. Washington's top receiver, Terry McLaurin, is questionable with a hamstring injury. The Commanders' offensive line gets right guard Sam Cosmi back for this one.

How good are the 2026 New York Giants under new head coach John Harbaugh? To find out, we spoke with Giants Wire managing editor Dan Benton to get the lowdown.

DB: The way the NFC East is shaping up, I believe so. But that says more about the division than it does about the Giants. A traditionally tough division looks like a mess this season, and that just happens to coincide with the Giants finally taking that first step out of their most recent rebuild. There have been notable improvements under John Harbaugh, but they're still a year away from being legitimate playoff contenders and two years away from being potential Super Bowl contenders. Luckily for the Giants, a bad division will help get them used to winning after over a decade of losing.

DB: Not exactly. And how could anyone be? We all know who Jameis Winston is. "The Jameis Winston" experience is a very real thing, and I think that adds uncertainty to any team he's ever started for. The good news? He can light up the scoreboard at times, and fans always know he has that potential in his back pocket. You just never know what you're going to get from Jameis from week to week, game to game, and play to play.

DB: The Giants actually have quite a few strengths offensively, from improved line play to talented wide receivers and big running backs who bully opponents. Then there are the tight ends, Isaiah Likely and Theo Johnson, who create mismatches all over the field. The biggest weakness, outside the unpredictability of Winston, is ball control. The Giants' backs have coughed it up entirely too many times this season, and it's becoming obvious it's not a flash-in-the-pan issue.

DB: They're a mixed bag. They are truly a bend but do not break defense through four weeks, and while I expect that to settle down, they have some issues. Teams are getting the ball out very quickly against them, which has neutralized their pass rush. They're still getting to the quarterback, but they're struggling to bring them down to get into longer down-and-distance situations. That puts incredible strain on the secondary, which is primarily man coverage under Dennard Wilson. Thus far, they've been able to survive and navigate those waters, but eventually the dam will break (as we saw against the Los Angeles Rams).

DB: They've been extremely impressive. I think Arvell Reese is a legitimate Defensive Rookie of the Year candidate; Francis Mauigoa has been especially strong as a run blocker; Malachi Fields is mature and professional; and Jake Kelly has been an under-the-radar special teams contributor. The one struggling thus far is cornerback Colton Hood. His introduction to the NFL has not been kind.

DB: I'm torn on this one. The Commanders have had the Giants' number over the past four meetings, and Jayden Daniels typically plays them well. However, he's coming off an injury, and the game will be played in sloppy, rainy conditions -- the third week in a row for New York. There's also the John Harbaugh factor, which we've seen in back-to-back weeks with last-second wins. I don't think the Giants can threepeat that result, but I'll side with the changing tide and believe they won't have to. Giants 27, Commanders 17.

title: A €30m steal, Liverpool have green light to sign elite talent
description: Liverpool have got the chance to snap up one of the world's most exciting young talents. A €30m steal, no less.Liverpool are on a mission to find elite young talent. Some have been locked down alrea...
fullText:
Liverpool have got the chance to snap up one of the world's most exciting young talents. A €30m steal, no less.

Liverpool are on a mission to find elite young talent. Some have been locked down already, with the likes of Jeremy Jacquet thriving in the first-team team right and looking set for a long, exciting future.

Then there are others who have agreed to join down the line. Liverpool struck two deals a year in advance this summer, and they're currently looking to find more.

It's quite clearly a major plan at Anfield right now. They want to build their next first-team - or at least the core of it - a long time in advance and that means paying fairly large sums on what are essentially gambles.

There's rightly a lot of hype around Gilberto Mora right now. The 17-year-old was the youngest player at the summer's World Cup and then he grabbed his first international goal during this break.

Mora is expected to leave Tijuana shortly. In fact, the only reason he's stuck around there is because he can't move before turning 18 but January represents a golden opportunity for him to depart.

Liverpool's long-standing interest will put them in a strong position to get him and it seems Tijuana are ready to sell. Journalist Cesar Luis Merlo reports on his YouTube channel that Mora can move for between €20m and €30m next year.

That may well be a steal. Mora is playing well beyond his years and does look like the kind of player who develops steadily and consistently - he's not dependent on pace, has strong technique, and is already capable of playing against elite professionals.

That green light at €30m looks like a fantastic deal, really. Liverpool are in the mix and have been for months - now's their opportunity to snap him up.

So keep an eye on this one. Mora may well arrive as one of the most exciting prospects in years.

title: Mbappe, Trent start in a 4-2-3-1: How Real Madrid can line up against Villarreal
description: Following a three-week hiatus due to the international break, Real Madrid are back in action later tonight as they host Villarreal in La Liga at the Santiago Bernabeu.The Spanish capital giants find t...
fullText:
Following a three-week hiatus due to the international break, Real Madrid are back in action later tonight as they host Villarreal in La Liga at the Santiago Bernabeu.

The Spanish capital giants find themselves under intense pressure, having succumbed to a defeat to Atletico Madrid in the derby right before the break.

The result has left Jose Mourinho & co. trailing arch-rivals FC Barcelona by six points, with the Catalans sitting comfortably at the top of the table, having won all of their matches so far.

Therefore, Real Madrid have no margin for error as they take on Villarreal, knowing that another slip-up could put further distance between themselves and Hansi Flick's men.

The good news for Mourinho is that he has recovered some of his injured stars as Kylian Mbappe and Ibrahima Konate are back to fitness after returning from international duty with minor injuries.

Furthermore, Federico Valverde, who suffered an injury in the derby, has also recovered and been included in the squad list to face the Yellow Submarine.

However, Eder Militao remains unavailable, along with Ferland Mendy, Raul Asencio, and Rodrygo Goes. Dean Huijsen also misses out through suspension.

Here's how Real Madrid could take the field at the Santiago Bernabeu against Villarreal.

Thibaut Courtois will man the goal as usual for Real Madrid and will be hoping to keep a clean sheet, having not managed a single one in their last five matches.

Fit to start. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Meanwhile, in defence, Ibrahima Konate is expected to start from the get-go despite only recently recovering from a knock, given the absences in defence. Partnering the summer signing will be veteran defender Antonio Rudiger.

There is intense competition at right-back, but Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to edge out Denzel Dumfries for the starting spot, considering that he had a lighter workload during the international break compared to the Dutchman.

On the opposite side, Alvaro Carreras is expected to get the nod ahead of summer signing Marc Cucurella, who was heavily involved with Spain during the international window.

Mourinho has yet to figure out his best midfield combination as Real Madrid look for ways to control and dictate matches.

While Fede Valverde has started each of Real Madrid's games so far, he is only returning from a considerably serious ankle injury and might not be risked from the start.

This should pave the way for veteran star Bernardo Silva to start in the centre of the park, from where he will hope to provide the team with creativity and vision.

Bernardo Silva to get a starting berth? (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images)

Partnering the Portuguese international will be Aurelien Tchouameni, who has worked hard during the international break to regain his peak fitness and rhythm.

Eduardo Camavinga, who impressed for France under Zinedine Zidane, will have minutes off the bench.

Jude Bellingham has been Real Madrid's best player so far this season and will line up as the attacking midfielder.

There has been a lot of talk surrounding Vinicius Jr and his poor form and the possibility that Mourinho could decide to bench the Brazilian. However, for now, the superstar winger is expected to start against Villarreal on the left flank.

On the right side of the attack, Arda Guler is expected to get the nod from the get-go, meaning marquee summer signing Yan Diomande will have to wait for his opportunity.

Kylian Mbappe, despite only recently recovering from an injury, will be leading the line for Real Madrid tonight at the Santiago Bernabeu.

title: Barcelona president hits out at Real Madrid: ‘They talk about other topics to divert attention’
description: Relations between Real Madrid and Barcelona are at an all-time low, and it is clear that Los Blancos are looking to discredit Barcelona by any and every means possible at this point.With Barcelona enj...
fullText:
Relations between Real Madrid and Barcelona are at an all-time low, and it is clear that Los Blancos are looking to discredit Barcelona by any and every means possible at this point.

With Barcelona enjoying a stunning start to the season and Real Madrid struggling to keep up, they have resorted to a new low of going to UEFA to bring up the Negreira scandal once more.

After all, it only serves as a means to shift the spotlight away from them and onto a fabricated story, which, at this point, has repeatedly been proven false.

Barcelona president Joan Laporta spoke to the media earlier today in a detailed discussion where he addressed the topic of Real Madrid and how the club is intentionally running a smear campaign against Barcelona to cover up their own shortcomings.

Perez and Co. have handled matters poorly in recent times. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

"In Madrid they talk about other topics to divert attention. Barça is in a sweet moment, we are enjoying football, a very beautiful moment in our history, an international recognition," he began.

"We have nine players in the squad who have been world champions, we have a team that falls in love, with players in different positions who are references in the world of soccer. From Madrid they try to minimize all this," he added.

Elaborating on the Negreira case, which Real Madrid are again attempting to bring back to the spotlight, Laporta said,

"The Negreira Case, I will not stop saying it, they tried to condemn us before judging us, when it is being shown that there was nothing they accused of. I fully trust in Barça's acquittal."

"Those who are constantly talking about it, try to harm and tarnish the image of Barça, because they will have to rectify. There will be time to talk about this when we have the sentence," he added.

Laporta hit out at Real Madrid unforgivingly. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

He then lashed out at Real Madrid, making it clear to the world that what was being orchestrated was nothing but a smear campaign.

"They extend the summary as much as they can to keep the flame alive, but it doesn't go anywhere. It's just to discredit Barça."

Finally, the Barcelona president highlighted how the current situation reflected very poorly on Real Madrid themselves, contrary to the objective they are seemingly trying to achieve.

"They do it to harm football, because they are against everything. They go to UEFA, They go to the Euroleague and they are against everything and everyone.

"It says a lot about a club that is losing prestige, recognition and credibility at the national and international level."

"It's clear, I was at the EFC conference and they didn't even have representation. They have a very arrogant attitude, very arrogant, very arrogant. They will know what they are doing, but it is leading them to have a huge lack of credibility," he added.

Elaborating on how Real Madrid's decisions and actions serve to benefit no single party, Laporta concluded, saying,

"Just like with the Euroleague, in the end they finish everyone, but along the way they only put obstacles to what the rest of us want to do. They should make self-criticism about this because it seems inappropriate to me."

title: Fantasy football analyst believes Jaguars TE is a must-sit in Week 5
description: Should you start or sit Jacksonville Jaguars TE Brenton Strange in Week 5?
fullText:
Fantasy football analyst Matt Okada from NFL.com believes that Jacksonville Jaguars' tight end Brenton Strange should be on your bench in Week 5.

As Okada notes, last week was a good outing for Strange, but the Eagles will present a more difficult tight end matchup.

"Strange was excellent in Week 4, with seven catches for 95 yards ... but that was a matchup against the TE-friendly Bengals. He had seven catches total in the three games prior," wrote Okada. "If you picked him up off waivers, keep him tucked away on your bench for now."

According to CBS Sports, on average this season, opposing tight ends are averaging four receptions and 39 receiving yards against the Eagles. A tight end is yet to score a touchdown.

It would seem that outside of Parker Washington, it's difficult to gauge on a weekly basis how many targets each of the Jaguars' pass-catchers will see. In the Liam Coen offense, the ball gets spread around.

And while blocking doesn't necessarily impact your fantasy football scoreboard, Strange plays an important role in the run game, and his well-rounded skill set opens up the playbook for Coen with all the different hats he can wear.

Through four games, Strange has caught 14 of 18 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown.
