title: Jon Jones ‘leaving doors open’ for fighting future, still in UFC drug-testing pool
description: Jon Jones continues to be drug-tested by UFC
fullText:
Jon Jones is done with fighting. Well, just about done, anyway.

The former UFC heavyweight and light heavyweight champion kept the torch of a comeback dimly lit late Friday evening, taking to Twitter to respond to a fan asking if he plans to fight again. Jones wrote, "More than likely, I won't fight again," but added that he is still in the UFC's drug-testing pool, and that he is "leaving doors open."

More than likely, I won’t fight again, but as of right now I’m still getting drug tested. Leaving doors open, you never know what the future holds. https://t.co/2SV3t9BWou

More than likely, I won't fight again, but as of right now I'm still getting drug tested. Leaving doors open, you never know what the future holds.

According to the UFC's official drug-testing website, the 39-year-old Jones has been tested four times in 2026.

Jones is widely regarded as one of the greatest fighters in MMA history, having held multiple titles at 205 pounds with 11 successful championship defenses in that division from 2011 to 2020. He remains the youngest fighter to ever win a UFC title, having accomplished the feat at the age of 23.

"Bones" added to his impressive résumé in 2023 when he submitted Ciryl Gane to capture a heavyweight title vacated by Francis Ngannou, who departed the UFC to join PFL. He successfully defended the belt against heavyweight legend Stipe Miocic at UFC 309 in what was, to date, the final fight of Jones' career. Jones later retired in June 2025, spoiling a potential matchup with interim champion Tom Aspinall, but soon announced his intentions to fight again when UFC CEO Dana White and President Donald Trump announced the UFC White House event, though Jones was eventually left off of that card.

Jones' legacy is complicated by his numerous outside-of-the cage controversies, including his involvement in a 2015 hit-and-run that resulted in his first light heavyweight title reign ending due to the UFC stripping him of his belt, failed drug tests, and a 2021 arrest for domestic violence (a charge later dropped when Jones pleaded no-contest to a related charge of injuring or tampering with a vehicle).

This past week, Jones has been active on social media, continuing his long-running feud with former UFC fighter Colby Covington, who called Jones a "terrible human being" while criticizing Jones' tutelage of heavyweight prospect Gable Steveson. The two went back-and-forth with Twitter comments, and Jones remained dismissive in his latest response.

Trust me, bud, I’m not the one holding the garage. I literally have zero reason to hate on anyone. God has been unimaginably good to me. I just like reminding Colby that I’m not the man I used to be. And even at my weakest, I’ve always been better than him. I’m everything he… https://t.co/OGfxmG93S9

"I just like reminding Colby that I'm not the man I used to be," Jones said. "And even at my weakest, I've always been better than him. I'm everything he could never be, and I know it kills him inside. You can see it in the passion he has when it comes to me.

"I just want to give him a little more to hate. That's all."

title: Jaxson Dart’s Girlfriend Marissa Ayers Announces Personal Update Amid Giants QB’s Injury Rehab
description: Marissa Ayers, a successful social media influencer and New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart’s girlfriend, is making plans to finally live alone for the first time ever. “I’m going to pick up my keys to my very first apartment, living alone for the first time,” Ayers said in a TikTok video.
fullText:
Marissa Ayers, a successful social media influencer and New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart's girlfriend, is making plans to finally live alone for the first time ever.

"I'm going to pick up my keys to my very first apartment, living alone for the first time," Ayers said in a TikTok video. "This is crazy. Today's finally the day. I've been planning to move to get my own place for well over a year now. I graduated college in May 2025. I've basically been living out of a suitcase since then. I don't know how I've done it for so long, but it was honestly just the era I was in."

While Ayers had been planning to live alone since December 2025, she explained how her plans changed as Dart offered to come on several trips with her during the offseason.

"He was like, 'You want to come to California?' I was like, 'Yeah.' 'You want to go to Hawaii?' 'Let's go.' We just wanted to do everything together. I had the flexibility to do so because I worked from my phone, so it was like, why not? Like, let's just go, let's have fun," Ayers continued.

While Jaxson Dart focuses on his recovery, his support system remains front and center. 

Ayers had noted yet another achievement in September. She secured her first modeling photoshoot gig in New York and shot pictures with Ali Brunson.

Ayers is all set to begin an exciting journey in New York. Her beau Jaxson Dart, however, will unfortunately have to wait out the end of the 2026 season at home.

Dart suffered an MCL tear along with damage to his meniscus and PCL, which occurred in the 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

"He's determined; he's bummed," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said about how Dart was feeling. "The season's not over, but it is for him. We need to be the best Giants we can be."

Ayers was among the ones who commented after the team posted about the injury, reacting with "🙏🏼💔," a short but heartbroken message. While talking about her new plans, she didn't leave Dart out of them.

"I'm kind of just going to slowly start furnishing it and, like, hop over there and do some things each day, but I'm really going to be with Jax a lot because, with his injury, he had surgery this month, and he really needs, like, that extra helping hand," she said. "So I want to be there for him, and I want to take care of him, and that's something that I just feel in my heart. I mean, we take care of each other, and that's just what we do."

Dart has undergone surgery to relieve his problems, which Harbaugh confirmed has "went well."

The quarterback will be out for quite some time, but should the Giants make the postseason, there is a very slight chance Dart could perhaps return.

Now, while Ayers will keep hold of the keys to her new apartment in New York, which she plans to decorate with all of the eclectic art and furniture she can find in the city, she is helping her boyfriend to recover from his injury for now.

title: Serie A Preview: Napoli vs Frosinone – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
description: Stadio Diego Armando Maradona sets the stage for a high-stakes Serie A clash between Napoli and Frosinone. There’s little margin for error for Massimiliano Allegri in Saturday’s fixture, as his fu...
fullText:
Stadio Diego Armando Maradona sets the stage for a high-stakes Serie A clash between Napoli and Frosinone. There's little margin for error for Massimiliano Allegri in Saturday's fixture, as his future at the club hangs by a thread.

Despite taking charge of Napoli in the summer, Allegri has already come under heavy scrutiny. The former Milan and Juventus manager has overseen just two wins in the first five Serie A rounds (D1, L2), and the Partenopei faithful are putting pressure on Aurelio De Laurentiis to relieve him of his duties.

A 1-1 draw at Fiorentina just before September's international break left Napoli six points adrift of table-topping Roma, and there's a feeling that another slip-up here could spell the end of Allegri's tenure in Naples. However, this doesn't look like a simple task for last season's runners-up, with Frosinone set to roll into town in high spirits.

Back to Serie A after a two-year absence, Massimiliano Alvini's men look determined to stay up this time around. After a narrow 1-0 home loss to Juventus on the opening weekend, the visitors have hit the ground running, securing three wins from their last four league outings (D1), including a 2-0 victory over Como before the break.

As a result, they commence this matchday three points clear of their more esteemed hosts.

It's been a complicated start to the 2026/27 season for Napoli. In addition to their domestic struggles, the Partenopei slipped to a 1-0 home loss to Arsenal in their curtain-raising Champions League fixture, as the pressure continues to mount on under-fire Allegri, who's on the brink of an unwanted piece of history.

The 59-year-old could suffer ten league defeats in one calendar year for the first time since 2012, but Napoli's strong record against newly promoted clubs offers the Italian coach a silver lining. Indeed, they've emerged victorious from their last six league encounters against newcomers, a feat they've only eclipsed twice before.

Another triumph could be on the cards here, not least because Napoli have beaten Frosinone in five of their six previous Serie A meetings (D1). However, they'd be wise not to get complacent after failing to win the last two competitive showdowns against this opposition (D1, L1), including a 2-2 draw in their most recent league clash at this stadium.

Even the most optimistic Frosinone fans could not have expected the Canaries to open the season the way they did. Quick to bounce back from a day-one loss to Juventus, Alvini's charges have bested Como, Venezia, and Fiorentina while sharing the spoils with Genoa at the Marassi.

To give Frosinone's high-flying Serie A start further perspective, they've become the first newly promoted side to hit a 10-point landmark after the opening five rounds since 2012/13. As if that's not inspiring enough, the visitors' unbeaten away run in league action now spans more than 12 months (W10, D7).

Another win here, though it'd have to come at long odds, would see Frosinone become the first Serie A newcomer to reach 13 points after the first six matches since Juventus in 2007/08. They can take further confidence from breaking the deadlock in four consecutive league outings as they seek their maiden away win over Napoli in Serie A.

Italian starlet Antonio Vergara has joined Alisson Santos, Alessandro Buongiorno, Mathias Olivera, and Costantino Favasuli on the sidelines and could be unavailable until November. However, Napoli have welcomed Alex Meret, Leonardo Spinazzola, and Scott McTominay, with the latter likely to start on the bench.

On the other hand, Florian Grillitsch remains the most notable absentee in the Frosinone squad. Free-scoring striker Antonio Raimondo is a doubt after picking up a minor injury during the international break. In case Alvini refuses to put his in-form star at risk, Tomas Bobcek could be in line for his first Serie A start.

Napoli (3-4-2-1): Meret; Marin, Rrahmani, Badiashile; Di Lorenzo, Gilmour, Lobotka, Spinazzola; Neres, De Bruyne; Hojlund.

Frosinone (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Bracaglia; Masini, Calo; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Bobcek.

Despite being in far better shape ahead of Saturday's kickoff, Frosinone could be out of their depth here. With key first-team stars returning to the fold, Napoli look all set to bounce back from recent slumps and draw level with their resilient visitors on ten points.

title: ‘Losing prestige, recognition, and credibility’ – Joan Laporta blasts ‘arrogant and overbearing’ Real Madrid
description: Some strong words from the Barcelona president.
fullText:
Joan Laporta has hit out at Real Madrid yet again over the Negreira Case after Los Blancos compiled a dossier and sent it to UEFA.

The Barcelona president says Madrid have "relentlessly and consistently accused us" and added that their fierce rivals are "losing prestige, recognition, and credibility, both nationally and internationally."

"Barça is in a sweet moment, enjoying the club and a very beautiful moment in our history, receiving praise from all sides, but from Madrid they are trying to downplay all of this. In the 'Negreira case' they tried to condemn us before we were even tried, and now that we are being tried, it has been shown that there is nothing to what they accused us of and that this will end with Barça's acquittal," he told reporters.

"They have relentlessly and consistently accused us, trying to discredit and damage Barça's image, but they will have to back down, no matter how much they drag out the investigation to keep the flame alive. They are trying to discredit Barça, but I don't think they are doing it innocently; rather, they want to harm football ."

"You go to any institution and they're against everything. You go to UEFA and the Euroleague and they're against everyone. It's the attitude of a club that is losing prestige, recognition, and credibility, both nationally and internationally."

Laporta also went a step further and spoke about a recent experience at an ECA Assembly meeting.

"They had no representation, displaying a very arrogant, overbearing, and haughty attitude," he said. "They may know what they're doing, but their lack of credibility is enormous. They are always creating obstacles and obstructing progress. They are completely out of place."

fullText:
This certainly isn't how Sandro Wagner imagined the start of his second spell as a head coach. He arrived at Hannover 96 before the international break amid considerable optimism.

So far, the coach has had little to smile about on his debut in Magdeburg today. Quite the opposite: his team treated him to a major defensive lapse right from the start.

Although the visitors started on the front foot and pressed high, it was 1. FC Magdeburg who scored the first goal of the day. Hannover goalkeeper Leo Weinkauf took too long before passing to teammate Franz Roggow under pressure. Roggow also dallied, and his attempted clearance went wrong. Moritz Kwarteng caught him by surprise from behind, stuck out a foot and deflected the ball into the left corner of the net, leaving the keeper with no chance (3rd minute).

Sandro Wagner's time at the Lower Saxony club therefore begins with a slapstick goal and a very early deficit. There is still plenty of time, though, to turn this nightmare start around.

title: Russell Had Power Surge Before Singapore GP Sprint Crash as Antonelli Gets Lucky
description: George Russell got a power surge that led to his crash in F1 Singapore GP from leading the sprint race in wet conditions. The start of the F1 Singapore GP sprint was delayed due to a rain shower just ahead…
fullText:
George Russell got a power surge that led to his crash in F1 Singapore GP from leading the sprint race in wet conditions.

The start of the F1 Singapore GP sprint was delayed due to a rain shower just ahead of the start. When it got going after a few laps behind the safety car, Mercedes' Russell got a better launch to take the lead from pole-sitter Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

He held the lead for a few laps until his crash in the final corner. He touched the white line coming off the last corner and spun into the barrier, coming across it before coming to a halt. Russell apologised multiple times on the radio, as he missed a good chance to score well.

Post-sprint, Russell noted a power surge from the battery which pushed him towards the white line and, after that point, he was just a passenger. "Yeah, I just misjudged it, to be honest," he said to the media. "I came around the corner, I came on the throttle, I got more power than I was expecting from the battery.

"I went a little bit wide, and then I touched the white line and the number one rule in the rain is don't touch the white lines and, yes, a very, very silly mistake. Overly confident. Yeah, just think it's my first crash of the year. It's annoying to happen from that position," summed up Russell.

The Brit was certainly annoyed, considering teammate Andrea Kimi Antonelli lucked to finish fourth after a late collision between the McLaren pair of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri on the final lap. Russell had a good chance to score handy points, which he missed.

He now has a car to be repaired, plus take the power unit penalty to start from the back of the grid. On top of that, Antonelli only extended his points lead. The Italian felt better with the package, even though he ran mostly behind the McLaren pair.

Head up George, we go again for Quali https://t.co/oETnNXP9KJ

— Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team (@MercedesAMGF1) October 10, 2026

Towards the end, he was close to the duo when they collided, which helped him to pick up more points. There is potential in the package, as he feels, even though it has been a head-scratching situation for Mercedes from Malaysia to Singapore.

"Yeah, I mean, we tried some things, and it did feel a little bit better," said Antonelli. "Hopefully, now, I mean, we will make some changes going into qualifying and, hopefully, they will help us a little bit. Because yeah, the window seems very, very small where this package operates.

"But yeah, we saw some good things last night and, hopefully, we can improve some things and extract the potential out of the package, because I truly believe that, yeah, there is potential in this package. So, we will just need to find the right balance and, hopefully, we can improve our pace," summed up Antonelli.

The Italian is stuck with the package for the whole weekend, as deputy team principal Bradley Lord alluded. On Russell, he hopes that the car can be fixed as soon and that he can take part in the main F1 qualifying – even though they know where he will start from anyway.

"I mean, there's never been a qualifying session we are less needing to compete in," joked Lord, speaking to F1 TV. "So, if it can't be fixed, that's okay, because that is where he is starting tomorrow regardless. But we will try and get him out. We think it should be to swap the rear end, right front corner, and hopefully the floor isn't too badly damaged. It didn't look it, but you never know."

title: Funding Pat Fitzgerald's MSU football program priority for Spartans AD
description: Dan Bartholomae promised to add funding to Pat Fitzgerald's Michigan State football program. The new AD knows it is sorely needed after past failures.
fullText:
Dan Bartholomae provided the type of homecoming week message Michigan State football fans wanted to hear.

The Spartans' new athletic director – in a letter sent to alums, students and donors this week – said he intends to get his inherited first-year football coach more money for his program.

Even in the midst of a three-game losing streak. Even with Bartholomae not even two months into his new job. Even after MSU received a $10 million donation from Joe and Julie Serra a week earlier that will help with the massive undertaking of upgrading Spartan Stadium.

"Football must be resourced to be competitive immediately," Bartholmae wrote, "and they will be."

IT'S GAMEDAY: Michigan State football vs Illinois picks: Who gets 1st Big Ten win?

Five games and two athletic directors into his MSU career, Fitzgerald appears to have found a staunch ally in Bartholomae, who after the loss at Notre Dame on Sept. 19 stood inside the media room and confidently declared to a reporter that he felt the Spartans have a strong football coach for the future. And the letter Bartholomae sent on Wednesday, Oct. 7, reaffirmed those private sentiments publicly.

And it started the stopwatch that went on pause this summer with the departure of the AD who hired Fitzgerald, J Batt.

As President Kevin Guskiewicz wavered toward leaving MSU, Kentucky swooped in and hired away Batt on June 15. A little more than a month later, at Big Ten media day in Chicago, Fitzgerald talked to reporters about his program being left in limbo before even playing a game as he tried to figure out the new financial landscape of college sports, calling it "a little pause there."

"Where it needs to go, those are conversations for when we get our next AD on board," he said July 29. "And I've got to live it for a year, honestly."

Guskiewicz ultimately remained at MSU after accepting and then reneging on the presidency at Clemson. On Aug. 17, he hired Bartholomae away from Western Michigan. The two Pittsburgh-area natives have blue-collar backgrounds similar to that of the Chicago-raised Fitzgerald, Cheboygan native hockey coach Adam Nightingale and Upper Peninsula icon Tom Izzo, something the Hall of Fame MSU basketball coach trumpeted Thursday at Big Ten basketball media day in Rosemont, Illinois.

"I think that it's hard to say, especially for some of us that have been there so long, that this time, we got it right. Because we have been through a hell of a 10 years with too many missing parts and too many people leaving and all that stuff," Izzo said. "But I do think this group is gonna hang tight. I think Dan is gonna be here for the long run, Fitz and Adam.

"I'll be here, though, until I die or something."

Izzo's program is preparing to chase his second national championship in his 32nd season, the first in 2000. Nightingale has resurrected MSU's proud hockey tradition and been among the nation's elite the last few years, winning the last three Big Ten regular-season titles but falling short of reaching a Frozen Four for the first time since winning it all in 2007. Both have established revenue sharing rhythms and funding over the past five years since the 2021 Supreme Court ruling allowing athletes to receive name, image and likeness payments.

Fitzgerald, meantime, arrives at the midpoint of his first season against Illinois on Saturday (3:30 p.m., FS1) having endured a significant number of injuries to his depth chart's already-thin top layer, with running back transfer Cam Edwards out for the season and linebacker Jordan Hall having already missed two games with two separate injuries. Beyond the absences of the primary playmakers on both sides of the ball, the Spartans have been battered and bruised over the past three weeks by No. 3 Notre Dame, Nebraska and Wisconsin – three teams with a combined 14-1 record.

"That's just kind of how life works. It's trials, it's tribulations," Fitzgerald said on his weekly radio show Wednesday night. "It's just kind of Relationship 101. And this is our first year as a staff going through it with the guys and learning a lot of new personalities. This is going to be ongoing through this whole year. It'll reset in January – hopefully with not 62 new guys and a whole new staff. And a whole new support staff. … Everybody will have lived it.

"And it's not an excuse for our performance currently. It's just the storm we're in. You know what? You can have the storm impact you or you can be the storm. We're somewhere in the middle right now."

That physical toll has fueled an inability to generate big gains and prevent sacks on offense and a failure to stop explosive plays on defense. But a day after talking "his favorite sport" with NFL Network's "Good Morning Football" show, Izzo was immediately asked about the oblong ball and Fitzgerald during his media day availibility.

And he delivered a full-throated endorsement.

"I don't need to be Pat's PR guy, but I love Pat," Izzo said Thursday. "I mean, there's fits for places. I think I was a fit for East Lansing myself. And I think we've had some good coaches – some have made it, some haven't. But some fit the place. And he fits the place. He's got energy galore. He's a tough blue-collar guy, and that's what he wants to be and that's what he is.

"I think you're gonna see Pat Fitzgerald – you know, we've struggled a little bit lately – but he's gonna get it done there. I have no ifs, ands or buts about that. And being the big football fan I am, I hope he gets it."

To get it done, Fitzgerald and Bartholomae also must get it right with funding after five years of stops and starts in the NIL sphere. MSU is on its fourth athletic director and fourth football coach since Mark Hollis resigned in 2018 and Mark Dantonio retired in 2020.

All of them pledged but failed to bridge the gap from the Spartans' success under Dantonio in the 2010s into the new era of college sports with promises of elite recruits, new revenue streams and increased donations from boosters and sponsors.

"Providing those resources as we build towards the future is my primary focus every day," Bartholomae wrote. "This includes resources for roster development AND other football priorities such as Spartan Stadium renovations. We can't just pick one – they both must be addressed.

"Prioritizing football success still allows the department to resource and support other programs. Comprehensive investment in football will ultimately benefit everyone invested in MSU Athletics. Clear, well-placed priorities create additional opportunities for department-wide success."

Along with his praise for Fitzgerald, Izzo also gave a hearty endorsement for the hardy Bartholomae.

"I think Dan's been good. I think it's another fit," Izzo said. "I mean, when you say that, right when you say that, you're insulting somebody else, and I'm not insulting anybody else. But I think right now, we've got guys that, I keep using the word blue-collar, because that's what I think we are – lunch-bucket guys. Myself, Adam our hockey coach, who is unbelievable.

"I really love what Fitz is doing. And I think Dan brings to the table, he's got energy, he's built it at a smaller level."

The challenge to chart a course for the next five years for Fitzgerald and Bartholomae is much bigger now than it was anywhere else they have been before.

title: Stephen A. Smith announces the good and bad about LeBron James winning a fifth ring with 76ers
description: Stephen A. Smith has high expectations for LeBron James following his move to the Philadelphia 76ers over the summer.
fullText:
Stephen A. Smith has high expectations for LeBron James following his move to the Philadelphia 76ers over the summer.

LeBron's move was perhaps a surprise to some, given the 76ers, at least in recent times, have struggled to reach the NBA Finals.

However, Stephen A. Smith is confident that the 76ers will be able to win James his fifth NBA championship.

In a clip shared by Legion Hoops on X, Smith stated that the 'good news' is LeBron will get another championship in Philadelphia.

He said: "This season or next season, the Philadelphia 76ers are gonna win LeBron James his fifth NBA championship. That's the good news."

But Smith followed that up by explaining the 'bad', pointing out that he still won't have six championships and LeBron is only the second-greatest of all time behind Michael Jordan.

He continued: "Here's the bad: It still ain't six, baby. This man is the second-greatest player of all time. He is not the GOAT.

"He is the second-greatest player of all time. OK, number two behind a six-time champion, a 10-time scoring champion, a nine-time All-NBA First Team defensive player, the greatest closer in NBA history, who is Michael Jeffrey Jordan."

LeBron made his preseason debut for the 76ers earlier this week, scoring 10 points in 18 minutes against the Brooklyn Nets.

Meanwhile, he is expected to make his proper NBA debut for Philadelphia on October 20 in a week one meeting against the New York Knicks.

title: President Donald Trump makes Georgia vs. Alabama game decision as Hurricane Isaias approaches
description: No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama, both unbeaten, remained on schedule as of Friday for a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff Saturday at Bryant-Denny Stadium, with Hurricane Isaias bearing down on the Gulf Coast.
fullText:
No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama, both unbeaten, remained on schedule as of Friday for a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff Saturday at Bryant-Denny Stadium, with Hurricane Isaias bearing down on the Gulf Coast. Isaias, the first hurricane of the Atlantic season, formed as a tropical storm early Wednesday off eastern Mexico. It strengthened to a Category 3 on Friday and was projected to make landfall near the Alabama-Florida border that evening before moving north and east toward the Carolinas.

Alabama announced on Thursday that it had barred tailgating until 1 p.m. ET and banned tents, and ESPN's College GameDay moved its Saturday morning broadcast inside Coleman Coliseum. The most high-profile guest expected in Tuscaloosa is now out as well.

President Donald Trump announced on Friday afternoon that he would no longer attend. "Based on the fact that a huge Hurricane/Storm is coming, it is important to have our wonderful First Responders, Law Enforcement, and others, focused on that Storm, and in no way be thinking about the safety, or presence, of the President of the United States, ME!" Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"I will be visiting both of those teams at a later date," he added in the post. He also said he hoped the game would go on as planned, and he kept a rally in Clarksville, Tennessee, on his schedule. The original plan had him flying to Tuscaloosa after that afternoon rally.

On Wednesday, asked if the storm could change his plans, Trump had sounded set on going.

"Well, hurricane and football? I love Alabama. I gotta go to the game. It'd be awfully hard," Trump said.

Alabama, Florida and Georgia declared states of emergency as the forecast hardened, and National Guard members were deployed to areas in the projected path.

NEW: President Donald Trump will no longer attend the Georgia vs. Alabama game due to Hurricane Isaias, @JournoRyan reports.

Tuscaloosa sits under a tropical storm warning but outside the projected path of the eye. Projections had the storm reaching northern Alabama around kickoff, and the early expectation was that the game itself might avoid the worst of it.

College football officials were still discussing the storm's potential impact on Friday.

Trump's visit would have been his 10th college football game as president since 2017. He was in Knoxville in late September for Texas' 20-17 win over Tennessee, which made Saturday his second scheduled college football trip in three weeks. For fans in Tuscaloosa, his absence removes one layer of game-day logistics, since a presidential visit means heavier security and arriving early to clear it.

He was also at Bryant-Denny for the 2024 meeting between these teams, when Alabama built a 28-point lead and held on to win 41-34.

title: Former Bears QB Jim Harbaugh recalls the side of Mike Ditka cameras missed
description: Jim Harbaugh held his Friday news conference with the Chargers hours after the family of Mike Ditka announced that the Hall of Fame coach had died at 86. Ditka coached the 1985 Bears to the only Super Bowl title in franchise history. Harbaugh played quarterback for Ditka in Chicago from 1987 until the Bears fired […] The post Former Bears QB Jim Harbaugh recalls the side of Mike Ditka cameras missed appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Jim Harbaugh held his Friday news conference with the Chargers hours after the family of Mike Ditka announced that the Hall of Fame coach had died at 86. Ditka coached the 1985 Bears to the only Super Bowl title in franchise history. Harbaugh played quarterback for Ditka in Chicago from 1987 until the Bears fired Ditka in 1992, and when the questions turned to his former coach, he answered with a scene from those years that Ditka never made public.

"One time, he had me come into his office," Harbaugh said. "We were talking about the game plan, and he said, 'Hold on a second.' He was writing out checks and signing checks, and I could see that from across the desk. One, and then another, and then another, and then another, and another, and another, until finally I said, 'What are you doing, coach?'"

"He said he had gotten a letter, and it was a stack of letters from people in need," Harbaugh continued. "… He was never one to self-promote that. I just happened to have witnessed it with my own eyes."

In a 1992 game against the Minnesota Vikings, Harbaugh threw an out route that Todd Scott intercepted and returned 35 yards for a touchdown, and television cameras caught Ditka's tirade at his quarterback on the sideline.

That clip has followed both men for more than three decades. Harbaugh had a room full of reporters and an easy laugh within reach on Friday. He gave them the man behind the desk instead, a version of Ditka that never made a highlight reel and that Harbaugh said Ditka himself never mentioned.

Former Bears QB Jim Harbaugh on his former HC Mike Ditka ( @chargers): https://t.co/jGm3d0Ykr5

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 10, 2026

At Big Ten media days in Chicago in 2015, seven months into his tenure at Michigan, Harbaugh pulled a Ditka Bears jersey from under the dais and said he would be proud to wear it. He listed Ditka with his father, Jack Harbaugh, former Michigan coach Bo Schembechler and former Raiders owner Al Davis as the biggest influences on his football life. He had eaten dinner with Ditka at his former coach's Chicago restaurant the night before.

Ditka stayed on that list through everything that came after, including a national title at Michigan and the move to the Chargers.

Harbaugh also said in a statement: "Our heartfelt condolences to Mike's family, his Bears family, and to the countless people he touched from near and afar. It is impossible to think of the history of the NFL without seeing his face and his famous mustache. Sadly, Mike has passed on, but his legend will live forever."

title: After playoff elimination, Liberty players’ silence on coach Chris DeMarco speaks volumes
description: NEW YORK — Breanna Stewart knows not to take the WNBA Finals for granted. It’s a message her former teammate Sue Bird has been carving into her brain since she was a rookie. But what does she do when the franchise she plays for is taking her for granted? Her MVP-caliber season, over in one clean semifinals sweep with an 85-83 loss Friday night to the fourth-seeded Atlanta Dream. So now what?
fullText:
NEW YORK — Breanna Stewart knows not to take the WNBA Finals for granted.

It's a message her former teammate Sue Bird has been carving into her brain since she was a rookie. But what does she do when the franchise she plays for is taking her for granted? Her MVP-caliber season, over in one clean semifinals sweep with an 85-83 loss Friday night to the fourth-seeded Atlanta Dream.

There isn't one answer; there are many, beginning with coach Chris DeMarco's job security. It was notable that Stewart, Jonquel Jones and Sabrina Ionescu — all of whom are under contract through the 2027 season — did not offer their outright support of bringing back DeMarco when given the chance.

The first-year coach said "Yes" when asked if he expects to return, but the answer is much lengthier. Liberty general manager Jonathan Kolb set a precedent when he fired championship-winning coach Sandy Brondello last year after a first-round playoff exit in pursuit of "evolution" and "innovation." In New York, championships are the bar, and if you can't clear it, at the very least, you need to be playing for one.

DeMarco passed the first bar, making it out of the first round as a No. 8 seed after the Liberty survived an injury-riddled season. But in the semifinals, the Liberty looked outmanned and outcoached. The most egregious mistake came in a pivotal Game 2 when DeMarco and his staff were unaware whether New York possessed a reset timeout in overtime. Compounding the error was the fact he left Stewart to answer for it.

But that's what Stewart has done over and over again. She's come up with an answer. Amid multiple injury issues for which DeMarco struggled to find solutions and his failed attempts to establish a team identity, Stewart was the constant.

She finished fifth in MVP voting, but she's the only other candidate besides A'ja Wilson to take her team to the semifinals. Her scoring average was the best it's been since her last MVP season in 2023. Through the Liberty's playoff push, she was their most valuable player, averaging 27 points and 6.8 rebounds through five games. And still, she goes home the same as players on 14 teams without the 2026 title.

"Frustration," Stewart said, describing the season's ending after a peak year. "Because I believe that no matter what cards are dealt, you can always … I can always make something happen. Coming up short with the team really sucks."

The best players in the world don't need their coach, until they do. And this season, Stewart hasn't needed much from DeMarco, but in Game 2 she did. After the semifinal sweep, DeMarco said, "If a few things go differently, we're up 2-1 right now."

Using the reset timeout in Atlanta wouldn't have guaranteed the Liberty head back to New York with the series tied 1-1, but at the very least, it puts arguably the best player in the WNBA in the best possible position to do what she does best — come up with an answer.

Kolb touted his hiring of DeMarco as a thorough process. He prioritized NBA candidates for his third coaching hire since he took the role in 2019, bringing in the former Golden State Warriors assistant coach. But that doesn't necessarily mean Kolb got the best person for the job, nor that all the right people were consulted.

Asked specifically if she weighed in on the hiring of DeMarco, Stewart paused before a Liberty spokesperson interrupted what had previously been a lengthy back and forth between the two-time MVP and a small contingent of media. "You don't have to answer that," he said.

"Do you want me to?" she replied.

She opted not to go deeper. But Stewart should, as the biggest star on the Liberty, have major influence. And yet, it seems she wasn't consulted in a significant way about DeMarco's hiring. Her silence in response to the question spoke volumes, as did Jones and Ionescu's input on DeMarco's future.

Jones dodged a question about if she hopes DeMarco returns.

"Our job is to go out and play good basketball and represent the organization well," she said after her 26-point, 14-rebound, three-block performance in Game 3. "I think we do a good job of focusing on that and, you know, it is what it is."

Ionescu expressed gratitude for DeMarco and the way he "poured into" the team amid a tumultuous season, but she said she doesn't know what his future holds. Stewart told reporters she plans to share her thoughts with management on whether a coaching change is necessary in addition to roster construction.

This brings us to the next answer that is Kolb's to address: Is the big three big enough?

Stewart and Jones were brought to New York in 2023 to join forces with Ionescu and finally bring the Liberty its first WNBA title. They made a trip to the finals in their first season together and then went a step further, making history in 2024. Since then, the Liberty have failed to keep up with a swiftly evolving league. The problem, however, was never Brondello. It was and remains the roster.

Stewart, Jones, Ionescu and forward Leonie Fiebich were the four remaining players from the championship roster this season. DeMarco said teams like the Dream are playing a "different brand of basketball." That brand is faster and more athletic than the Liberty could muster.

Angel Reese outplayed Jones across the three games, while Ionescu struggled to keep up with the Dream's explosive backcourt that was, by the way, missing its leading scorer in Allisha Gray for most of the series. Fiebich didn't have a substantial impact, but she showed spurts on defense.

Stewart was Stewart, the ever-reliable presence.

She didn't want to go into detail on what needs should be addressed in the offseason, but she did emphasize defense.

"Defense wins championships," Stewart said. "And Atlanta, they have three of the top players in the top three in steals. It's no compare-and-contrast because we're the New York Liberty, but we needed to understand our identity a little bit better from the jump."

That summarizes the offseason task at hand for Kolb, figuring out the Liberty's identity. It starts and ends with Stewart, everyone else should be replaceable.

title: Mike Norvell owns ‘extremely poor performance’ as Florida State road skid hits 11
description: Florida State led 14-0 early in the second quarter on Friday night, had the ball at the Louisville 2-yard line and a chance to go up three scores in search of its first road win since 2023. Louisville outscored the Seminoles 44-6 the rest of the way and won 44-20 at L&N Federal Credit Union […] The post Mike Norvell owns ‘extremely poor performance’ as Florida State road skid hits 11 appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Florida State led 14-0 early in the second quarter on Friday night, had the ball at the Louisville 2-yard line and a chance to go up three scores in search of its first road win since 2023.

Louisville outscored the Seminoles 44-6 the rest of the way and won 44-20 at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium. After the fourth-down stop, the Cardinals outgained Florida State 438-190 and finished with 537 total yards.

The loss was Florida State's 11th straight in true road games and 13th straight away from Doak Campbell Stadium.

The Seminoles' last true road win came on Nov. 25, 2023, at Florida, which puts the drought at 1,049 days. Last season, the Seminoles lost all five road games, at Virginia, Stanford, Clemson, NC State and Florida, and this season's first trip ended in a 50-36 loss at Alabama on Sept. 19.

Mike Norvell kept his offense on the field for fourth-and-goal from the 2, and the pass to freshman receiver Jasen Lopez went nowhere. On the next snap, Isaac Brown ran 97 yards for a touchdown, the longest play in Louisville program history.

Brown finished with a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on 17 carries, and Louisville ran for 397 yards as a team. The go-ahead score came on the opening drive of the second half, after a 71-yard kickoff return by Brown and a horse-collar penalty handed Louisville a short field.

"An extremely poor performance by us," Norvell said. "We started the game well. We jumped up 14-0, but too many missed opportunities. Too many times, we didn't show the detail, the discipline, the mental toughness that's necessary on the road."

On the fourth-down call itself, he stood firm. "We felt good about the play, still feel good about the thought process," Norvell said.

Florida State has not won a road game since November 2023 https://t.co/HrbcfIPCL2

— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) October 10, 2026

Florida State had a two-touchdown lead and the ball inside the 5 at Louisville, the kind of start a team trying to break a road skid needs, and it scored six points the rest of the night.

Norvell's own diagnosis pinned the collapse on the road, the same place 11 straight losses point.

Quarterback Ashton Daniels, who threw both Florida State touchdown passes to Micahi Danzy, kept his answer short. "We killed ourselves tonight," Daniels said.

The Seminoles (3-3, 1-2 ACC) play at No. 4 Miami next Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium, the second half of back-to-back road games, and the Hurricanes are 5-0.

"We have a huge game next week," Norvell said.

After Miami, Florida State's remaining road trips are Boston College on Nov. 7 and Pitt on Friday, Nov. 13. That leaves three chances to end a streak that began the weekend after Thanksgiving in 2023.

description: The Trojans will need a balanced offensive attack at Penn State, and Jontez Williams needs to make defining plays in his tenure at USC
fullText:
USC football won last week against Washington, but it was a victory that was far from impressive. Beating Penn State on the road in front of a whiteout would show this USC football team is on the right track.

Here is how Week 6 will play out for the USC Trojans against the Penn State Nittany Lions:

Last season, it was the win against Iowa. This season, it will be a win against Penn State. Jayden Maiava will improve his draft stock and earn some more credibility by taking down Penn State on the road. He will have to be sharp, and it would not hurt if he used his legs. Penn State is in need of a great defensive performance; Maiava will not allow that. Jayden Maiava will lead an effective performance and help the Trojans maintain an impressive record.

King Miller had an impressive run last season as he had a couple of 100-yard performances against Big Ten opponents. This could be his big performance. Lincoln Riley continues to steer away from the run game, even when it is being extremely effective. King Miller will be undeniable this game. Miller will run for 100 yards and a touchdown. While he will be successful in his own right, he will also pave the way for Jayden Maiava to be dangerous in the passing attack. King Miller and Jayden Maiava will be the biggest reasons that the Trojans have offensive success on the road.

Many of the Trojans' wins have been at the hands of their freshmen playing their part. This game will be no different. Luke Wafle will play his part and wreak havoc. The Trojans will have their most productive offensive players be freshmen. Kayden Dixon-Wyatt and Ethan Feaster will both come up clutch for Jayden Maiava.

Robinson, in his first start, made the most of his opportunity, making a ton of plays. He will be extremely valuable to the Trojans' defense moving forward. Week 6 will reflect that. Robinson has earned some more snaps for this game. If he gets another chance, the Trojans know he will show up. Nonetheless, I think he will have another week where he makes a ton of plays, even if he does not get the start.

Jontez Williams has come close before, however, this week he will finally get his first interception at USC. Rocco Becht has thrown 3 interceptions in the past 2 games. He can be reckless at times; this will be a game where Jontez Williams will show off his ball skills. Williams first interception will also end up being a huge momentum swing.

title: Verstappen wins sprint after Russell crashes out
description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen wins an incident-packed sprint race at the Singapore Grand Prix after George Russell crashes out of the lead.
fullText:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen won an incident-packed sprint race at the Singapore Grand Prix after Mercedes driver George Russell crashed out of the lead.

Russell was leading in tricky conditions, with half the track dry and half wet, when he got a little too wide at the final corner at the end of the first lap.

He lost control of his Mercedes, which spun across the track into the inside wall, before bouncing back again to the outside, the rest of the field somehow avoiding him.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton took second having made a superb start from sixth on the grid with team-mate Charles Leclerc third.

A final-lap collision between the McLarens as Lando Norris tried to pass Oscar Piastri at Turn Five promoted Russell's team-mate Kimi Antonelli to fourth place.

In combination with Russell's retirement, that extends the Italian's championship lead to 89 points.

A chaotic race saw the start delayed by 30 minutes by a tropical downpour, and then Verstappen navigating a safety car period following Russell's accident, a restart, and initial pressure from Hamilton to eventually ease away into a comfortable lead.

It was the Dutchman's second Formula 1 win in seven days, after his maiden victory this season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, and the first time he has won in Singapore.

The rain before the start hit only parts of the track. The second sector stayed dry while the first sector, particularly Turns Two and Three, were soaking wet with standing water.

Once the rain abated, the field did two laps behind a safety car to check conditions before racing began with a standing start.

Russell gave himself a golden opportunity to breathe some life into his almost-extinguished title hopes when he beat Verstappen off the line and took the lead into the first corner.

But after leading the first lap, he made a mistake at the final corner.

Russell said: "I just misjudged it, got more power than I was expecting from the battery, got a little wider than I expected and touched the white line. Rule number one in the wet is don't touch the white line. Very silly mistake."

That left Verstappen in front, with Hamilton behind. But after the seven-time champion pursued his erstwhile 2021 title rival for a few laps, the Red Bull began to ease away and was clearly in control, leading Hamilton, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris and Antonelli.

With overtaking difficult around Marina Bay, the field was static until the closing stages.

Leclerc was struggling, and he began to be caught by the McLarens and Antonelli.

Norris had been pressuring Piastri for some laps before the Australian also began to close in on Leclerc, and Antonelli, struggling with oversteer in the early laps, picked up the pace.

On the final lap, Norris made a better exit out of Turn Three and saw an opportunity to try to pass Piastri at Turn Five.

He got the car well enough alongside to make a legitimate passing attempt, but Piastri defended his position robustly, the cars touched, and spun in unison.

Piastri, who hit the barriers, was out on the spot, but Norris was able to keep going, although he fell down to eighth, behind Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson, Haas driver Oliver Bearman and Audi's Nico Hulkenberg.

The stewards will investigate the Norris-Piastri incident after the race.

The delayed start to the sprint means grand prix qualifying will begin 30 minutes later than originally scheduled, at 14:30 BST.

fullText:
Third-year quarterback Bo Nix has been under center for every game this year, helping the Denver Broncos to a 2-2 start ahead of Week 5. He's halfway through an $18.6 million rookie contract that runs through 2027, with a team option for 2028.

While contract negotiations are locked until March 2027, the future of the 2024 12th overall pick remains a hot topic. In fact, analyst Colin Cowherd is already calling for the Broncos to cut their losses with the young quarterback.

On Wednesday, "The Herd" host advised the Broncos against giving Nix a contract extension: "Bo Nix, do not sign him to an extension." According to Cowherd, while Bo Nix had 61 college starts and was expected to be ready to play immediately, "you can have a floor, but it can't be a basement". Cowherd explicitly warns. "Right now, Bo Nix, you cannot sign him to an extension".

Explaining his logic, Cowherd also outlined, "Do not make choices or decisions to validate earlier choices… Bo Nix right now is the problem on the team". On the other side, analyst Nick Wright, the Broncos offense is averaging 3.3 points in the first half with Nix. That said, Nix seems to play much better when the team is losing late in the game.

"In every other circumstance he looks so bad… And lastly on Bo, what I am most interested in is not so much if Colin Cowherd's opinion has changed on him. I wonder if Sean Payton's opinion has changed on him some," Wright said.

Nix is legally ineligible for a contract extension during the 2026 season. Because he is currently in his third year, NFL rules require him to wait until January 2027 to sign a long-term deal.

title: Maresca: Man City players can shut out controversy against Liverpool
description: Enzo Maresca has no concerns about his players' mentality as Manchester City brace themselves for a hostile reception at Liverpool. City travel to Anfield on Sunday for their first match since it was announced the club had been found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations.
fullText:
Enzo Maresca has no concerns about his players' mentality as Manchester City brace themselves for a hostile reception at Liverpool.

City travel to Anfield on Sunday for their first match since it was announced the club had been found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial regulations.

They could face severe punishments, including points deductions or demotion, if their appeal against the verdict fails.

While the situation could be unsettling for the squad, Maresca insists the players remain fully focused.

The Italian said: "For me and the players, we can control just the pitch, the football side. We are focused on that. This what we can control. We cannot control something different.

"Viewing the environment in the last two days, I am not worried at all. The environment of the players is nice.

"In this moment we are top of the league, so the players have all the reasons to be happy and excited.

"It will be a tough game for sure, a tough test, but we need to be ready."

Former manager Pep Guardiola also expressed his backing for City last week, declaring his support for "my club" and insisting "we will get through this together".

The Spaniard is set to return to the Etihad Stadium for the first time since standing down last summer by attending next week's Champions League game against Paris Saint-Germain.

Maresca said: "I spoke with Pep the last time after the Man United game. I know he is coming on Wednesday.

"It is always a pleasure. After 10 years here he can come any time he wants, not just for a game but for a training session, at any moment. It will be nice for him and the fans, for everyone."

Maresca spoke confidently of the club's position at a press conference on Friday, reiterating their belief they will succeed in their appeal.

City maintain they have a "comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence" in support of their case.

He said: "I trust the club because I know the people but I promise you my focus is just about football.

"I am not thinking about different things, first of all because I don't understand much about different things. I just focus on the things I can control and that is the football side."

fullText:
Is Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young an early-season MVP candidate after Week 4? He wrapped up the week with a 32–26 win over the Detroit Lions on Sunday Night Football, throwing for 329 yards and two touchdowns.

Even though Young's amazing season so far has made headlines, national experts still rank Brock Purdy and Patrick Mahomes ahead of him.

While appearing on ESPN's "First Take," former Carolina Panthers defensive tackle Gerald McCoy said, "I believe you guys are grading on a curve because of where Bryce Young was at to where we're seeing him now. I believe that this is a stat. He's playing really good football, but MVP conversation, that's a different level of conversation.

"The Kansas City Chiefs have two people that are in it in their quarterback and (running back) Kenneth Walker III," he added. "Obviously, we know Patrick Mahomes. And then you have what (running back) Bijan Robinson is doing in Atlanta. You have what Brock Purdy is doing with the 49ers. He's playing great football. But we've seen quarterbacks lead the league in passing before and have a lot of yards and not be in the MVP conversation. I think with Bryce Young, we're so happy to see the number one overall pick finally playing well that we might be grading on the curve a little bit. He's playing really good football, but MVP, not just you."

Veteran ESPN analyst Stephen A. Smith weighed in on whether Young is an MVP candidate. "I like Bryce Young a lot," Smith said. "And what I'm really really proud about is that when he was drafted number one because of the way we saw CJ Stroud playing as a rookie… We were like, 'Yo, that I mean, they made a mistake'… before I even think of considering him remotely as an MVP candidate, Carolina's going to have to show me they could be better than the .500 football team. You won a division last year at 8 and 0.

"This is a respectable football team that's moving forward, and they deserve a lot of credit," he added. "But when you start talking MVP, I need to see you a few games above .500. Is that too much? I don't think so."

Is Bryce Young an MVP candidate?@Geraldini93 and @stephenasmith weigh in pic.twitter.com/bq9jWuVgpE

— First Take (@FirstTake) October 8, 2026

Young is putting up elite numbers right now. He ranks right near the top of the league in QBR, deep passing yards with 321, passing first downs at 63, and a 7.8 yards-per-attempt average. Through four games, he is leading the NFL with 1,268 passing yards, 9 touchdowns, and 2 interceptions, carrying a 100.0 passer rating for the 2-2 Panthers.

ESPN's Bill Barnwell MVP evaluation and the weekly NFL QB Index place both quarterbacks above Young. However, Young actually leads all of them in passing yards with 1,268 yards.

title: Barcelona president fires shots at Real Madrid over Negreira case stance: ‘Losing prestige, recognition and credibility’
description: Speaking to the media earlier today, FC Barcelona president Joan Laporta launched a strong criticism of Real Madrid over their position in the Negreira case and their institutional relationships withi...
fullText:
Speaking to the media earlier today, FC Barcelona president Joan Laporta launched a strong criticism of Real Madrid over their position in the Negreira case and their institutional relationships within football and basketball.

It is no secret that both Barcelona and Real Madrid are at total war, with the relationship between the two institutions currently at the lowest it has been in ages.

Real Madrid continue to fight Barça over the Negreira case, with the matters recently getting escalated after the club submitted a large dossier of documents to UEFA to support their accusations and calling for sanctions against the Catalans.

Real Madrid's actions have not gone down well at Barcelona, with Laporta now taking shots at the Spanish capital club.

The Barça president began by praising the club's current form, describing it as a "sweet moment".

"We are enjoying the football and the club, and we are receiving recognition around the world," he started, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo.

"We have nine players in the squad who have been world champions, a team that captures people's imagination, players who are role models, and we are receiving praise from all sides. From Madrid, they are trying to play all of this down," he added.

Laporta has lashed out at Real Madrid. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Laporta then returned to Real Madrid's role in the Negreira case, insisting that Barcelona had been judged in the court of public opinion before the legal process had run its course.

"I will never stop saying that they tried to condemn us before putting us on trial. It is being demonstrated that there was nothing behind the accusations made against us.

"This will end with Barcelona being acquitted. Those who have relentlessly and constantly tried to damage Barcelona's image will have to retract their claims," he declared.

He also criticised the length of the investigation, arguing that the case was being prolonged to keep the controversy alive.

"They are dragging out the proceedings for as long as they can to keep this whole thing alive, but it is going nowhere. It is intended to discredit Barcelona. I do not believe they are doing it innocently," Laporta added.

Barcelona and Real Madrid are at war. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Laporta also addressed Real Madrid's absence from meetings involving European Football Clubs and the EuroLeague, using the issue to question the club's approach to institutional relationships.

"It says a lot about the attitude of a club that is losing prestige, recognition and credibility at national, state and international level. That is clear to see," he firmly stated.

"They are choosing an attitude that is very haughty and very arrogant, and they will have to decide for themselves what they want to do. They should engage in some self-criticism."

The Barcelona president's comments represent another forceful intervention in the increasingly strained relationship between the two Spanish giants, with the Negreira case continuing to fuel tensions between the clubs.

title: ‘Can’t Openly Disrespect the Coach’ — NFL Analyst Highlights Problematic Steelers Angle After Viral Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy On-Field Feud
description: Tensions can run high in the NFL, and the latest example involves Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy. The incident has prompted fans and analysts to question the team’s on-field communication and how the confrontation […] The post ‘Can’t Openly Disrespect the Coach’ — NFL Analyst Highlights Problematic Steelers Angle After Viral Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy O
fullText:
Tensions can run high in the NFL, and the latest example involves Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy.

During Thursday Night Football, the two were involved in a heated exchange that quickly went viral. The incident has prompted fans and analysts to question the team's on-field communication and how the confrontation could affect the Steelers moving forward.

In a recent episode of "Pro Football Talk", analysts Mike Florio and Chris Simms discussed the controversy, focusing on the importance of maintaining respect between players and the coaching staff.

Florio shared his views on how players should work with the coaching staff and emphasized that they must respect the head coach's authority. He said:

"You need to defer to the coach. You need to have players who are involved in partnership with the coaching staff, but they can't take over and they can't openly disrespect the coach. That's the core problem. And we showed that split screen, the look of derision, almost hatred, like the eyes of Aaron Rodgers. And when you're the quarterback who's out there in the middle of the fray and everyone is watching you, got to be very careful the messages you send to the world. Everybody sees it. But wait for the split screen."

It's one thing for the Steelers to be a "player-led" team. It's another thing for the players who are leading the team to not properly respect the coaches. pic.twitter.com/QeNBBAvkud

— PFT Live (@PFT_Live) October 8, 2026

Florio's comments highlighted his concern that a quarterback's public reaction toward a head coach could affect how the rest of the team perceives its leadership. As one of the most visible players on the field, Rodgers has to be mindful of the message his body language sends to teammates and fans.

Simms, however, offered another perspective, suggesting that Rodgers' frustration could stem from his familiarity with the plays and his expectations of the coaching staff.

"I think he knows these plays like the back of his hand. He's expecting the coach to know them too. And, yeah, the coach gives off vibes there of, like, I'm not saying the play the right way and that it's not as detailed as it should be. Even on that last little clip there, he's looking around like, 'Did I say that right?' And Rodgers is going, 'What? That wasn't in the game plan.' So I can see Rodgers get frustrated, but, like you said, he's got to be careful about how far you go."

Simms acknowledged that the head coach must remain the leader, but he also emphasized the importance of veteran players holding one another accountable.

"And, you know, I think what he means too, you're right. The head coach has got to be the man, but there's got to be guys in the locker room that keep everybody held to the standard."

The discussion highlights the balance NFL teams must maintain between respecting coaching authority and encouraging veteran leadership. While Florio stressed that players should not openly undermine their head coach, Simms pointed out that experienced players can also help establish standards and hold teammates accountable.

Ultimately, the incident has sparked a broader conversation about the relationship between a veteran quarterback and his head coach. As the season continues, Pittsburgh will need to ensure that its on-field frustrations do not become a distraction from the team's performance and objectives.

title: WWE Money In The Bank Odds; Who Will Climb The Ladder Of Success?
description: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 odds and predictions for tonight in New Orleans! Get betting favorites, match picks, ladder match winners, and championship predictions.
fullText:
The WWE season is, pardon the phrase, about to make a turn.

The company loves to start its preliminary build towards Wrestlemania about this time every year and Saturday night Money in the Bank is the premium live event to (sort of) kick things off.

Emanating from a bummed out New Orleans (I told you Atlanta would win), MITB has a limited card in terms of matches. Only five have been announced as of this writing and I see nothing being added. Every match has been properly built up and a couple of them could be bangers. If you're willing to place a wager or two, odds on four of the five matches can be seen on BetOnline.

Matches not necessarily in the order WWE will present them:

The champ is a -1500 favorite which tells you everything you need to know. Poor LA Knight has been shoehorned into a position of being fed to Reigns for the second time. He was white hot a couple of years ago and was wasted because Reigns and Cody Rhodes was in the offing. Now, it seems Oba Femi may be the endgame for the OTC somewhere between now and Summer Slam next year.

Knight deserves better. He's cooked Reigns on the mic several times, the crowd pops for him and he can go in the ring. Unfortunately, it looks like he's an occasional main eventer and at his age may never be given a chance to run with the title. Unless of course, he's behind the Royce Keys/945 angle which would make sense. Knight has been battling some incarnation of the bloodline for years. Maybe he's at his breaking point. I don't see it though. This will be a good-to-great match but in the end a showcase for Reigns.

Prediction: Roman Reigns retains by pinfall.

I say give these guys 20 minutes and let them beat the hell out of each other. This should be a fun match. Reed is a hell of a worker and Femi is otherworldly right now. Hopefully this won't turn into an overbooked mess with everyone from The Vision getting involved but we all know better. At -500, it almost assures that it will be. WWE relies too much on the gang warfare for my taste. These guys aren't the Four Horsemen by any stretch.

Reed is a presence on his own. Let him show out against Femi, take the loss and let the potential beat down courtesy of Bron Breakker happen after the bell. Maybe I'm asking for too much. In fact, I know I am. WWE has had Femi lose before, granted it was to Brock Lesnar. I can see it happening again leading to Femi absolutely destroying The Vision once and for all.

Prediction: Femi wins by disqualification.

No odds posted for this match. Possibly because this match may be changed? Seth Rollins on Friday disclosed on the Rich Eisen show that Lynch suffered a "slight" vertebrae fracture a few months back and she's slowly working her way back. She's looked just fine recently so maybe there just aren't odds on this one. It's an absolute toss-up anyway.

Morgan has been doing some of the best character work of her career and is now a main event fixture. Good for her, she deserves it. Lynch is bulletproof and can be counted on to carry any role the company asks of her. Vaquer may be the best wrestler in WWE male or female but her connection to the audience is not quite there. A superstar making performance alongside Morgan and Lynch is just the medicine for any apathy the fans have towards her. If she gets in there and tells the story at the level of her opponents then Vaquer can have a long run with the title.

Prediction: Vaquer retains.
Something to watch: Will Roxanne Perez finally do the unforgivable and cost Morgan the title, intentionally or not? The slow burn with Liv continues.

Is everyone else underwhelmed by this? Legend has impressed, Perez is her usual excellent self, Jayne was a focal point in the women's division not that long ago. Now we're talking. Unlike the women's match this one has some juice. You have Penta fresh off an incredible challenge to the World title. title: How Liverpool’s clash with Manchester City casts awkward new light on Premier League’s big-money model
description: Manchester City’s trip to Anfield will be more highly charged than ever after the revelations of their financial misconduct, but the meeting of the two sides also highlights different attitudes to money at the top of the Premier League
fullText:
Money has long been a theme in meetings of Liverpool against Manchester City. It promised to be once again when the transfer window concluded. This, it seemed, was set to be the first Premier League game to feature five £100m men and both of those who share the British record as the £125m buys. Then, after the independent commission's verdict on City cast some of their past spending in a different light, came what might be deemed less dramatic news: Alexander Isak is injured.

Not for the first time, either, but not seriously, Andoni Iraola believes. So instead there could be two players on each side who cost nine-figure sums: the Liverpool duo of Florian Wirtz, whose £100m fee could rise to £116m, and Bradley Barcola, who joined for £106m, which could go up to £123m, and the City midfield pair of the £116m Elliot Anderson and the £125m Enzo Fernandez.

City were the biggest spenders in the Premier League in 2026. Liverpool had the summer's biggest net spend. And yet a point at Anfield, despite expenditure that has amounted to more than £650m over the last three transfer windows, is that their model has always been self-sustaining, that they only pay what they can afford, whether from player sales or broadcast, commercial and matchday revenue.

Liverpool took the decision to prioritise quality over quantity. They could have a bigger squad, but with fewer high-priced players. And so it is that, in the first game since the ruling City had benefited from more than £900m in disguised funding, the striker they face might be a rookie who cost nothing and who is yet to start a Premier League game, in Lewis Koumas.

Or maybe not, with Iraola considering his options. Hugo Ekitike, the £69m alternative to Isak who flourished last season, is also out. Federico Chiesa, who may have been a failed attempt at Moneyball from former sporting director Richard Hughes, is on the comeback trail but has yet to play this season. Iraola is uncomplaining.

"We also have other players who can cover the positions," he said. "When you coach Liverpool you still have very good players available. I trust the players we have ready to go."

Even the most logical makeshift choice is sidelined: Cody Gakpo, in form this season, with a past experience of leading the line, is also injured. That may mean the line is led by one of the £100m recruits, whether Wirtz as a false nine or Barcola, to use his blistering speed further forward. "I think he can cover the three positions up front," said Iraola. "He's a super-valuable player for us."

The counter-argument is that, quick as the France international is, his finishing can be erratic. He is yet to open his Liverpool account. "I said it [after his] first game, against Atletico Madrid, he missed two or three quite clear chances," said Iraola. "I don't care. Honestly. I care but I want him to see [him] there."

Whether it is the profligate Barcola or the homegrown Koumas operating as the furthest man forward, there is an obvious contrast with their City counterpart, in Erling Haaland. That the Norwegian is the only specialist striker in Enzo Maresca's squad means it is not a department where City possess more depth though Iraola may note that their Plan B in the middle of the attack is Antoine Semenyo, a player who progressed dramatically under his management at Bournemouth. Liverpool liked Semenyo when he became available in January; City had the financial muscle to sign him, even if Barcola ended up costing far more seven months later.

Another link between the clubs is found in the centre of the City defence. Marc Guehi almost joined Liverpool last summer and instead moved to City in January; a bigger salary made the Etihad Stadium an attractive destination for the centre-back. Remarkably, Guehi's time at Crystal Palace and City meant he played in five victories over Liverpool last season, spread across four different competitions; Arne Slot thought his former transfer target should have been sent off when Pep Guardiola's City won at Anfield.

Liverpool were defending champions when they pursued Guehi; when he joined City, he may have felt himself likelier to win silverware there. Such assumptions could now be destroyed.

City top the league but the immediate threat to their prospects does not come on the pitch, but in the footballing courts, their fortunes resting more with lawyers than defenders.

It is different for Liverpool. Iraola has noted their next four league games are against the current top four. They will be a barometer of their chances, and the nature of the opposition makes a striking shortage ill-timed. And yet in the build-up, Isak's thigh problem has become a subplot. There have been bigger issues.

title: 2026 Baycurrent Classic: Adam Scott, Justin Thomas move into contention
description: In search of his first PGA Tour win in six years, Adam Scott shot two eagles on Saturday to move to T-4 at the Baycurrent Classic.
fullText:
YOKOHAMA, Japan — Adam Scott and Justin Thomas moved into contention at the PGA Tour's Baycurrent Classic in Japan on Saturday, one stroke off the lead after three rounds at the Yokohama Country Club.

Scott, looking for his first PGA Tour win in six years, shot a 6-under 65 which included two eagles and Thomas a 67. They were tied for fourth.

First-round leader Jacob Bridgeman (69) was in a tie for the third-round lead with Michael Brennan (65) and PGA Tour rookie Zach Bauchou (67) with 13-under 200 totals.

"You got to be pleased with that and something like that tomorrow might be enough," Scott said of his 65. "It's not a bad spot to be a few back. Hopefully we'll be in for a great day."

The PGA Tour's lone stop in Asia features its strongest field of the FedEx Cup Fall series, with 13 of the 24 players who competed in the Presidents Cup two weeks ago at Medinah in the Chicago suburbs.

Don't miss the Baycurrent Classic from Yokohama Country Club in Yokohama, Japan.

title: 49ers get Mike Evans news but lose two key pieces for Seahawks game
description: The 49ers took a 4-0 record into Friday’s final injury report for Sunday’s NFC West game at Seattle, and they came out of it with Mike Evans cleared and two veterans ruled out. Evans has no designation after practicing on a limited basis on Friday, a week after he was listed as questionable for the […] The post 49ers get Mike Evans news but lose two key pieces for Seahawks game appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The 49ers took a 4-0 record into Friday's final injury report for Sunday's NFC West game at Seattle, and they came out of it with Mike Evans cleared and two veterans ruled out.

Evans has no designation after practicing on a limited basis on Friday, a week after he was listed as questionable for the Denver game. Evans hurt his ribs in the second quarter of the 36-30 win over Arizona on Sept. 27 and was carted to the locker room. He played through it on Oct. 4 and caught five passes for 76 yards in a 24-14 win over the Broncos.

"It's my job, and I take pride in trying to suit up every chance I get," Evans said ahead of the Denver game. "But if there's something I can play through, I'm going to be there for my team as best I can."

Nick Bosa will miss a third straight game with knee and calf injuries, and fullback Kyle Juszczyk is out with a knee injury. Juszczyk hyperextended his right knee and suffered a bone bruise when Broncos defensive back Jahdae Barron hit him low after a catch in the Denver win.

Safety Marques Sigle and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. are also out with ankle injuries. Cornerback Upton Stout is questionable with a shoulder injury.

49ers ruled out FB Kyle Juszcyk and DE Nick Bosa for Sunday’s game at Seattle. WR Mike Evans is off the injury report and has no injury designation. https://t.co/ntvB00IDbA

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 9, 2026

Bosa hurt his calf during warmups before a practice in the week leading up to the Arizona game. Kyle Shanahan said on Sept. 25 that Bosa could miss "around a few weeks," and that estimate has now stretched to three games.

San Francisco is doing pretty well; they won both games he has missed so far, though the defense looked very different in each. Arizona scored 30 points in the Week 3 shootout, and Denver managed 14 in Week 4. Thompson missed both of those games as well and is out again on Sunday, so the defensive line has been without two regulars for the entire stretch.

Seattle sits at 3-1, one game behind the 49ers. A Seahawks win on Sunday would pull them level with San Francisco at the top of the NFC West and give them the head-to-head result. Seattle will be shorthanded too, having ruled out running back Zach Charbonnet with a knee injury.

Mykel Williams, whose 2025 season ended with a torn ACL, is questionable with a knee designation after his second week of practice. Shanahan said the 49ers will activate him from the physically unable to perform list on Saturday, which would put the edge rusher in line for his first game since the injury with Bosa still sidelined.
