title: Time to rise? Ranking European football's sleeping giants
description: From Sampdoria to Saint-Etienne and Real Zaragoza, who are the sleeping giants of European football?
fullText:
Deportivo, Parma, Hamburg. Not just a football hipster's holiday hit-list, but a sample of erstwhile headline acts who have returned to their respective top flights in recent years.

You can throw Leeds United, Nottingham Forest, Schalke and Malaga into the mix too.

But with such footballing royalty back in the big time, where can you find Europe's current sleeping giants? Which once-mighty sides are still snoozing?

We first need to establish some criteria - history, heritage, fanbase, stadium. Clubs with huge potential who currently exist outside the top flight.

Calling a big city home helps, but it is not a deal-maker - sorry to fans of Bristol City and second-tier Russian outfit FC Ufa, where the local population tops one million.

Likewise, some clubs with good-sized stadiums have not made the cut. Bari, whose Stadio San Nicola is the third-largest in Italy and was built for Italia '90, stands out, though some of their calcio colleagues outside Serie A also have grounds of more than 30,000 - Hellas Verona, Messina and Palermo among them.

There's a plethora of ex-Premier League teams with top-flight worthy arenas and storied pasts, while Germany is stacked full of historic clubs with huge homes who arguably deserve a spot - Fortuna Dusseldorf, Wolfsburg, Hannover 96 - but we can't include them all.

A sleeping giant must have experienced some element of former glory and Pro Vercelli are the obvious candidate there, winning seven Italian titles by 1922. But, despite being under new ownership, the third-tier side boast neither the ground nor local population to awaken that historic status any time soon.

The other nuance is, that success cannot have come too recently. West Ham, for example, won a European competition three years ago, Wolves are recent top-flight regulars; likewise Stade de Reims, twice European Cup runners-up, and eight-time French champions Nantes.

Leaving out Steaua Bucharest was another big call. European Cup winners 40 years ago and Romania's most dominant club, they now play in Liga II. But, following a deeply divisive split, many of the traditional fanbase follow top-flight FCSB. So who really owns that legacy?

And there was a case for Boavista, title winners in 2001 but whose existence now hangs by a thread. Facing financial ruin, despite fans' best efforts, they have been ejected from Portugal's professional leagues.

Anyway, let's get on with this. Piped through the matrix above, here are my top 10 European sleeping giants - you can have your say in the comments, too.

League titles: One (2009-10). Domestic cups: One (1985-86). Division: 1.Lig, second tier. Stadium: Centennial Ataturk Stadium (43,361)

Historically dominated by Istanbul's elite teams, Bursaspor snapped that long-running streak by becoming only the second club from outside of the city - and first since Trabzonspor almost three decades earlier - to clinch the Turkish title in 2010.

That meant Champions League nights against Manchester United and Rangers, but in 2024 the Green Crocodiles dropped into the fourth tier for the first time in their history.

Based in a city of about 2.5m people - Bursa sits in the north west, south of Istanbul, near Mount Uludag - and with a unique crocodile-shaped stadium that can house 43,361 fans, Bursaspor have soared up the pyramid since and are looking to return to the Super Lig for the first time since 2019.

League titles: Eight (most recent East German DDR-Oberliga 1989-90). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 89-90). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Rudolf-Harbig-Stadion (32,085).

Without wanting to turn this into a 2.Bundesliga table, this is the first of four German entries. But Dynamo Dresden, bearing a complex history and situated in the underrepresented east, feel a little different.

Initially enjoying the support of the security forces before their best players were relocated to Berlin, Dynamo became European regulars and lost to Liverpool in the Uefa Cup in 1976 and European Cup two seasons later.

One of East Germany's most dominant clubs, they won eight titles and seven cups and joined the Bundesliga in 1991 following reunification, but they dropped into the third tier four years later amid relegation and mounting debts.

Dynamo, with alumni including Matthias Sammer, have bounced around the regional and lower leagues for many years but now sit in 2.Bundesliga.

Based in a city of more than half a million people, their potential is underpinned by a large, passionate fanbase who averaged over 30,000 for home games in the second tier last term.

League titles: Four (most recent 1997-98). Domestic cups: Two (most recent 95-96). Division: 2.Bundesliga. Stadium: Fritz-Walter-Stadion (49,327)

With their 1997-98 success, Kaiserslautern remain the only side to win the Bundesliga immediately after promotion, albeit following a surprise relegation having also been champions in 1991 and enjoyed cup triumphs in 1990 and 1996.

European regulars in the 1990s and early 2000s, it is now almost 15 years since they competed in the Bundesliga, spending four seasons in the third tier before a promotion in 2022.

Despite modest league finishes, the club continue to record average crowds of more than 46,000 and almost pulled off another shock in 2024 when they reached the German Cup final, losing to Xabi Alonso's Leverkusen.

League titles: Four (most recent 1929-30). Domestic cups: Four (most recent 90-91). Division: League One, third tier. Stadium: Hillsborough (39,732)

Sheffield United fans may argue that they, not city rivals Sheffield Wednesday, should make this list. But the Owls edge it on history and heritage - even if the most recent of their four league titles came almost 100 years ago.

Wednesday were League Cup winners in 1991, and in living memory for many gave us magical moments from the likes of David Hirst, Chris Waddle and Paolo di Canio. Yet they now sit in the third tier after entering administration and enduring relegation last season, before a US consortium bought the club in May.

The Owls, boasting England's 12th biggest club stadium, were relegated from the top flight in 2000, but fans are fuelled with fresh optimism that a reawakening is possible.

Leagues: Two (most recent 1931). Domestic cups: Two (most recent 2002). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Olympiastadion (74,475).

I'm convinced Hertha have huge potential, if not the history to match some of their counterparts. Their only titles, for example, precede the Bundesliga era.

But the Old Lady once reached a Uefa Cup semi-final and beat Chelsea in the Champions League in 1999.

This season is their fourth consecutive campaign outside the top tier, but Hertha continue to play at Berlin's Olympiastadion and regularly attract more than 50,000 fans. A new ground on the Olympic Park site, housing up to 52,000, is being considered.

Currently top of 2.Bundesliga, Hertha can tap into a deep talent pool on their doorstep - highly rated youngsters Ibrahim Maza and Kennet Eichhorn have joined Leverkusen, goalkeeper Tjark Ernst went to Feyenoord - and look equipped to return to the Bundesliga in fine shape.

Leagues: Six (most recent 2008-09). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 12-13). Division: Regional 1, sixth tier. Stadium: Stade Atlantique (42,115)

Bordeaux's recent troubles have been well documented. Relegated from Ligue 1 in 2022 before administration meant they tumbled into the fourth tier, this summer they were again demoted to the regional sixth tier because of financial issues.

Having seemingly hit the bottom, the 2009 French champions now at least have something to build on after being bought by US investment fund Park Bench for one euro.

Les Girondins are dripping in history. Once home to former greats Jean Tigana and Zinedine Zidane, as well as current France internationals Aurelien Tchouameni and Jules Kounde, their decade-old home hosted a Euro 2016 quarter-final - albeit Bordeaux are not playing there at present as they try to shape their future.

League titles: Nine (most recent 1967-68). Domestic cups: Four (most recent 06-07). Division: 2.Bundesliga, second tier. Stadium: Max-Morlock-Stadion (50,000).

Perhaps it's not overly imaginative to be opting for the current top two in Germany's second tier but FC Nuremberg meet all the selection criteria laid out above.

They have the history - nine titles, with the latest of four cup triumphs coming in 2007; a 50,000-seater home; large local fanbase in a one-club city - and the heritage.

They're nicknamed 'Der Club' because of their status in early German football.

Oh, and World Cup winner and Germany's all-time top goalscorer Miroslav Klose is their boss.

Domestic cups: Six (most recent 2003-04). European: Cup Winners' Cup (1994-95). Division: Primera Federacion, third tier. Stadium: La Romareda (under reconstruction but projected 43,000).

David Seaman, look away now. Arsenal fans of a certain vintage will remember former Spurs boy Nayim's long, looping winner beating the moustachioed stopper in the final minute of extra time to give Real Zaragoza the Cup Winners' Cup.

There have been two Copa del Rey triumphs, European journeys and star names since - Pablo Aimar, Diego Milito and David Villa among them - but three decades later, Los Manos find themselves in Spain's third tier.

Ander Herrera, aged 37, is back at his boyhood club, who are in the process of developing a new 43,114-capacity stadium for the 2030 World Cup, in an attempt to help the fallen giants return to former glories.

"Real Zaragoza belong to Europe, they belong to compete for trophies, to be fighting with the biggest clubs in Spain and in Europe," said Herrera.

League titles: 10 (most recent 1980–81). Domestic cups: Seven (most recent 2012–13). Continental: European Cup runners-up (1975–76). Division: Ligue 2, second division. Stadium: Stade Geoffroy-Guichard (41,965)

Saint-Etienne were, until Paris St-Germain overtook them in the past decade, the most-decorated club in France with 10 league titles in 25 seasons from 1956-57 to 1980-81.

Les Verts reached the European Cup final in 1976, losing to a vintage Bayern Munich side, while their last silverware came in the now-defunct Coupe de la Ligue 13 years ago with a team spearheaded by Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang.

They are presently spending their fourth season in five in the second tier, but they continue to produce top prospects. Star defenders William Saliba and Wesley Fofana came off the production line, while 18-year-old attacking talent Djylian N'Guessan will join Liverpool in January.

Then there is their 41,965-capacity Stade Geoffroy-Guichard home, nicknamed the 'cauldron', which was a whisker from seeing Ligue 1 football again this term - Les Verts lost to Nice in the promotion/relegation play-off, meaning the wait to rejoin France's elite continues.

League titles: 1990-91. Domestic cups: Four (most recent 93–94). Continental: Cup Winners' Cup (89–90), European Cup runners-up (91-92). Division: Serie B, second tier. Stadium: Stadio Luigi Ferraris (33,205)

Sampdoria were once continental big-hitters, not merely domestic champions during a golden era of Italian football.

Buoyed by Paolo Mantovani's investment, the Genoa outfit won the Coppa Italia four times between 1985 and 1994, clinched the Scudetto in 1991 and reached three European finals, winning the Cup Winners' Cup in 1990 a year after losing to Barcelona in the final.

In 1992, the team of Gianluca Vialli, Roberto Mancini and Gianluca Pagliuca were again beaten by Barcelona in extra time of the European Cup final at Wembley.

More big names followed in the period between Sven-Goran Eriksson's side winning the club's last major trophy in 1994 and a first relegation five years later - Clarence Seedorf, Juan Sebastian Veron and Ariel Ortega included.

Samp had spells back in Europe before finishing bottom of Serie A in 2023 amid serious financial problems and almost dropped into the third tier.

Under new ownership, though, fans hope the club's future is more stable - and the architecturally iconic Stadio Luigi Ferraris home they share with rivals Genoa is set to undergo an expensive redevelopment before Italy host Euro 2032.

title: Four downs from Mason football wrapping up outright CAAC Red title
description: Mason stays unbeaten with 45-14 win over Williamston in CAAC Red finale.
fullText:
WILLIAMSTON — Here is reaction from Mason football wrapping up the outright CAAC Red title with a 45-14 victory over Williamston on Friday, Oct. 9

TROY PETERS, MASON: Another week, another game where the junior made a big all around impact for the Bulldogs. The junior had touchdowns in three different ways while helping Mason claim the outright league title. He had 10 rushes for 180 yards and two touchdowns, threw for 35 yards and a touchdown and also had a receiving score for the Bulldogs. Peters added an interception on defense.

Williamston was driving late in the second quarter while trailing 28-7 and had a chance to tighten the game before receiving the kickoff to open the second half. That scoring chance was ended by Peters interception in the end zone with around 30 seconds left in the second quarter. Mason turned that into points when Luke Goss threw a TD pass to Frankie Trigo with 1.7 seconds left to give the Bulldogs a 35-7.

Mason (7-0, 5-0) wraps up the outright CAAC Red title and ends the regular season unbeaten against Greater Lansing teams. The league championship was the seventh in eight seasons for the Bulldogs, who wrap up the regular season with home games against Hastings and Harper Woods. Williamston (4-3, 3-2) had its two-game winning streak halted and missed an opportunity to claim a share of the CAAC Red title.

"Last year was a down year but (we got) back to what we do. We worked super hard this summer and in the season and we came out with the title so that's great." — Mason senior Luke Goss on the Bulldogs winning the outright league title after having title streak snapped in 2025.

title: Miguel Rojas Takes Step Forward as Dodgers Delay NLCS Roster Decision
description: Questions about infielder Miguel Rojas' status for the NLCS continue as the Los Angeles Dodgers mull roster decisions for the postseason.
fullText:
Questions about infielder Miguel Rojas' status for the NLCS continue as the Los Angeles Dodgers mull roster decisions for the postseason.

On Friday, a full day after the Dodgers' NLDS celebration, manager Dave Roberts said the Dodgers are still waiting to see how Rojas progresses before making a definitive call either way.

"Today was encouraging," Roberts said. "He had imaging, and a lot of it was kind of stuff where he has had prior history. … There's nothing definitive, but I will say today was a step in the right direction."

Roberts added that Rojas took part in some baseball activities, fueling optimism, but with a flight to Milwaukee left for the Dodgers, they'll be patient with the 37-year-old veteran.

"I just think that there's no upside in announcing it yet when we still have a plane flight, there's another workout, there's no deadline right now, we're not up against it," Roberts explained.

"So we have time to ultimately make that decision."

Rojas did not play in Game 4 of the NLDS after leaving Game 3 with a lower back injury he sustained from a defensive player.

He stayed in for a few innings before leaving in the eighth inning, mid-at-bat. It was a 1-1 count after Rojas swung at a foul ball.

Tommy Edman came in to relieve Rojas, who was favoring his back in the dugout before heading to the clubhouse.

The following day, the Dodgers did not make Rojas available. Despite his optimism that he would return soon, he did not play and seemed to favor his lower back.

The Dodgers will carry 13 position players and 13 pitchers, a departure from their 14-position player, 12-pitcher split in the NLDS, Roberts announced.

The cleanest move for the Dodgers would be to just swap Rojas out for a pitcher and keep Hyeseong Kim as a speed and defensive threat.

If Kim is coming off the roster no matter what and they want a more natural replacement, Alex Freeland makes sense.

He can play all over the infield and switch-hit, even if his bat is unspectacular.

title: Louisville 44, FSU 20: Seminoles blow early lead in latest embarrassing loss
description: Florida State’s road woes continued on Friday, with a 44-20 loss marking the 11th-straight away from Tallahassee for the Seminoles. Mike Norvell falls to 41-37 (23-28 in ACC play) in his Florida State tenure. In the inverse of last week’s Virginia beatdown, Florida State started off hot in the first quarter and then faltered the […]
fullText:
Florida State's road woes continued on Friday, with a 44-20 loss marking the 11th-straight away from Tallahassee for the Seminoles. Mike Norvell falls to 41-37 (23-28 in ACC play) in his Florida State tenure.

In the inverse of last week's Virginia beatdown, Florida State started off hot in the first quarter and then faltered the rest of the way, allowing the Cardinals to score 35 straight as the Seminoles sputtered on each side of the ball.

FSU's defense was especially atrocious, giving up three touchdown runs of 40-plus yards (97, 44, 68), allowing the Cardinals to rack up 537 total yards.

The pivotal moment came on a failed fourth-down attempt from Louisville's one-yard line, on which a successful conversion would have put Florida State up 21-0. Instead, a failed wide receiver screen to Jasen Lopez lost two yards and the next play, Louisville ripped off a 97-yard run to recapture some momentum. A quick FSU three-and-out followed, resulting in the first of five straight punts, and the Cardinals took advantage of blood in the water.

After tying things up before halftime, Louisville began the third quarter with a 71-yard kickoff return and took the lead for the first time, never looking back as it turned what looked like an embarrassing home loss into a dominant showing.

Florida State managed to add one more touchdown in the fourth to snap its scoreless run, but failed to convert a two-point attempt. Any hopes of a miracle comeback were quickly snuffed out on the subsequent Louisville series as Isaac Brown reeled off a 68-yard touchdown run.

Next up for Florida State is another road game, this time heading down south to take on the Miami Hurricanes.

title: Jalen Hurts Never Forgot Nick Saban, and His Latest Gesture Shows Why Alabama Will Always Be Home
description: While the Eagles quarterback missed Nick Saban’s documentary premiere, his surprising delivery to the legendary coach’s home showcased the deep-rooted gratitude and character defining his Crimson Tide journey.
fullText:
Some players come through the University of Alabama football program, win championships, break records, and eventually move on to the next chapter of their careers. Their names are remembered, their accomplishments are celebrated, and their highlights become part of Alabama football history. But every once in a while, a player comes along whose impact on a program goes far beyond what happens between the white lines.

For me, Jalen Hurts will always be one of those players.

There have been plenty of incredibly talented quarterbacks to wear the Crimson Tide uniform over the years, but I genuinely believe Hurts has one of the most remarkable stories in Alabama football history.

Not simply because of the games he won or the championships he helped bring to Tuscaloosa, but because of the way he handled adversity, carried himself when things didn't go his way, and continued to demonstrate the kind of character that Nick Saban spent his career trying to develop in his players.

And this week, Hurts reminded Alabama fans once again why his legacy in Tuscaloosa will always be about so much more than football.

On Thursday night, October 8, the Bama Theatre in Tuscaloosa hosted the premiere of ESPN's six-part documentary series, Saban, chronicling the extraordinary career and life of former Alabama head coach Nick Saban. Former players, coaches, family members, and countless individuals who played a role in Saban's remarkable journey gathered to celebrate the man who transformed Alabama football and impacted so many lives along the way.

Although Hurts was not in attendance, he made sure his former head coach and Miss Terry knew just how much they meant to him. Hurts had a beautiful arrangement of white flowers delivered to the Sabans' home in Tuscaloosa, accompanied by a personal handwritten-style message expressing his appreciation for the opportunity to be part of Saban's journey. Miss Terry shared the thoughtful gesture with those in attendance and read Hurts' message aloud.

The note began with words that perfectly captured the relationship between the former quarterback and his coach:

"Coach Saban, thank you for the opportunity to be a part of your story."

Hurts went on to reflect on receiving that recruiting phone call in 2015, the journey that followed, and the impact of Saban's leadership before congratulating him and Miss Terry on the documentary premiere.

I don't know about you, but that is the kind of story that makes me love college football even more. Because think about what those flowers represented.

This wasn't about a championship ring, an NFL contract, a Heisman Trophy campaign, or another football accomplishment. It was about a former player taking the time to acknowledge someone who played an important role in shaping the man he became.

It was about gratitude, respect, loyalty, and a relationship that extended far beyond a football field. And if you have followed Hurts' journey from his freshman season at Alabama to his success in the NFL, you know just how meaningful that gesture truly was.

Hurts arrived in Tuscaloosa in 2016 as a talented young quarterback from Texas with tremendous expectations surrounding him. It didn't take long for him to establish himself as one of the most exciting young players in college football. As a true freshman, Hurts took over the starting quarterback position, helped lead Alabama to an SEC championship and a national championship appearance, and quickly became one of the most recognizable faces in college football.

He wasn't necessarily the most polished passer at that point in his career, but he was a competitor. He possessed tremendous athletic ability, confidence, and a calmness that was remarkable for someone his age.

More importantly, he seemed to understand the responsibility that came with being the starting quarterback at Alabama.

Over his first two seasons, Hurts compiled a 26-2 record as Alabama's starting quarterback. He won games, delivered memorable performances, and helped maintain the championship standard that had become synonymous with Saban's program.

But as impressive as those accomplishments were, I would argue that the most important chapter of Hurts' Alabama career began when he was no longer the starting quarterback.

During the 2017 national championship game against Georgia, Saban made one of the boldest decisions of his coaching career. With Alabama trailing at halftime, he replaced Hurts with freshman quarterback Tua Tagovailoa.

We all know how that story ended.

Tagovailoa delivered one of the most memorable performances in Alabama football history, leading the Crimson Tide to an overtime victory and another national championship. The game-winning touchdown pass to DeVonta Smith on second-and-26 remains one of the most iconic moments in college football history.

But while the rest of the college football world celebrated Tagovailoa's heroics, Hurts was suddenly facing a situation that very few young athletes could ever fully prepare themselves for.

He had helped lead his team to the national championship game, only to watch another quarterback come off the bench and finish the job.

Imagine spending countless hours preparing, practicing, studying film, and doing everything your coaches asked of you, only to have your role change on the biggest stage in college football.

Imagine being a young athlete who had experienced tremendous success, only to suddenly find yourself facing questions about your future, your abilities, and your place on the team.

Hurts had every opportunity to become bitter. He could have complained publicly, created distractions, blamed his coaches, or immediately decided that he wanted nothing more to do with Alabama.

And I will always believe that decision revealed more about his character than any touchdown he ever scored.

Hurts returned for the 2018 season knowing that Tagovailoa had become Alabama's starting quarterback. Rather than allowing disappointment to dictate his attitude, he continued working, supported his teammates, and prepared himself for whatever opportunity might come his way.

That kind of humility and discipline is easy to talk about when everything is going your way. It becomes much harder when you're the one standing on the sideline watching someone else do the job you once held.

But Hurts continued to demonstrate what it meant to put the team above himself.

And then came December 1, 2018.

Alabama was facing Georgia in the SEC Championship Game inside Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta. The Crimson Tide found itself in another difficult battle against the Bulldogs, and when Tagovailoa suffered an injury, Hurts was called upon to lead the offense.

The circumstances almost seemed too remarkable to be real.

Less than a year earlier, Hurts had been replaced by Tagovailoa against Georgia in that same stadium. Now, with another championship hanging in the balance, Alabama needed the quarterback who had spent the season preparing quietly behind the scenes.

Hurts stepped onto the field and delivered one of the most unforgettable redemption performances in Alabama football history, helping lead the Crimson Tide to a 35-28 victory and another SEC championship.

I can still remember the emotion surrounding that moment.

It wasn't simply about Alabama winning another football game. It was about watching a young man who had faced public disappointment, criticism, and uncertainty refuse to allow those circumstances to define him.

He didn't spend the season demanding recognition or insisting that he deserved another opportunity. He worked, remained prepared, and made the most of the moment when it finally arrived.

And that is exactly the kind of mentality Nick Saban spent 17 seasons trying to instill in his players at Alabama.

Following that victory, Saban became visibly emotional while discussing Hurts and what he had accomplished. For a coach who was often known for his demanding personality and relentless pursuit of excellence, it was a rare glimpse into just how deeply he cared about the young men he coached.

What made the moment so special was that Saban understood the challenges Hurts had experienced. He understood the disappointment, the work that happened when cameras weren't rolling, and the commitment it took to remain ready despite not knowing whether another opportunity would ever come.

And years later, it is evident that those experiences helped create a relationship built on genuine mutual respect.

Even at Thursday night's documentary premiere, Saban reflected on the way Hurts handled that difficult situation, praising his character, competitiveness, and commitment to being a good teammate. He emphasized that Hurts' response deserved far more recognition than it received.

In today's college football environment, where transferring has become increasingly common and players have more opportunities than ever to pursue different situations, Hurts' decision to remain at Alabama for that 2018 season stands out.

And I want to be clear about something: I don't believe transferring automatically means a player lacks loyalty or character. Every athlete has unique circumstances, and sometimes a change is the right decision for their future.

Hurts eventually made that decision himself, transferring to Oklahoma for his final college season in 2019.

He went on to have an outstanding season with the Sooners, became a Heisman Trophy finalist, and continued developing into the quarterback who would eventually succeed in the NFL. Oklahoma played an important role in his story, and that deserves to be acknowledged.

But the fact that he finished his college career somewhere else doesn't erase what he accomplished at Alabama or the relationships he built in Tuscaloosa. He can appreciate his time at Oklahoma while still being an Alabama legend. Those two things aren't mutually exclusive.

Alabama helped shape Hurts, and Hurts helped shape Alabama football during one of the most successful stretches in program history. That's something no transfer decision can ever take away.

His professional success has made that story even more remarkable. Hurts developed into the starting quarterback of the Philadelphia Eagles, led the franchise to multiple Super Bowl appearances, and ultimately captured a Super Bowl championship while earning Super Bowl MVP honors.

For someone who once faced questions about whether he could develop into an elite quarterback, his journey has become an extraordinary example of perseverance and continued growth.

Yet what I appreciate most is that the success doesn't appear to have caused him to forget the people who helped him along the way.

He could have simply watched the documentary, sent a congratulatory text, or acknowledged the premiere on social media. Instead, he took the time to send a thoughtful gift and a personal message to the man who gave him an opportunity nearly a decade earlier.

There wasn't a camera crew following him to the florist. There wasn't a press conference announcing the gesture. In fact, had Miss Terry not shared the story, the public might never have known about it.

And to me, that's what makes it so meaningful.

It wasn't a gesture that needed an audience. It was simply a former player expressing gratitude.

One of the things I have always appreciated about Saban's coaching philosophy was his emphasis on developing players beyond football. Yes, he demanded excellence. Yes, he expected discipline, accountability, and an unwavering commitment to the process. But he also consistently talked about preparing young men for life after their playing careers ended.

When we look back at Saban's time at Alabama, it's easy to focus on the national championships, SEC titles, NFL Draft selections, and incredible winning percentage.

Those accomplishments are remarkable, and they deserve to be celebrated. But I believe one of the greatest measures of his legacy is found in the lives of the individuals he influenced.

It's found in the former players who return to Tuscaloosa years after their careers have ended. It's found in the relationships that continue long after the final whistle. And it's found in moments like this one, when a Super Bowl-winning quarterback takes a few minutes out of his life to remind his former coach how much his leadership meant to him.

That's the part of college football that I wish we talked about more.

The lessons that don't always show up on a stat sheet but influence the direction of someone's life.

I think there's also an important lesson in Hurts' journey for anyone who has experienced disappointment or watched something they worked incredibly hard for unfold differently than they imagined.

Sometimes adversity reveals parts of our character that success never could. Sometimes the greatest growth happens during seasons when we feel overlooked, disappointed, or uncertain about what comes next. And sometimes the very circumstances we would have never chosen become part of the story we are most grateful for years later.

That's what makes Hurts' journey so powerful.

His story didn't unfold the way he probably envisioned when he first arrived in Tuscaloosa. There were incredible victories, difficult setbacks, unexpected changes, and moments when his future was uncertain. But looking back now, it's hard to imagine his story being quite as meaningful without those challenges.

The same young man who was benched during a national championship game eventually became the quarterback who helped Alabama win an SEC championship, earned a fresh opportunity at Oklahoma, and went on to reach the pinnacle of professional football.

And through it all, he never forgot where an important part of that journey began.

When Hurts sent those flowers to Nick and Miss Terry Saban, he wasn't simply congratulating a legendary coach on a documentary premiere. He was acknowledging the relationship, lessons, and experiences that helped shape his life.

For Alabama fans, it was another reminder of why Hurts will always hold such a special place in Crimson Tide history.

Not because he never faced adversity, but because of the way he responded when adversity came. Not because his journey was perfect, but because he refused to let difficult moments prevent him from continuing to grow. And certainly not just because of the football games he won, but because of the character he displayed when winning wasn't guaranteed.

Nick Saban's legacy will always include championships, records, and some of the greatest teams college football has ever seen. But his influence on players like Hurts may ultimately be one of the most meaningful parts of his story.

And Hurts' legacy at Alabama will always be about more than the numbers he put up or the trophies he helped win.

It will be about perseverance, humility, loyalty, and what it looks like to handle both success and disappointment with maturity.

So yes, Oklahoma fans can celebrate what Hurts accomplished in Norman. Philadelphia Eagles fans can celebrate everything he has achieved in the NFL. But Alabama fans will always have a special reason to celebrate Jalen Hurts.

Because long before he was a Super Bowl MVP, he was a young quarterback in Tuscaloosa learning how to lead, how to respond to adversity, and how to keep moving forward when life didn't go according to plan. And nearly a decade after that journey began, a beautiful arrangement of flowers and a heartfelt message reminded us all that those lessons were never forgotten.

Jalen Hurts will forever be part of Alabama football history.

But more importantly, he will forever be part of Nick Saban's legacy. And I think that's something worth celebrating.

title: 3 Biggest X-Factors For Giants to Take Down Commanders This Week
description: Here are three of the biggest X-Factors for the New York Giants to win this week against the Commanders.
fullText:
The New York Giants have opened the 2026 NFL season with a record of 3-1 through the first four weeks of the year.

New York did lose starting quarterback Jaxson Dart to a season-ending injury, but the team has been able to stay the course. The Giants' defense has played well, sealing each of the last two wins for this team.

Now, the Giants will be heading out on the road to face their NFC East rivals, the Washington Commanders. Washington is 1-3 on the season, and they will be trying to get back on track against New York.

Here are three of the biggest X-Factors for the Giants to take down their rivals this week:

1. Get Malik Nabers More Involved

Wide receiver Malik Nabers returned from injury this season and as each passing week has gone by, he has slowly looked more comfortable for the Giants. Last week against the Cardinals, Nabers posted six catches for 112 yards and one touchdown, helping New York get the win.

Against the Commanders, getting Nabers more involved will be key for this team, and quarterback Jameis Winston. If Nabers is healthy, he has incredible talent that can flip a game almost in an instant.

2. Win the Jameis Winston Experience

Since he entered into the NFL, Winston has been one of the more inconsistent players in the entire league. Some weeks Winston looks like the former No. 1 overall draft pick that he was, and in others, he looks like he should only be a backup quarterback in the league.

Through the first two games with New York, the Giants have gotten the full Winston experience, seeing the highs and lows. But against the Commanders, if New York can be on the positive side of this, they will have a good chance to win.

3. Put Pressure on Jayden Daniels

Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels will be coming back from injury in this game against the Giants, after missing the last few weeks. Daniels could be a little rusty, so the Giants will need to do whatever they can to make his life as uncomfortable as possible in this contest.

Daniels has never lost to the Giants in his NFL career, going 3-0 to start, but this is a different New York team that will be trying to change that narrative. If the Giants can contain Daniels, keeping him in the pocket, they should have a strong chance to move to 4-1 on the season.

title: Gideon Gash powers Novi Detroit CC rally over Orchard Lake St. Mary's
description: No. 2 Novi Detroit Catholic Central rallied from a 14-point 4th quarter deficit to beat No. 5 Orchard Lake St. Mary's in Week 7 MHSAA football action.
fullText:
No. 2 Novi Detroit Catholic Central coach Justin Cessante and the Shamrocks' sideline erupted onto the field as the Orchard Lake St. Mary's last-ditch Hail Mary fell to the turf.

Catholic Central rallied from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit on the road with timely turnovers and a revived rushing attack for a 27-20 win over the No. 5-ranked Eaglets on Friday, Oct. 9, in Week 7 of the 2026 Michigan high school football season. The defending Division 1 champions made timely plays and answered every gut-check for their 21st straight win, this time taking down the defending Division 2 champions.

"We knew what we had inside of us and what we needed to do," Cessante said. "I don't really care what people think, but we wanted to prove and send a message to the state that we are not going anywhere."

THE SCORES: Michigan high school football results of Week 7 games

Catholic Central rallied while their starting quarterback, senior Duke Banta, cheered from the sideline in a sling. Banta injured his collarbone in a win over Toledo Central Catholic last week, forcing Peyton Sofran to move from receiver to QB.

Sofran, dealing with his own ailments from last week, kept the offense on schedule and popped up after every big hit.

"I am just so proud of Peyton," Banta said, who added he hopes to return in the playoffs. "I am proud of this team and being a part of this community."

But CC's offense took three quarters to heat up. OLSM did well to stuff the run early while the Eaglets built a 20-6 lead by halftime. The Eaglets could have led by more, but missed all three extra point or two-point conversion attempts.

OLSM marched right down the field for an opening-drive touchdown, which CC answered with a 40-yard Ty Goddard field goal, making it 6-3. CC star Gideon Gash jumped a route from his deep position in cover 3 for an interception on the next drive. But CC fumbled a punt snap, leading to a safety. OLSM added another touchdown and CC added a field goal, making it 14-6 at half.

Interceptions from Gash and linebacker J.J. Chevalier – aided on a pressure from edge rusher Josiah Neal – kept the deficit manageable.

"We knew we were going to face adversity and we were going to have to forget the first half and come out hot in the third and fourth quarters," Gash said.

St. Mary's pushed the lead to two touchdowns late in the third quarter on a 20-yard connection between Jabin Gonzales and tight end B.J. Adams. CC responded with a methodical 12-play touchdown drive, ending with a Gash 6-yard touchdown run on a receiver sweep in a wildcat set.

The Shamrocks forced its first three-and-out of the game on the ensuing possession, getting the ball back with 7:05 left. CC only needed five plays this time, with Gash taking another sweep 50 yards for a touchdown. St. Mary's safety D.J Taylor blocked the extra point, maintaining a 20-19 advantage.

"We had to realize that we were missing an important piece," Gash said. " We had to find out what kind of mentality our team had."

On the next drive, CC safety Aiden Kersey jarred the ball loose for a forced fumble, and sophomore linebacker Dylan Miller-Ramsey jumped on to recover it at the St. Mary's 45 in the final four minutes.

The Shamrocks burned up the rest of the clock before a Ryan Jaafar 4-yard touchdown with 10 seconds left put thems in the driver's seat to win the Catholic League Central Division title again.

"The offense depended on the defense and the defense depended on the offense," Miller-Ramsey said. "All of us came together. Teamwork, that's all I can say, and proper preparation. Our coaches know we are built for this moment and we know we are built for this moment."

For St. Mary's (5-2), the missed opportunities from penalties will sting. The Eaglets' first celebration penalty helped CC start with field position on the plus-side of the 50 just before halftime to add a field goal and make it a one-possession game at the break. The next penalty moved them back on an extra point, leading to a failed 2-point conversion attempt from 18 yards out.

"We beat ourselves with penalties," St. Mary's coach Jermaine Gonzales said.

For CC, it was an emphatic reminder they are still the team to beat in Michigan, even if they do not have Banta until midway through what the Shamrocks hope is another playoff run ending with a wooden mitten trophy at Ford Field.

"Peyton is only going to get better," Cessante said. "Our offense is going to get back into a groove. We are going to get Duke back. We are going to be better for this.

"I told them, we are going to water this adversity and we will be a better team for it. Whatever happened, happened for a reason so we can get to our ultimate goal, winning a state championship. But the Catholic League championship, to me, is as hard as anything to win."

fullText:
Jaylen Brown demands Adidas give Anthony Edwards 'some condoms' after commercial diss appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

The prevailing opinion is that Jaylen Brown will have a colossal chip on his shoulder this upcoming season, but he is seeking revenge against more than just the Boston Celtics. The 2024 NBA Finals MVP and new Philadelphia 76ers wing recently caught a jab from Minnesota Timberwolves superstar Anthony Edwards, who poked fun at the hairlines of both Brown and LeBron James during am Adidas commercial in September. He paid for those jokes on Friday.

While streaming live on Twitch with Sixers teammate VJ Edgecombe, Brown went right for the jugular. "{Adidas} needs to get my boy some condoms," the two-time All-NBA Second-Team selection joked, eliciting a big reaction from Edgecombe.

“VJ do you have a hand in this, cause you with adidas…you need to give my boy some condoms.”

Jaylen Brown responded to Anthony Edwards’ commercial for the AE 3s 😅

(via fchwpo/Twitch) pic.twitter.com/Pj31A1WvkE

— ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 10, 2026

Edwards had four babies with four different women, and did so in the span of only a year. He has found himself in multiple child support cases. Brown is hardly the first person to use this controversy to roast the Timberwolves cornerstone, but one has to wonder what the reaction will be when Philly and Minnesota collide in January.

The NBA would obviously prefer if Edwards' off-court activities remain out of the limelight, as he is one of the likeliest candidates to succeed LeBron James as the face of the league. Actions have consequences, though. Despite providing financial assistance, Edwards did not seek custody of all of his children. He married longtime girlfriend Shannon Jackson in July.

Jaylen Brown is clearly not afraid to call out his fellow Georgia native, even if it was in jest. Perhaps Anthony Edwards will think carefully about the script before he films his next Adidas advertisement.

title: FSU football gets run over by Louisville in 44-20 blowout loss
description: FSU football routed by Louisville's run game, blown out 44-20 in loss that extends road losing streak to 11.
fullText:
Once ahead 14-0, Florida State football allowed 35 unanswered points as Louisville extended the Seminoles' nearly three-year-long road losing streak with a 44-20 win on Friday, Oct. 9 at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium.

FSU (3-3, 1-2 ACC) has not won away from Doak Campbell Stadium since the 2023 ACC championship against Louisville, and has lost 13 straight away from home when accounting for neutral-site contests.

Cardinal running back Isaac Brown accounted for 313 total yards, including a 71-yard kickoff return to open the second half and two long rushing scores. In total, Louisville rushed for 397 yards, the most allowed in program history.

Louisville quarterback Lincoln Kienholz went 11-for-15 for 140 yards, while FSU quarterback Ashton Daniels went 21-for-37 for 209 yards and a pair of touchdowns alongside an interception.

Here are three takeaways from the Seminoles' blowout loss to Louisville.

Ahead 14-0 and on the two-yard line with goal to go, Norvell rolled the dice and went for it on fourth down. A screen pass to Jasen Lopez was blown up, and it resulted in a turnover on downs, but left FSU's defense in a favorable position.

That is, until Brown ripped off a 97-yard touchdown run that flipped the momentum of the game.

The ensuing kickoff after the score was taken out of the end zone, rather than being a touchback, and FSU started its drive at the 12-yard line. The Seminoles went three-and-out, with back-to-back runs for a loss of yards. Louisville completed its momentum turn with a 7-play, 59-yard drive that ended with a Marquise Davis six-yard score to tie the game at 14.

After the 4th-down stop, Louisville rattled off 35 unanswered points and scored 44 total to storm back into the game and into the win column. The Seminoles collectively shut down after the turnover on downs, and the Cardinals' comeback mirrored what FSU did to Virginia last week. Despite success on the ground, the Seminoles' passing attack was marred by drops and mental errors.

Daniels started the game with his 10th rushing touchdown of the game, the most by a quarterback in program history, which capped off a 14-play, 75-yard drive that looked easy. It seemed he was set to build off his record-breaking five rushing touchdowns against Virginia, and while he found success on the ground, his struggles throwing the football were apparent.

Hesitation and indecisiveness in the pocket stalled plays, and when he got the chance to get the ball off, accuracy was at a premium. Add in a case of the drops from FSU's wide receivers, and the aerial attack was never able to get going against the Louisville secondary.

Daniels finished the night with one touchdown, a throw behind Micahi Dazny that required an impressive one-handed snag from the receiver. He rushed for 45 yards on 13 carries, but he never looked confident after the fourth-down stop on the play to Lopez.

While he didn't turn the ball over until the game was already out of reach, Daniels struggled to locate the football and only completed 9 of his 19 passes in the second half. Even with success on the ground, 153 yards, including a sixth straight game of 80 or more yards by Ousmane Kromah (88 yards), FSU found itself needing Daniels to make plays to get back in the game.

He was unable to do so as Louisville's secondary was strong in coverage and the Cardinal pass rush got home for four sacks.

And Daniels wasn't aided by the Seminoles' defense.

The Cardinals averaged 163.9 rushing yards entering the game and recorded more than double with 397 yards. All of that was done without star running back Keyjuan Brown.

Despite his absence, I. Brown accounted for 313 total yards and rushed for 325 yards on 17 carries with two touchdowns. His 97-yard score ignited the comeback, and the Cardinals' success on the ground started in the second quarter with 147 yards.

The Cardinals scored six times on the ground, with four players recording a rushing score, including a pair by Kienholz and Brown, who scored on long runs of 97 yards and 68 yards, which was the dagger in the fourth quarter.

After a dominant performance against Virginia, FSU's defense failed to carry over any momentum, which Louisville gratefully accepted with its dominant run game.

title: Turnovers hurt Beaver Falls High School football in loss to Neshannock
description: Early turnovers plagued Beaver Falls High School football as it dropped its first MAC game of the year to Neshannock.
fullText:
BEAVER FALLS — During the team's hot start to MAC Conference play, Beaver Falls High School football limited turnovers in its two wins against Freedom Area and Mohawk.

But against Neshannock in Week 7, four first-half turnovers plagued the Beaver Falls offense in its 27-8 loss on Friday, Oct. 9.

"We are a better team than what we put on the field tonight and that is completely on me," Beaver Falls head coach Jim Mooney said. "The heavy blitzing and stunting from Neshannock caused me problems early on. I've got all the faith in the world in this team; we just need to get back to the drawing board."

Last week in the team's victory over Mohawk, Beaver Falls (4-2, 2-1 MAC) had seemed to figure things out on offense, with junior athlete Xavier Clark rushing for over 100 yards, while Rodney Slappy had his best game of his young career, finishing with three total touchdowns and giving the team its first 100-yard receiver in several years.

However, against Neshannock (6-1, 4-0 MAC), the team's offense could not get into rhythm as Beaver Falls committed four first-half turnovers.

The biggest turnover of the night came on the game's second drive, when Slappy's pass hit off his receiver's hands and right into Neshannock defensive back Justin Edworthy's hands, which he took back for a pick-six.

"It's tough to win a ballgame with those turnovers and it's something as a staff that we have to clean up," Mooney said. "Neshannock was bringing two guys off the one side that caused me a lot of grief after we were practicing slide protection all week.

"I thought we had a good plan going in, but we just have to reset after this one."

Related Reading: Aliquippa native and Pro Football Hall of Famer Mike Ditka dies at 86

Crunching the Numbers: Who are the Times' high school football stat leaders through Week 6?

While the team had its struggles on offense, the Beaver Falls defense kept the team in the game.

Outside of the third quarter, the unit forced a multitude of three-and-outs, turned Neshannock over on downs and also forced a Lancers punt after the team had the ball in the red zone after a Beaver Falls fumble.

Beaver Falls also forced a turnover late in the first quarter, with Clark intercepting Jared Corey's pass to give the Tigers some momentum before it was negated by another turnover.

"That defensive line is great and we held their [Neshannock] run game in check for the most part," Mooney said. "Our back end got hit a couple of times, but that's going to happen. Hats off to Neshannock; they're a well-coached team that has some quick kids that can make plays.

With the loss, Beaver Falls will aim to bounce back as it travels to take on Riverside at 7 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 16.

title: Somerset football tops Bedford, Fochtman earns 1st career coaching win
description: Somerset earned its first win of the season with an LHAC football triumph over Bedford in Week 7.
fullText:
SOMERSET — It took seven grueling weeks to do so, but first-year head football coach Braden Fochtman earned his first career win, Friday, Oct. 9, as Somerset edged Bedford 14-7, on homecoming.

"Having this be my first win feels amazing," said Fochtman. "I told the kids in school at the pep rally that having the whole community out here tonight means the world to me and these kids. I am glad we could bring a positive light to this weekend for this community and for the kids going to homecoming."

Somerset managed only 129 yards of offense. The Golden Eagles were penalized 10 times for 85 yards, but still found a way to win.

Week 7 highlights Pa. high school football, Somerset County Week 7 live score updates

Comprehensive coverage Complete Somerset County high school football coverage for 2026

It was the special teams that made the first big play of the game for Somerset. Sophomore Carson Sredy blocked a Bedford punt that was scooped up by freshman Levi Buterbaugh and returned for a touchdown. Chris Thompson tacked on the extra point for a 7-0 lead with 1:36 to go in the first quarter.

"We've taken special teams extremely serious all offseason and leading into the season," Fochtman said. "It's great to see some guys that don't get to play offense or defense come up huge for us on special teams. That helped win us this game."

The score remained that way until the third quarter.

Somerset capitalized on a high snap over Bedford quarterback Blake Cragan's head that was recovered by senior Chase Elchin at the 1-yard line. Senior quarterback Garret Reese called his own number on the next play for a touchdown. Thompson added the PAT for a 14-0 advantage with 9:01 left in the quarter.

Elchin came away with another fumble recovery in the third as well.

Bedford (2-5) took advantage of a Somerset turnover to crack the end zone. Junior Grey Livengood dashed 17 yards out of the wildcat to pull the Bisons within seven.

Somerset made one more defense stand, and wide receiver Caden Stephens connected with tight end Gavin Berkey for 18 yards on a fourth-and-7 to seal the victory.

The defense and special teams shined for Somerset. The Golden Eagles blocked a field goal on the Bisons opening drive and made a fourth-and-1 stand at their own 10-yard line in the second quarter.

"Coach (Jake) Heiple and (Jared) McCormick do a great job preparing these guys each week," Fochtman said. "I am so thankful to have them on my staff. They have the ability to adjust when things aren't going our way to neutralize some of the better players that we've competed against.

"Hats off to our players. These guys have given the same great effort through six weeks of practice. I am so thankful to get them a win and feel what it feels like when hard work pays off."

title: Steelers WR Gives Blunt ‘Throw You Into the Fire’ Take on Aaron Rodgers’ Ruthless Offensive Approach
description: Michael Pittman Jr. is still settling into life with the Steelers. Pittsburgh Steelers fell 27-24 at Cleveland on October 1, a Thursday night loss that left the team at 2-2. Now, with his former team coming to town, the veteran receiver has opened up about the toughest part of playing with Aaron Rodgers. fullText:
Michael Pittman Jr. is still settling into life with the Steelers. Pittsburgh Steelers fell 27-24 at Cleveland on October 1, a Thursday night loss that left the team at 2-2. Now, with his former team coming to town, the veteran receiver has opened up about the toughest part of playing with Aaron Rodgers. His answer shows how steep the learning curve has been.

Pittman joined the Steelers in March through a trade with the Indianapolis Colts. Pittsburgh sent a sixth-round pick and received Pittman and a seventh-rounder. The team then signed him to a three-year, $59 million extension.

Learning Rodgers' pre-snap system has been the hard part. According to Yahoo Sports reporter Jori Epstein, Pittman said there were no formal meetings to explain the signals when he arrived. Rodgers simply flashes a signal and snaps the ball, which leaves little room for second guesses.

"Aaron's style is kind of like, throw you into the fire," Pittman told Epstein. "It's sort of funny because it's almost like you learn it better once you mess it up the first time. Because you don't want to mess it up again."

Pittman believes the process works because mistakes stay with players.

Michael Pittman Jr. on chaos of Aaron Rodgers’ hand signals?

“Aaron’s style is kind of like, throw you into the fire…” he told me. “It’s sort of funny because it’s almost like you learn it better once you mess it up the first time. Because you don’t want to mess it up again.” https://t.co/i0T95r27NN

— Jori Epstein (@JoriEpstein) October 8, 2026

The signals are not his only hurdle. Michael Pittman Jr. has battled plantar fasciitis, missed the Week 2 loss to the Patriots and caught four passes for 31 yards over the last two games. He was also seen on a scooter with his foot elevated at practice this week.

Rodgers' signal system has drawn attention far beyond Pittsburgh, and the numbers behind it are striking.

Backup quarterback Will Howard gave a rare look at the system. Rodgers asked him to build a Google Doc of signals on the first day of 2025 training camp. The list began with about 25 to 30 signals and grew to roughly 75 by season's end.

Epstein also gathered estimates from other teams. The Broncos reportedly use 15 to 25 signals, and the Ravens use 20 to 30. The Eagles and Seahawks sit around 50 to 60, still well below Rodgers' total.

Receivers feel the weight of that list. DK Metcalf described it as a lot of signals, and tight end Pat Freiermuth said in training camp that he is still learning what Rodgers expects.

Rodgers' demanding style has also shown on the sideline, including a heated exchange with head coach Mike McCarthy. If players who spent a full season with Rodgers are still catching up, it is easy to see why Pittman, a newcomer slowed by injury, needs extra time.

Pittsburgh hosts the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at Acrisure Stadium. Pittman faces his former team while still learning Rodgers' system and managing a sore foot, so his comfort with the signals could shape how well the offense moves.

title: Former players reminisce playing under Mike Ditka
description: While fans saw the public persona of legendary coach Mike Ditka, it's his players who knew him better.
fullText:
CHICAGO (WGN) - While fans saw the public persona of legendary coach Mike Ditka, it's his players who knew him better.

In the annals of Chicago sports history, Mike Ditka will always be upper tier.

The scrappy kid from Aliquippa, Pennsylvania was tough on the field for his beloved Bears, and maybe even tougher on the sidelines as the coach.

Former player and fellow Pro Football Hall of Famer Dan Hampton recalled that all Ditka asked of his players was to be smart and to play hard all the time.

Legendary former Chicago Bears Head Coach Mike Ditka dies at 86

"You brought your A-game, he had no complaints and he didn't bother you. Itwas just some of the players that didn't want to toe the line and do what was necessary, then he had some run-ins with them. At the end of the day, it was all for a common good, for the good of the organization, for the Chicago Bears, and that's why he is legendary and that's why all of us loved him," Hampton said.

Ditka had a contentious relationship with then-Bears Chairman Mike McCaskey. After he and the team parted ways, he became head coach of the New Orleans Saints, but never achieved the same success.

He also had a stint as a network football analyst all while running his two Chicagoland restaurants of the same name, one downtown and one in Oak Brook. He was often found at his restaurants entertaining and engaging with guests.

Former Bear Dan Jiggetts played under Ditka in his first year as Bears head coach in 1982. He then covered him as a Chicago TV sports anchor and reporter.

Mike Ditka: A legendary coach and pop culture icon

"If it was on his mind, you were going to hear it, believe me, and the thing about Mike was that you're not always going to agree with him or like what he has to say, but you were going to hear it one way or the other, and I think that that was well-established when he came in for that first meeting, and it just grew from there," Jiggetts said.

Ditka died Friday at the age of 86.

Mike Ditka was an NFL icon and his death Friday has resulted in tributes from a plethora of his former players, assistant coaches and associates. The former Chicago Bears coach was well-known for his outbursts while coaching and his demonstrative style.

Former Bears QB Jim Harbaugh on his former HC Jim Harbaugh (📹 @chargers): pic.twitter.com/KcXoIGIlHO

— Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 10, 2026

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

One of his most famous incidents came when the was coaching the Bears in the 1992 season. The Bears had built a 20-0 lead in a road game against the Minnesota Vikings at the Metrodome. The game had reached the third quarter and Ditka wanted quarterback Jim Harbaugh to play it safe with a conservative game plan. That meant running the ball or being safe with his passes.

Shortly after sending that message to Harbaugh, the quarterback threw an out pattern that was picked off by Minnesota's Todd Scott and the defensive back brought it 35 yards for a touchdown. Ditka lit into Harbaugh with a memorable tirade that TV cameras captured.

Despite the embarrassing scene, Harbaugh and Ditka were quite close and the Chargers head coach was clearly influenced by Ditka. He reminisced about the coach following the announcement of his passing.

"I was sitting in his office and we were about to go over the gameplan," Harbaugh said. "Mike was sitting at his desk and he was writing out check after check. This went on and I asked him what he was doing. He explained that he had gotten letters from people who were struggling and needed money. I asked him if he knew the people, and he said that he didn't. He just wanted to help since they asked him."

title: Former Mercury forward DeWanna Bonner helps Atlanta Dream reach WNBA Finals

fullText:
NEW YORK — DeWanna Bonner is heading back to the WNBA Finals, just one year after helping the Phoenix Mercury reach the championship series.

title: Multiple playoff teams have never started 0-5
description: One of the five 0-4 teams entering Week 5 (the Buccaneers) has finally gotten its first win of 2026.
fullText:
One of the five 0-4 teams entering Week 5 (the Buccaneers) has finally gotten its first win of 2026. Four winless teams remain.

Two of them — the Chargers and Texans — made the playoffs last year.

Via NBC Sports research, the last time two playoff teams started the next year 0-4 happened in 1999. That year, both Super Bowl teams from the prior season (the Broncos and Falcons) got off to an 0-4 start.

Also, no pair of playoff teams has started 0-5 in the next season. Ever.

No playoff team has started 0-5 the next year since the 2017 Giants.

The most teams ever to start the year 0-4 is five. The 2026 quintet matches five 0-4 teams in 2009, 1996, 1991, 1979, and 1962.

With the 0-4 Texans playing the 0-4 Titans, the most possible 0-5 teams this year will be three: the Chargers, the Dolphins, and the loser of Texans-Titans.

title: Kevin Durant believed Russell Westbrook had '5 or 6 more years left' in NBA
description: Kevin Durant believed Russell Westbrook had '5 or 6 more years left' in NBA.
fullText:
Even with the offseason over, we're still feeling the ripple effects of Russell Westbrook's NBA retirement. When you're a basketball pantheon, the game feels your absence for a long time. He played an epic 18 seasons and is a sure-fire Hall-of-Famer at the end of the decade.

Westbrook played his first 11 seasons on the Oklahoma City Thunder. He enjoyed his best years there. Both at the individual and team level. The former MVP winner shattered every triple-double record. Along the way, he was a perennial All-Star and All-NBA member. Oh, and he had a few scoring and assist titles under his belt.

It wasn't just all video-game-esque stats, either. Alongside Kevin Durant, Westbrook co-starred in OKC's first title contender. They had several deep playoff runs in their time together. Even though they failed to bring home a Larry O'Brien trophy, that type of high-bar success is a rich-filled era fans will immortalize.

Even if things ended badly with Durant's departure to the arch-rival Golden State Warriors, I think time will look fondly on that NBA superstar duo. They spent eight years together as a constant title threat. You don't just forget about all of the highs and lows that come with that type of run together. They're forever tied to the hip because of their history and well-documented imperfect pairing and relationship.

Westbrook had about as pitch-perfect a career as you could dream of. Sure, he never won a ring, but he was an era-defining NBA superstar. When we look back at the 2010s, he's one of the five names that will pop into mind. That said, Durant felt like the 37-year-old had a little bit left in the tank to give to the game.

"I was a little sad. I thought Russ still had five or six more years left," Durant said. "He's an athletic body that can still impact the game positively. But sometimes, people are at the point where they want to step away and do something different. Congrats to him on an iconic career."

The timing of Durant's comments is interesting. Just this past Monday, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander voiced something similar. Westbrook did put up decent numbers on the Sacramento Kings last season as a 15-point scorer, but I think the NBA had slowly drifted away from his chaotic style of play. Especially since his Superman athleticism had taken a downturn over the past half-decade.

But hey, Westbrook rode off on the sunset. He had little to prove. At least he was able to leave on his own terms — for the most part. That type of storybook ending to a legendary NBA career seldom happens. Now, we await his eventual Hall of Fame induction and the Thunder's inevitable No. 0 jersey retirement.

Kevin Durant on Russell Westbrook: “I was a little sad. I thought Russ still had 5 or 6 more years left. He’s an athletic body that can still impact the game positively. Congrats to him on an iconic career.” pic.twitter.com/qM2kFpgoFt

title: Holland football celebrates final senior class at Hope's Ray & Sue Smith Stadium
description: An electric kickoff return and the seniors slow walk were the final moments for the Holland at Hope College.
fullText:
HOLLAND - Senior night is a memorable game for high school football teams.

This one had a little extra meaning for the Holland High School Dutch. Friday, Oct. 9, was the final senior night at Hope College's Ray & Sue Smith Stadium after 47 years.

It didn't end the way the Dutch hoped, losing 51-21 to Comstock Park, but the moment was still memorable for the seniors especially, who took their traditional walk across the field together after the game.

While the entire community is looking forward to this historic stadium, the Holland seniors concluded the 47-year history of home games on this site.

"I don't think it is something I will forget," Holland senior Simon Garza said. "The cumulation of the past four years and the work I have put in on this team. I love everyone on this team."

More: High school football Week 7 live scoreboard and roundup for Holland area

For Garza, it has been a four-year journey on this field as a player and as a baritone player in the marching band.

"I have been playing here since I was a freshman. They pulled me up (to varsity) before the first game and I was so excited," he said. "I have always loved this field."

The former Holland Municipal Stadium was sold to Hope College in 2013 and Holland High school has its first-ever on-campus stadium currently under construction.

Holland has continued to play on the same field for nearly a half century.

"You always want to go out on a good note. It doesn't always hit (the seniors) at the end of the game, so that walk is something they will remember doing together," Holland coach Will Siffin said. "It is a special moment for them to kind of complete their journey as a class. They went out proud and are still fighting. I am so proud of them."

Despite the loss, Finn Galloway put the exclamation point on Holland's tenure at the stadium with a 98-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in the final minutes, breaking the school record for longest return set by Corey Willis (95 yards), who was in the house as the honorary captain.

"It was special for sure. It definitely boosted the morale. It was the last game for a lot of guys and it was something bright that we could send them off on. I am really glad we could send them off that way," Galloway said. "It is surreal (to break the record). I mean, he's a legend around here - a guy I have looked up to for a long time and want to follow in his footsteps. It really means a lot."

It meant a lot to all of the Dutch.

"That brought a little light to things. It shows we still have athletes who are playmakers," Siffin said. "We need to make more of those situations happen."

The former Holland Municipal Stadium has seen decades of memories for the Dutch.

Some were good, some were tough.

Holland endured a few winless seasons along the way, but also some memorable triumphs and playoff qualifiers.

But the good memories of great players are what will last.

Great passers, including Jeff Fox, Zach Hop, Amari Powell and Eli Wolters threw plenty of long touchdowns on site, including Wolters' school-record 99-yard touchdown pass as a freshman.

Great catches were made by Andon Grigg, Tailen Luna, Tanner Kingery, Jake Helm and now Finn Galloway.

Great runners, including Corey Willis, Donovan Webb, Elroy Payne, Jacob Torres and Nelson Figueroa once ran wild, with Willis leading the Dutch to their greatest win in school history, a stunning upset of defending state champion East Grand Rapids in 2011.

Linebacker Nathan Ricketts once roamed the middle of the field, the first Holland player to be named a Parade All-American. He and Scott Tackett anchored a defense that helped the Dutch their best season in school history in 2011.

Willis was an all-state quarterback on that team and was back Friday for the final game.

"I had some of my best memories and biggest heartbreaks on this field. The best memory was coming onto the field and looking into the stands and seeing something I had never seen before with how packed the stadium was," Willis said. "The support we had made that the best year. It shows you that this Holland community is built on loyalty and putting one foot in front of the other."

The final chapter at Ray & Sue Smith Stadium started on a positive note, but didn't stay that way.

Finn Galloway scored on a direct snap run of 15 yards. Julius Hall scores on 7 yard run but Holland trailed 20-14 at halftime.

The Holland offense sputtered from there without Wolters at quarterback, who broke his wrist two weeks ago.

But it ended with a 98-yard kickoff return for a touchdown by Galloway.

It was also the final game in the stadium for the cheerleaders and marching band as those groups will be building new traditions next year, too, in a brand new era.

title: Oklahoma CB Eli Bowen added to Friday availability report
description: Friday featured plenty of movement for the Sooners.
fullText:
The Friday availability report remained unchanged for the No. 1 Texas Longhorns heading into Saturday's Red River Rivalry against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas, but there was plenty of movement for Brent Venables and his team.

The headline news for the Sooners is junior cornerback Eli Bowen joining the injury list as questionable with a report emerging from Oklahoma that the 5'9, 189-pounder won't be available against the Longhorns. A starter for the Sooners, Bowen gave up a 41-yard completion against the Bulldogs two weeks ago, but has allowed receptions on just 38.1 percent of the 21 passes targeted against him in coverage with two pass break ups and two penalties committed.

In another significant development for OU, starting left tackle Michael Fasusi was downgraded to out with the shoulder injury sustained in the season opener. Fellow offensive lineman Eddy Pierre-Louis was also downgraded, from questionable to doubtful in a blow for the Sooners.

Four players were upgraded from probable to available while tight end Jack Van Dorselaer remains probable.

title: Familiar Feeling to Latest Red Wings Collapse
description: Even though they came into the night with a losing 1-2 record, there wasn’t necessarily a sense of doom and […]
fullText:
Even though they came into the night with a losing 1-2 record, there wasn't necessarily a sense of doom and gloom surrounding the Detroit Red Wings.

Considering all the offseason shenanigans involving this club, that was really saying something positive about them.

For the most part, they'd played decent hockey. Five-on-five, a bugaboo for the Wings last season, wasn't bugging them at all.

And then, just like that, the Seattle Kraken cracked the whip. They lowered the boom.

good to go, freddy gaudreau 🤝 pic.twitter.com/56APcIUhb1

— Seattle Kraken (@SeattleKraken) October 10, 2026

It only took a span of three minutes and five seconds to have everyone saying, or at least thinking, here we go again.

"I feel like we've played well up until that point and one bad period cost us the game," Red Wings forward Alex DeBrincat said.

We've all seen this film before. The Red Wings give up a goal. That gets the snowball rolling downhill. Momentum takes over.

Suddenly, mistakes multiply like rabbits. Detroit's defensive zone coverage resembles archival footage of the Keystone Cops.

One goal against becomes two, and then three. Hopes of victory are dashed in the span of a few moments. Defeat becomes their frequent companion.

The question we again find ourselves asking, just four games into a new season, is what can this team do to head off such a malady before it grows from a flesh wound into a fatal infection?

"I guess the coach could call a timeout earlier, first of all," Detroit coach Todd McLellan said. "But you're only given 84 timeouts during the year.

"You want the players to grab it and settle things down. There's lots of game left. We went from being in control to being out of control."

Detroit played a solid first period. The Wings outshot the Kraken 18-5, but came out of the frame deadlocked at 1-1.

"I really liked our start," McLellan said. "We probably didn't get rewarded for the effort, and I thought it cost us in the second."

Only 39 seconds after William Wallinder made it 2-1 for the Red Wings, the Kraken scored. It was the first of those three goals in a span of 3:05 that turned the tide and left Detroit reeling.

"We got loose and impatient, and we didn't stick with it, and all of a sudden the puck's in our net," McLellan said. "Now we're chasing the game."

WHAT A PERIOD 🤯 pic.twitter.com/93Zv4Fk54W

— Seattle Kraken (@SeattleKraken) October 10, 2026

"Yeah, it's disappointing," McLellan said. "We put a lot of time and work into doing things right, and we give it back.

"We've got to go back to the drawing board."

There's a double-edged sword feel to the start of this Red Wings season. Until Friday, for the most part, they've played decent hockey. And yet, in the standings, they are 1-3.

"Put it this way," McLellan said. "We scored three tonight. That's enough to win.

It certainly is an interesting – and perhaps even frightening – notion to ponder.

Should it be considered a sign that better days are ahead for this team? Or is it merely an indication that we're discovering who the Red Wings really are, and this is going to be as good as it gets?

title: Isaac Brown brings Louisville back from the brink as Cardinals pummel Florida State 44-20
description: (AP) — Isaac Brown ran for a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on just 17 carries, including a game-changing 97-yard score, as Louisville rallied to take down Florida State 44-20 on Friday night.Known for his big-play capabilities, Brown's long touchdown run came on the first play of a second-quarter drive after Louisville DB Kaleb Beasley stopped Florida State WR Jasen Lopez at the Cardinals 3 on a fourth-and-goal.
fullText:
LOUISVILLE, Ky. (AP) — Isaac Brown ran for a career-high 235 yards and two touchdowns on just 17 carries, including a game-changing 97-yard score, as Louisville rallied to take down Florida State 44-20 on Friday night.

Known for his big-play capabilities, Brown's long touchdown run came on the first play of a second-quarter drive after Louisville DB Kaleb Beasley stopped Florida State WR Jasen Lopez at the Cardinals 3 on a fourth-and-goal. The Seminoles had led 14-0 and appeared to be in total control of the game.

Louisville (3-3, 2-2 Atlantic Coast Conference) never looked back, outgaining the Seminoles 438-190 after the fourth-down stop. The Cardinals finished with 537 yards. That included 397 overall on the ground, where they accounted for all of their touchdowns. It also happened despite Keyjuan Brown, the Cardinals' top rusher this season, being sidelined with an injury.

Brown started the second half taking the opening kickoff 71 yards to the Seminoles 28 and got a horse-collar penalty added at the end. Four plays later, quarterback Lincoln Kienholz scored on a 3-yard run, his first of two scores, to give the Cardinals a 21-14 lead.

Brown finished his night with a 68-yard touchdown run midway through the fourth quarter.

Ashton Daniels completed 21 of 37 passes for 209 yards and two touchdowns as Florida State (3-3, 1-2) amassed 362 yards on offense. He also ran for a score.

Florida State: There has been a lot of head scratching about the Seminoles' football program in recent years. Another questionable decision came when they chose not to kick a short field goal early in the second quarter to potentially take a 17-0 lead over Louisville. But the Cardinals made it a moot point by scoring the next 35 points.

Louisville: There will be a lot of talk about Brown, but give the Cardinals defense credit. They started out slow, but after Brown's big run, they shut down the Seminoles in a game Louisville really needed to win.

Florida State plays at No. 4 Miami on Oct. 17.

Louisville plays at Syracuse on Oct. 17.
